=== PART B: ANSWER TO THE PI QUESTION — three sub-questions, three different answers ===

(1) INTEGRIN / cell-ECM. NO MAGNET. And the reason is not fidelity dogma — it is that the magnet is MORE work.
The trade-off the PI framed (fidelity vs build cost) does not exist here. The fine-grained parts are written and unit-tested: the two-sided adjoint clutch spring (`ff/fa_ecm.py:27`), the catch-slip KMC (`ff/fa_clutch_warp.py:59`), talin/vinculin/Hill maturation (`ff/fa_maturation.py`), the compliant-substrate series (`ff/substrate.py`), AND the engine-side adjoint joint kernel with commit-on-accept (`ac/engine/load_path.py:499,552`) plus the socket that demands it (`ecm_world.py:822`). Both endpoints already live in one CellTransaction (`composed_native.py`). Writing a lumped stand-in means writing NEW code, that satisfies no existing socket, that must then be deleted, and that reintroduces exactly the artifact class this project has been contradicted by six times. The remaining work is WIRING plus ~4 genuinely new small pieces (connector class, state machine, FA population, observables) — days, and every one of them is needed for the real thing anyway.
What the PI actually wants ("things just stick, compartments assembled on top") IS available without a magnet, in two legitimate forms: (a) put the rigid BC where rigidity is physically true — the DISH, via `ecm_far_field_anchor`, which already exists with a reaction ledger; (b) run the clutch with KINETICS FROZEN (bonds permanently engaged) while the MECHANICS stay two-sided and adjoint. (b) is a "magnet with a real load path": it double-counts nothing, it deforms the ECM, its traction distribution is set by real springs, and it is one flag from the kinetic version. That is the scaffold to take — not a stand-in force law.

(2) CADHERIN / cell-cell. OUT OF SCOPE, on SCOPE grounds — not a fidelity concession.
The baseline is ONE cell. Zero cell-cell interfaces exist, so there is nothing to abstract and nothing to scaffold; a magnet here would not be a simplification, it would be a fabricated interface. There is no cadherin connector among the 32 and no cadherin code in `ac/engine/`. When a ≥2-cell configuration is authored, the 2026-06-21 PI ratification stands unchanged and unnegotiated: full catch-bond (KU-4.2), de-cohesion EMERGENT, binary latch forbidden. Record the deferral explicitly as DEFERRED-BY-SCOPE with that ratification cited, so nobody later reads the absence as license for a latch.

(3) FAK / adhesion SIGNALLING. NOT MECHANICS. Out of this track entirely.
Sharp criterion: a mechanical load path is a force that appears in the momentum balance with an equal-and-opposite reaction on a named partner component. FAK phosphorylation, YAP/TAZ translocation, kinase cascades carry no momentum, appear in no force balance, and have no adjoint. They modulate PARAMETERS (myosin activity, polymerization rate, integrin expression, FA turnover rates). Under the connectedness gate they contribute nothing and cost a large set of unconstrained PI-GAP rate constants.
One boundary case must not be mis-sorted: talin unfolding → vinculin recruitment → k_int_eff, and Hill FA-area growth (`ff/fa_maturation.py`) LOOK like signalling but are mechanics — they change a stiffness and a load-bearing area, i.e. they enter the force balance. Keep them (Stage 2 below).
Signalling's real home is PI priority #5: it is the CELL-STATE axis. Since parameters are the eventual OUTPUT of sweeps, a signalling model is a candidate GENERATOR of the state→parameter map, fitted after the mechanics can sweep. Cheap thing to do now so it is not a retrofit: read adhesion parameters through a per-cell-state record indirection, so a future signalling layer writes into that record instead of injecting forces.

=== PART C: HONEST COST OF THE MAGNET, AND JUDGMENT ON THE EXISTING SF PIN ===

A magnet/rigid adhesion is a FIXED BOUNDARY CONDITION, and a BC is not neutral:
- It is a force SOURCE of unbounded magnitude. A pin supplies whatever force is needed to hold the node. Any "traction" read from it is a property of the constraint, not of a bond, and it will scale with whatever the cell pulls with — so it can never be falsified by being too large.
- No traction DISTRIBUTION. Clutch kinetics set the spatial distribution and the per-bond load statistics; a pin gives one resultant per pinned node with no bound fraction, no lifetime, no biphasic stiffness response. The entire class of published data the PI wants to sweep against (traction maps, stiffness sensing, spreading kinetics) is unreachable.
- It CANNOT let go. Crawl requires rear release. A magnet that cannot release cannot crawl — so the PI's own worked example (adherent cell on 2D collagen, migrating) is structurally unreachable with magnets, no matter how much else is assembled on top.
- The documented double-count trap: explicit integrin clutches AND a fixed FA BC in the same run. The pin absorbs the load the clutch should carry, the clutch reports a small load, and the traction is split between a constraint and a bond with no way to attribute it. `load_path.py:274` prevents the two SEMANTIC EDGES from double-counting; NOTHING today prevents pin+clutch, clutch+`membrane_ecm_contact` penalty at the same basal node, or clutch+Winkler spring on top of a live ECM.

JUDGMENT on `ac/engine/sf_motor_slice.py` + `scripts/ac_gate_b_sf_motor_native.py`: not yet in the double-count trap, but already in two others and one wiring step from the trap.
- NOT double-counting today: there are no integrin clutches in that run. The pin (`ac_gate_b_sf_motor_native.py:381-388`, `_pin_force_kernel:135`) is the ONLY adhesion representation, so nothing is counted twice. As a single-component isolation gate for "SF tension emerges from myosin events", the pin is a defensible scaffold.
- IS a metric-measuring-the-wrong-thing: `_fa_traction` (`:171`) reads the force left on a Dirichlet node — the final pass deliberately omits the pin mask to expose it (`:466`) — and names it traction. That is the constraint reaction. For a contracting closed dipole it is guaranteed non-zero and guaranteed inward, so the verdict key `fa_traction_is_inward` (`:584`) can only fail on a motor sign error. It is a legitimate SIGN check and an illegitimate traction. Rename to `pin_reaction_radial` and label PIN_REACTION_NOT_TRACTION.
- Magnitude is BLOCKED independently: the script's own contract requires residual/tension < 1% (`:49-53`) and the measured explicit relax does not converge there (~15.5%). Any number quoted from it is a transient.
- Critical-path consequence, not cleanup: because the FA end is pinned, the ECM cannot move — so this gate can NEVER show PI priority #1 ("compartments deform each other"). Replacing the pin with the real clutch into the live ECM owner IS the milestone, and both owners are already in the same transaction.

=== PART D: STAGED RECOMMENDATION + REQUIRED ARTIFACT LABELS ===

STAGE 0 (now — acceptable scaffold): FA Dirichlet pin allowed ONLY inside single-component isolation gates whose claim is strictly "this component's internal tension emerges". Rename the observable off the word traction. Label every artifact: `ADHESION=DIRICHLET_PIN_SCAFFOLD (pin at the FA, not the dish); TRACTION NOT MEASURED — value reported is a constraint reaction; ALL MAGNITUDES BLOCKED`.
STAGE 1 (before ANY two-component "they deform each other" claim; before `focal_adhesion` or `ecm` may claim CONNECTED): the composite FA joint must be force-real and two-sided against the live ECM owner; the Dirichlet moves from the FA node to `ecm_far_field_anchor` (the dish); a device assertion forbids any node being both pinned and a clutch endpoint. Kinetics MAY be frozen. Label: `ADHESION=CLUTCH_MECHANICS_REAL / KINETICS_FROZEN; de-adhesion NOT REPRESENTED; rear release, bond lifetime, stiffness sensing OUT OF SCOPE OF THIS ARTIFACT; MAGNITUDES BLOCKED`.
STAGE 2 (before any adhesion-dynamics, stiffness-sensing, spreading-area, or migration claim; before `focal_adhesion` → NATIVE): catch-slip kinetics + talin/vinculin/Hill maturation ON at native FA count. Label: `MAGNITUDES BLOCKED — α2β1–collagen card provisional (only α5β1–fibronectin is sourced: hand_kmc.py:150); F*≈7 pN vs KB ~30 pN UNRECONCILED (fa_clutch_warp.py:13-16); ligand density ρ_L and patch radius a ABSENT (substrate.py:33)`.
STAGE 3 (speed, PI priority #4): only after Stage 2 shape gates hold; then A/B the two default-off wins natively (cg_check_every early-exit, assembled per-fiber coarse) with the clutch in the loop — the clutch changes the stiffness spectrum, so an A/B without it does not transfer.
NEVER: a magnet at the cell-ECM interface in any run that reports a traction, a spreading area, a stiffness response, or a migration speed.

risks: LOAD PATH THAT SUMS TO ZERO — the dominant risk here. An unpolarised adherent cell has sum(f) = 0 exactly by symmetry, so the balance gate passes on a correct cell AND on a dead one. Mitigation: never report the balance residual without sum|f|, and treat trace(M_sym) < 0 plus the polarity-response of the deviatoric part as the load-bearing evidence. The prior crawl failure (isotropic radial grip cancelling laterally, F_net down to one clutch) is exactly this shape.

METRIC MEASURING THE WRONG THING — already live: ac_gate_b_sf_motor_native.py:171/:466 reads a Dirichlet constraint reaction and calls it traction, and :584 turns it into a verdict that can only fail on a motor sign error. Any adhesion artifact inheriting that naming inherits an unfalsifiable claim. Rename before reuse.

RAW |F| CONTAMINATION — per-clutch load taken from the node force array will include backbone/Lagrange and crosslink tension (a documented past failure). Load must come from the joint's own load_d (load_path.py:548).

DOUBLE-COUNTING, four distinct ways: pin + clutch on the same node; clutch + membrane_ecm_contact penalty at the same basal node; clutch + substrate Winkler spring stacked on a live ECM; and the two FA semantic edges resolving to two springs. Only the last is currently guarded (load_path.py:274). The others need the structural assertion.

PROTOCOL FLAG-CHECK MISTAKEN FOR EVIDENCE — ecm_world.py:832-841 validates DECLARED flags (equal_opposite_required, adjoint_transfer_required). A class can satisfy every flag and still scatter one-sided. The flags are not evidence; only the numeric balance gate with its denominator is.

STIFF-SERIES NON-CONVERGENCE — clutch k in series into alpha-actinin 4.6e5 pN/um; the SF slice already fails its own 1% residual criterion at 15.5%. Without the implicit solver, every traction number is a relaxation transient wearing a converged label.

COARSE-CONFIGURATION INFERENCE — six prior conclusions were contradicted natively. Clutch density is an AREAL density: a coarse basal patch changes per-clutch load and the whole turnover statistic. No adhesion conclusion may be stated from a reduced FA count.

BODY-FORCE CONFOUND RECURRENCE — ff/motility_warp.py:331 gravity_kernel and :371/:397 spreading push/reaction are the same family as the 19,000-47,000x SettlingForce that did the flattening credited to the lamellipodium and was locked in by regression gates. An adherent-baseline run using them would attribute clutch-driven flattening to a body force. A0 exists to catch precisely this.

GPU-ONLY VIOLATION VIA BOND SEARCH — ff/fa_ecm.py:24 host scipy cKDTree partner search inside the physical-time loop would break the zero-authoritative-roundtrip contract. Must be device-resident, or accepted-step-only with explicit PI approval.

MISLABELLED CHEMISTRY — the contract says alpha2beta1-collagen (contracts.py:281) but the only sourced preset is INTEGRIN_A5B1, alpha5beta1-fibronectin (hand_kmc.py:150). Running alpha5beta1 numbers under an alpha2beta1 label is a citation-integrity failure, not a modelling approximation.

SCAFFOLD BECOMING PERMANENT — a KINETICS_FROZEN clutch is comfortable: it is stable, it deforms the ECM, and it makes pretty pictures. It also cannot release, cannot crawl, and cannot sense stiffness. The label must state what is NOT represented, or the frozen scaffold will silently become the model.

GATE TOLERANCE AS A BACK DOOR — ledger.assemble_balance takes a caller-supplied tolerance. A tolerance chosen after seeing the residual is gate-loosening. It must be authored as a contract before the run (PI question below).

validation_steps.step: V0 — Single-source Pi_0 + static no-double-count audit (no physics, run first)
validation_steps.what_is_measured: (a) the number of distinct places a run reads Pi_0 from, and whether the value recorded in the run artifact is byte-equal to the value every kernel actually used; (b) the number of independent force channels in the assembled membrane/cortex force that produce an inward isotropic surface tension.
validation_steps.protocol: Build the cell at three Pi_0 values (the three in-tree claims 40/72/133 as LABELLED sweep points, resolved only through `common/turgor_pi0.resolve_pi0_pa`). Assert: every consumer (`ac/cell/assemble.py:147`, `driver.py:1057`, `ff/gamma_floor`, `configs/mcf7_baseline.yaml:81`) resolves from the ONE ledger call and the `Pi0Resolution.as_artifact_record()` in the output equals it. Then a static-import audit in the style of `tests/ac/test_warp_only_contract.py`: assert no runtime path reaches `ff/gamma_floor.gamma_passive_young_laplace` (it is diagnostic-only per its own docstring at `ff/gamma_floor.py:464-480`), and assert `ac/engine/forces_manifest.py` enumerates EXACTLY ONE volumetric/turgor pressure channel for the cytosol and exactly one surface-tension-producing channel for the cortex.
validation_steps.pass_criterion: Count identities, no magnitudes: (1) distinct Pi_0 sources reaching physics == 1; (2) artifact-recorded Pi_0 == kernel-used Pi_0 bitwise; (3) runtime import paths reaching `gamma_passive_young_laplace` == 0; (4) cytosol volumetric-stiffness channels == 1 and cortex isotropic-tension channels == 1 in the manifest.
validation_steps.negative_control: Three deliberate breakages, each must FAIL: (a) config sets 133 Pa while the code constant stays 40 Pa (today's actual tree state for `configs/mcf7_baseline.yaml:81`) -> source count 2, gate FAILS; (b) add `gamma_passive_young_laplace(Pi_0,R)` as an actual force term -> tension channel count 2, gate FAILS; (c) enable BOTH the Guo Pi(V) closure and a separate `K_vol*(V0-V)/V0` volume spring on the cytosol -> volumetric channel count 2, gate FAILS.

validation_steps.step: V1 — Water-flux SIGN, balance fixed point, and antisymmetry (membrane_cytosol_boundary in isolation)
validation_steps.what_is_measured: The integrated membrane volume flux Q = closed-surface integral of L_p(sigma*dPi - dP) dA, and its per-triangle distribution, as a function of the driving offset delta = (sigma*dPi - dP).
validation_steps.protocol: On the banked resting cell, hold geometry fixed and sweep delta through {-2d, -d, 0, +d, +2d} where d is an arbitrary internal unit of the driving force (its magnitude is irrelevant — only ratios are gated). Read `MembraneFluxBC.integrated_flux_d` and `unresolved_faces_d` (`boundary.py:270-300`), plus the per-triangle deposit. Cross-check on the Mac against `coupled_boundary_reference.kedem_katchalsky_influx`.
validation_steps.pass_criterion: Four magnitude-free identities: (1) delta == 0 -> Q == 0 to reduction round-off (the resting fixed point); (2) sign(Q) == sign(delta) on EVERY resolved triangle and in the integral (no mixed-sign faces); (3) exact antisymmetry Q(+delta) == -Q(-delta) and exact linearity Q(2delta)/Q(delta) == 2, both to round-off (the KK law is linear, so these are identities, not fits); (4) `unresolved_faces == 0` and the discretization string == 'LIVE_TRIANGLE_CONSERVATIVE'. Plus the existing NG-2 chain (surface quadrature == source integral == content change) must stay green.
validation_steps.negative_control: (a) Reverse the winding of half the membrane faces -> the outward normal flips, per-triangle signs go mixed and antisymmetry breaks -> must FAIL (catches the wrong-normal class that made the crawl traction cancel). (b) Inject a bogus 1e6 unit factor on dPi only (Pa vs pN/um^2 confusion) -> the delta==0 fixed point moves off zero -> must FAIL. (c) Set L_p = 0 -> Q == 0 for ALL delta, so sign-sense is vacuous; the gate must report VACUOUS rather than PASS.

validation_steps.step: V2 — Water and solute mass conserved SEPARATELY, on two independently sourced ledger channels, with rejected-step bit-identity
validation_steps.what_is_measured: Two distinct conserved quantities over K accepted steps: the water volume V_w (units um^3) and, per solute species i, the solute number N_i (units mol or molecule count). Explicitly NOT the poroelastic storage content `S*integral p dV`, which has different units and is a different quantity.
validation_steps.protocol: Add two new ledger channels (see new_code_needed) alongside the existing generic mass channel; they must be accumulated from independent sources, following the discipline already stated at `ac/engine/ledger.py:11` ('kept independently sourced so the global balance gate is a genuine check, not a self-satisfying one'). Run K accepted steps with sigma_i = 1 (impermeant) and no transporter events. Then run K steps with one permeant species (sigma_i < 1) and a nonzero solute flux. Then propose a step, force the transaction predicate to REJECT, and re-read both channels.
validation_steps.pass_criterion: (1) Water: |Delta V_w - sum(dt*Q_membrane) - swept_content| <= round-off, using the same divergence-theorem closure already proven for pressure content in `coupled_boundary_reference.coupled_step`. (2) Impermeant solute: Delta N_i == 0 BITWISE (not within tolerance — an impermeant species with no event cannot change at all). (3) Permeant solute: |Delta N_i - sum(dt*J_i)| <= round-off. (4) Rejected step: both V_w and every N_i restore bit-identically to the pre-proposal snapshot, and the flux epoch does not advance. (5) Unit guard: asserting the water channel against the solute channel must raise a dimensional error, not compare numerically.
validation_steps.negative_control: (a) Solvent-drag bug: make the water flux also increment the solute channel -> impermeant Delta N_i != 0 -> must FAIL bitwise. (b) Commit-on-reject bug: skip the rollback of the solute pool -> the rejected-step bit-identity FAILS. (c) Name-confusion control: point the 'water' channel at `field_grid.total_content` (the pressure content) -> the closure residual carries the wrong units and the dimensional guard must FAIL, proving the gate is not measuring a differently-named thing.
validation_steps.est_effort: 2-3 d (mostly the two new channels + transaction rollback)

validation_steps.step: V3 — Volume-vs-osmolarity MONOTONICITY with the emergent dPi_eff(V) wired in
validation_steps.what_is_measured: Equilibrium enclosed volume V_eq (membrane mesh volume minus nucleus mesh volume, by divergence theorem on device) as a function of medium ratio r = O_out/O_0, at the oracle's condition set r in {0.70, 0.85, 1.00, 1.15, 1.30} (`validation/oracles/osmotic_response.CONDITIONS`).
validation_steps.protocol: Wire `dPi_eff = RT * sum_i sigma_i*(N_i/(V - V_b) - C_out,i)` as the driver passed to `MembraneFluxBC.apply`, replacing the constant. V comes from the device closed-mesh reduce (reuse `ac/nucleus/envelope.py:177` pattern / `ff/motility_warp.py:341` kernel), NOT from a mean-radius sphere. Relax to the water fixed point at each r; record V_eq, dPi_eff, dP, and the residual driving force.
validation_steps.pass_criterion: Pure ordering and fixed-point statements: (1) V_eq(r) is STRICTLY monotone decreasing across all five r; (2) V_eq(r=1) == V_0 to the solver's own equilibrium tolerance and the trajectory does NOT drift (the reference is a fixed point); (3) the response is single-signed — hyper shrinks, hypo swells, for every b in the sweep; (4) the residual driving force at each converged r is <= the solver tolerance (it actually reached equilibrium, rather than being stopped).
validation_steps.negative_control: (a) THE decisive one: pin dPi back to the constant Pi_0 — i.e. today's shipping code (`driver.py:1057`) — then V_eq becomes independent of r and monotonicity FAILS. This makes the gate a direct discriminator between the current runtime and the new one. (b) Set V_b > V_0 -> unphysical, must raise at resolve, not produce a number. (c) Flip the sign of sigma -> the loop becomes positive feedback and V diverges; the gate must FAIL rather than clamp.

validation_steps.step: V4 — Boyle-van't Hoff SHAPE gate + round-trip parameter recovery (the magnitude-free centrepiece)
validation_steps.what_is_measured: v = V_eq/V_0 plotted against 1/r; the fitted slope and intercept; and separately the three principal stretches of the deformed cell.
validation_steps.protocol: From V3's five (or more) r-points, regress v on 1/r. Compare against the runtime-forbidden acceptance oracle `validation/oracles/osmotic_response.pbvh_v_eq` (which its own test already proves returns slope 1-b and intercept b exactly). Independently reduce lambda_x, lambda_y, lambda_z from the actual deformed membrane mesh (principal extents), and reduce V, A_basal, A_topdown, h as FOUR separate reductions.
validation_steps.pass_criterion: No absolute value anywhere: (1) linearity — regression r^2 >= 1 - eps with eps DERIVED from the per-point equilibrium residual, not chosen; (2) ROUND-TRIP IDENTITY — recovered intercept == the configured b = V_b/V_0 and recovered slope == (1 - b), to solver tolerance. Whatever b you put in you must get out, so the gate holds for any b and needs no literature value; (3) conservation — lambda_x*lambda_y*lambda_z == v exactly (the oracle's own conservation identity, now measured rather than assumed); (4) TAUTOLOGY GUARD — V/V_0, A_basal/A_0, A_topdown/A_0 and h/h_0 must be four independent reductions, and at least one r must produce V/V_0 != A/A_0; if they coincide for all r the metric is a tautology and the gate reports FAIL, not PASS.
validation_steps.negative_control: (a) Drop the osmotically-inactive volume (use V instead of V - V_b in the concentration) -> recovered intercept collapses toward 0 != configured b -> FAIL. (b) Measure 'volume' as A_topdown^(3/2) instead of the mesh enclosed volume -> recovered b is wrong -> FAIL. This is the direct guard against the recorded basal-vs-topdown A/A0 failure (twice) and the A/A0 == V/V0 == 1.000 tautology. (c) Report V/V0 for the WHOLE grid instead of membrane-minus-nucleus -> the intercept shifts by the nucleus fraction -> FAIL.

validation_steps.step: V5 — Per-step flux-sign identity and closure of the negative-feedback homeostat (dynamics)
validation_steps.what_is_measured: At every accepted step: sign(dV_w/dt) vs sign(sigma*dPi_eff - dP); and the magnitude |sigma*dPi_eff - dP| along a step-change trajectory.
validation_steps.protocol: Apply a step change in medium osmolarity at t=0 (impermeant, no transporters, R=0) and integrate to the new fixed point. Log the signed driving force and the signed volume rate every step. Fit the resulting v(t) to a single exponential, with tau_w FITTED FROM THE RUN (never supplied).
validation_steps.pass_criterion: (1) Per-step sign identity holds at EVERY step, with no exceptions — this is the Starling law's definition, checked as an emergent trajectory property; (2) the homeostat closes: |sigma*dPi_eff - dP| decreases MONOTONICALLY to <= tolerance, i.e. the chain V down -> C_in up -> dPi_eff up -> driving force down is realised, not asserted; (3) SHAPE gate against the analytic oracle: v(t) matches a single-pole relaxation `v_eq + (1-v_eq)exp(-t/tau_w)` (oracle `v_passive`) with fit residual <= tolerance and NO overshoot; (4) grid-invariance of the FITTED tau_w across two dx and two dt (so the timescale is physics, not discretization). Absolute tau_w in seconds is stamped BLOCKED.
validation_steps.negative_control: (a) Constant Pi_0 (today's code): the driving force does NOT decay monotonically to zero as V changes — it stays pinned — so criterion (2) FAILS. (b) Reverse sigma: positive feedback, V diverges, criterion (1) inverts -> FAIL. (c) Hard-wire dV_w/dt from the sign of the driving force instead of integrating the flux -> criterion (1) becomes vacuously true; the gate must detect vacuity by checking that dV_w came from the same accumulated flux the mass ledger used (V2 channel), not from a recomputation.

validation_steps.step: V6 — Load-unload reversibility cycle with an ATTRIBUTED hysteresis budget
validation_steps.what_is_measured: V(t) around a closed medium cycle r: 1 -> 1.30 -> 1 and 1 -> 0.85 -> 1; the closed-loop pressure work; and the decomposition of any residual into (numerical drift, crosslink-turnover dissipation, motor work).
validation_steps.protocol: Two configurations. ELASTIC: crosslink turnover OFF (`ff/motility_warp.py:356 xl_turnover_kernel` disabled), motors OFF, impermeant solute, no transporters. DISSIPATIVE: turnover ON and/or motors ON. Run the full closed cycle in both, integrating the same water-mass channel from V2 for the flux bound.
validation_steps.pass_criterion: (1) ELASTIC: |V_end - V_start| <= the accumulated flux-integration round-off bound derived from the V2 closure (a conservation bound, not a guessed tolerance), AND the closed-loop pressure work returns to zero to round-off; (2) DISSIPATIVE: the residual must be NONZERO and must EQUAL the independently measured dissipated work (turnover + motor channels) to within the same round-off — so hysteresis is EARNED and attributed, never numerical; (3) the numerical component of the residual is <= round-off in BOTH configurations.
validation_steps.negative_control: (a) Assert exact reversibility with turnover ON -> must FAIL, proving the gate can actually see irreversibility (a gate that passes both ways is the 'written so a broken build cannot fail it' failure). (b) Run the ELASTIC case with a deliberately loosened solver tolerance -> the residual must exceed the round-off bound and FAIL, proving the gate is not vacuous. (c) Attribute the dissipative residual to the wrong channel (swap turnover and motor accounting) -> the equality in (2) breaks -> FAIL.

validation_steps.step: V7 — Young-Laplace partner NOT double-counted: the slope-1/2 dimensionless test
validation_steps.what_is_measured: Measured cortical tension gamma (from the existing plane-cut / virial estimator, NOT from Pi_0) as a function of Pi_0 along the sweep axis, at fixed R.
validation_steps.protocol: Sweep Pi_0 across the sweep axis (V0's labelled points, plus intermediate values). At each point, converge the resting cell and measure gamma from the cortex stress independently of the pressure. Regress gamma on Pi_0. The static half of this gate already ran in V0; this is the dynamic half.
validation_steps.pass_criterion: One dimensionless ratio: fitted slope divided by (R/2) == 1 to solver tolerance, with the intercept equal to the myosin-only gamma at Pi_0 = 0. Young-Laplace makes the slope exactly R/2 as an OUTPUT; a double-counted passive tension shows up as a factor of exactly 2 in a dimensionless ratio, so NO absolute gamma and NO literature band is needed. Independent-tension-channel count stays 1 (from V0).
validation_steps.negative_control: Add `gamma_passive_young_laplace(Pi_0, R)` (`ff/gamma_floor.py:464`) as an actual force term -> the fitted slope/(R/2) comes out ~2 and the gate FAILS. Second control: omit Pi_0 entirely and let a default appear -> `resolve_pi0_pa` must raise `TurgorPi0Unspecified` (already covered by `tests/ac/test_turgor_pi0_gate_and_banners.py`). Third: use the MCF7 gamma band to select Pi_0 -> flagged as CIRCULAR and refused, since 133 Pa was produced exactly that way (`params_turgor.yaml claim_band_implied_133pa`).

validation_steps.step: V8 — CONNECTEDNESS: an osmotic step must actually DEFORM every mechanically-coupled compartment (the PI priority gate)
validation_steps.what_is_measured: Per-component displacement (membrane, cortex, nucleus, MT aster, IF cage, sf_arc, ECM anchor points) from ONE accepted osmotic step, plus each connector's two-sided transmitted resultant, plus the global resultant decomposition.
validation_steps.protocol: From the banked resting state, apply a step in medium osmolarity. Read displacements per component from the population ledger (unique-ID disjoint populations, `ac/engine/population.py`). Read each connector's A-side and B-side resultants. Assemble the global balance through `ac/engine/ledger.py` with the reaction and traction channels kept independently sourced.
validation_steps.pass_criterion: Four checks, all magnitude-free: (1) NON-ZERO DISPLACEMENT for every mechanically-connected component, and the loaded state must NOT be bit-identical to the rest state — the direct rebuttal of the measured 494,802-node failure where cortex moved 39.8 nm while the MT aster and nucleus moved 0.0 nm bit-identically; (2) each connector's two sides carry equal-and-opposite resultants to round-off (Newton 3rd), and the adjoint-work residual |<Wv,g> - <v,W^T g>| <= round-off (reuse `coupled_boundary_reference.adjoint_work_residual`); (3) the sum of all INTERNAL connector reactions == 0 while each individual transmitted magnitude is > 0 — internal cancellation must be shown to coexist with real transmission; (4) SYMMETRY: with ECM detached, an isotropic osmotic step must produce ZERO net COM translation to round-off (an isotropic Δπ cannot translate the cell).
validation_steps.negative_control: (a) Re-merge membrane and cortex into one shared position array (the co-location bug) -> check (2) becomes vacuously satisfied while check (1) fails for nucleus/MT -> gate FAILS, and it must report WHICH check failed. (b) Drop one connector's reaction (make it one-sided) -> check (2) FAILS and the global resultant becomes nonzero. (c) ⚠ Anti-vacuity control specific to this track: gate ONLY on the net force resultant. Because an isotropic osmotic traction is radial, its vector sum is EXACTLY zero by symmetry, so a net-force-only gate PASSES even when nothing is transmitted at all. The gate must demonstrate that this degenerate variant passes on a deliberately disconnected build — which is why checks (1) and (3) exist.
validation_steps.est_effort: 2-3 d, and it depends on making membrane_cytosol_boundary force-real

validation_steps.step: V9 — Grid, mesh, and dt invariance + derived CFL of the coupled water mode
validation_steps.what_is_measured: The V4-recovered b, the ordering of V_eq(r), and the V5-fitted tau_w, each at 2 grid spacings dx x 2 membrane mesh refinements x 2 dt, at the FULL native population.
validation_steps.protocol: Repeat V3/V4/V5 across the refinement matrix. Derive the water-mode stability bound from the Guo closure — tau = V/(L_p*A*K_eff) with K_eff = Pi_in0/(1-b), which is DERIVED (`ff/gamma_floor.py:329`), not tuned — and combine it with the existing `field_grid.cfl_dt` Biot bound.
validation_steps.pass_criterion: (1) recovered b and the r-ordering are invariant within solver tolerance across all six configurations; (2) V_eq converges at the design order under dx refinement; (3) fitted tau_w is invariant within tolerance; (4) halving dt changes the trajectory by <= O(dt); (5) the run at 2x the derived CFL bound is DETECTED as unstable and rejected, never silently clamped or stabilised by lowering L_p.
validation_steps.negative_control: (a) Coarsen only the membrane mesh and keep dx fixed -> if the answer moves beyond tolerance the gate FAILS, guarding the recorded failure mode where six conclusions were drawn from coarse/stripped configurations and later contradicted natively. (b) 'Fix' the stiffness by reducing L_p until the run is stable -> the L_p provenance record changes, and the gate must FAIL on the parameter-change audit (stability is the integrator's job, never L_p's). (c) Run the whole matrix at a stripped population and assert it substitutes for the native run -> must be refused by the native-population guard.

validation_steps.step: V10 — Adherent-on-2D-collagen: volume separated from SHAPE (the PI baseline configuration)

risks: LOAD-PATH-SUMS-TO-ZERO, and this track is the WORST case for it: an isotropic osmotic step produces a purely radial traction whose vector sum is EXACTLY zero by symmetry. So a global net-force gate is not merely weak here — it is vacuous, and it will pass on a completely disconnected build. This is structurally the same error as the crawl having no locomotory dipole (traction isotropic and laterally cancelling, F_net one quarter of one clutch). Mitigation: V8 gates per-connector transmitted MAGNITUDE and per-component DISPLACEMENT, and explicitly demonstrates that the net-force-only variant passes on a disconnected build.

METRIC MEASURING THE WRONG THING, three concrete instances already latent in the tree: (a) `ff/gamma_floor.turgor_pressure:335-338` computes V from the CORTEX mean radius as (4/3)pi*R_mean^3 — wiring the Guo law naively would couple dPi to a sphere-equivalent radius, which is badly wrong for an adherent flattened cell and would silently rescale every BvH result; (b) `field_grid.total_content` is `S*integral p dV`, a poroelastic storage content in pressure units, and calling it 'water mass' would be a naming error with no numerical symptom; (c) V/V0 measured over the whole grid instead of membrane-minus-nucleus shifts the BvH intercept by the nucleus fraction. All three are the same class as the recorded basal-vs-topdown A/A0 failure (twice), the Young-Dupre gate returning 120.0000 degrees by construction, and the A/A0 = V/V0 = 1.000 tautology.

TAUTOLOGY RISK, specific and high: if V, A and h are derived from ONE reduction (say a sphere-equivalent radius), then A/A0 = (V/V0)^(2/3) identically and the shape gate certifies nothing. V4's four-independent-reductions assertion exists solely for this.

TRIPLE PRE-STRESS DOUBLE-COUNT. Three volumetric/tension channels could be live simultaneously: the Guo Pi(V) closure (derives K_vol), a separate `K_vol*(V0-V)/V0` volume spring (the DCM law is in-tree and `configs/mcf7_baseline.yaml:70-78` still declares an `enclosed_volume` compartment with `turgor_dP0: 133.0`), and `gamma_passive_young_laplace` if anyone promotes it from diagnostic to force. The framework doc warns about exactly this at `CELL_MECHANICS_FRAMEWORK_2026-07-15.md:113-115` ('Do NOT re-add dP's Young-Laplace partner as an independent passive cortex tension'). Mitigation: V0's channel-count audit plus V7's slope/(R/2) == 1 test, where a double-count appears as a factor of exactly 2 in a dimensionless ratio.

THREE IN-TREE Pi_0 VALUES SPANNING 3.3x. 40 Pa (`ff/gamma_floor.py:105`), 133 Pa (`configs/mcf7_baseline.yaml:81`, still reading as CURRENT with no supersession marker), ~72 Pa (unwired). A sweep that reads Pi_0 from a different place than the artifact records produces an un-diagnosable inconsistency, and it is the exact setup that made 133 Pa circular in the first place. V0 is the guard; the yaml's missing supersession marker is an open PI item.

CIRCULARITY RE-ENTRY. 133 Pa was produced by inverting the MCF7 gamma band (`params_turgor.yaml claim_band_implied_133pa`, 'CIRCULAR by construction'). If the Pi_0 sweep axis is later narrowed using a gamma-band gate, the circularity returns wearing a sweep's clothing. V7's slope test is legitimate because it tests a SHAPE (slope = R/2, independent of Pi_0's value); using the gamma band to SELECT Pi_0 is not, and must be refused explicitly.

REFERENCE-STATE DRIFT. Every observable in this track is a ratio to V_0. With GATE A open, V_0 is not a converged equilibrium, so a drifting reference silently rescales the BvH intercept and slope. Mitigation: require the reference to be a BANKED, bit-reproducible, re-seedable state; record V_0 in the artifact; stamp every absolute magnitude BLOCKED.

STIFFNESS 'FIXED' BY LOWERING L_p. The water mode's timescale tau = V/(L_p*A*K_eff) with the Guo-derived K_eff can make the coupled system stiff. The tempting fix — reduce L_p until it is stable — is a parameter change made to pass a gate, which the hard rules forbid. Guard: L_p is an input with a provenance record; stability is the integrator's responsibility (implicit or sub-cycled, both already available), and V9's negative control makes the L_p-lowering path FAIL an audit rather than quietly succeed.

REJECTED-STEP LEAKAGE. The water and solute pools are the newest commit-on-accept state. A missing rollback shows up as slow monotone mass drift that looks indistinguishable from physics — and would be reported as an osmotic result. V2's bitwise rejected-step control is the only thing that catches it cheaply.

A NEW LUMPED CONFOUND ENTERING AS A 'STABILISER'. Any 'volume relaxation helper' or 'shell stabiliser' added to keep the pressurised mesh well-behaved is a lumped body force in disguise. The precedent is severe: SettlingForce ran at 19,000-47,000x real buoyant weight, was ON in every committed spreading run, was mislabelled proxy_off, did the flattening credited to the lamellipodium, and the regression gates locked the confound in. Guard: every force acting on the membrane must appear in `ac/engine/forces_manifest.py` with a provenance class, and the manifest COUNT must be asserted in the test — plus V10's clutches-disabled control, which reproduces the flattening if a body force is doing the work.

CONCLUSIONS FROM A COARSE CONFIGURATION. Six times a conclusion drawn from a coarse or stripped configuration was later contradicted natively; and the cortex mesh is currently 5-10x too coarse by its own provenance record (`params_turgor.yaml convenience_labels.cortex_seg_um`: 0.5 um vs a sourced 0.05-0.10 um). The osmotic response depends on membrane mesh resolution through the area and the volume reduce, so V9's mesh-only refinement leg is not optional, and the full-native run must be the arbiter.

BLEB CONCLUSIONS ARE ALREADY IN THE INVALID REGIME. `ac/cell/bleb_growth.py:185` passes the constant Pi_0. Bleb inflation redistributes enclosed volume on a timescale comparable to or faster than tau_w, so a pinned dPi supplies an inexhaustible pressure source and the growth law is wrong. Any existing bleb-growth claim from that path must be stamped BLOCKED, not quietly carried forward.

GATE VACUITY IN GENERAL. One in-tree gate was written so a broken build could not fail it (largest-fragment vs 2nd-largest instead of absolute connectivity), and one probe computed p - p, a self-difference identically zero for any field. Every gate above therefore carries a named negative control, and three of them (V1c, V6b, V8c) test the GATE rather than the physics — they must be run, and their failure to fail is itself a finding.

ION CHANNELS — approve the recommendation? My defensible answer is NO, not for mechanics now, and here is the reasoning. Aquaporin water permeability is LEGITIMATELY lumpable into L_p, and this is categorically different from the lumpings the project forbids: Bell-Evans-vs-Metropolis, Hill-vs-linear-stall, and Stam-Hocky-vs-2-head-spring all destroy a discrete, FORCE-DEPENDENT, LOAD-BEARING mechanism, whereas aquaporin bears no load, is not force-gated in the mechanical range, and enters the mechanics only through the scalar areal flux — nothing downstream can distinguish 10^4 channels each passing J/10^4 from a uniform L_p. So L_p is a constitutive coefficient, not a proxy for a mechanism. What is genuinely missing is one rung DOWN in the dependency order: the conserved pools N_i with per-solute sigma_i and the live enclosed volume V. Pools are STATE; channels are the RATE LAW that changes that state. Building channels before the pool exists would give a rate law with no conserved quantity to act on — structurally the same error as a load path that sums to zero. And in your current baseline (adherent, in medium, r = 1, quasi-static) ion fluxes are at homeostatic steady state by definition, so their net contribution to dPi_eff is a constant — which is exactly the constant Pi_0 you just ratified as a sweep axis. Adding channels now would introduce conductances, densities and pump stoichiometries that are all PI-GAPs, lowering the sourced fraction of the model while changing no mechanical prediction. Keep `ff/piezo.py` as a READ-ONLY reporter wired to the membrane tension the model already computes, with CA_FEEDBACK_GAIN at 0. TRIGGERS to add them, proposed as a contract: T1 any claim involving ACTIVE volume regulation (the oracle's R != 0) — passive water flux cannot produce recovery, recovery requires N_i to change; T2 permeant-vs-impermeant discrimination (mannitol vs glycerol), which needs per-solute sigma_i plus a solute permeation pathway; T3 the inference platform treating ion homeostasis as a CELL-STATE axis (same MCF7 in DMEM vs Krebs at matched osmolality, or a transporter-inhibitor perturbation) — then the channel is the inferred object and must be explicit; T4 a mechanosensitive channel asked to CLOSE A MECHANICAL LOOP (tension -> Ca -> contractility), at which point it bears causal weight on force and must be fine-grained, with conductance/density/Ca-gain sourced FIRST; T5 the hypotonic/lysis limit where the volume trajectory is bounded by channel-mediated efflux rather than by V_b. ANTI-TRIGGER: wanting a 'more realistic' cytoplasm, or trying to fix an absolute Pi_0 — that is a magnitude problem you have explicitly deprioritised, and channels are the most expensive possible way to adjust a scalar. When they do come, they come as rate-conditioned transporter EVENTS on the conserved pool under the accepted-step transaction (the clutch / monomer-flux discipline), never as a continuum current density. Please ratify or amend T1-T5.

MEDIUM AS STRUCTURED STATE. `CellState.osmotic_state` is currently the string 'physiological_resting' (`ac/engine/cell_state.py:142,220`). Promote it now to a sourced composition (species, C_out,i, sigma_i, osmolality) — a state-schema change — or leave it a label until T1/T2 fire?

CHANGE `ProtrusionGraphConnector.accumulate_actor(actor)` (`protrusion.py:133`) to a two-endpoint `accumulate_actor(actor, endpoint)` mirroring `MicrotubuleGraphConnector.accumulate_rig(rig, endpoint)` (`microtubule_rig.py:143`) — as written the protocol has no external endpoint and therefore structurally cannot scatter the adjoint reaction its docstring promises. Bind the seam/root as transient-actin Hookean+Bell pairs, then run the full T3-4 closure battery plus a slip sweep over bound fraction. Exercise `branch_angle_kernel` (already native on the cortex path at arp23_fraction=0.33) under the lamellipodium OWNER for the first time.
validation_steps.pass_criterion: (a) PROTOCOL CONFORMANCE + ADJOINT: the seam connector receives BOTH endpoints and Σf_protrusion + Σf_cortex = 0 to ≤1e-12. (b) DRAG: pushing the protrusion tip moves cortex root nodes, with sign along the push (per T3-5). (c) SLIP MONOTONICITY: with the transient bonds unbound, protrusion-relative-to-cortex displacement > 0 (it is a connector, not a weld); relative displacement decreases monotonically with bound fraction. (d) ARP2/3 DISTRIBUTION: the branch-angle histogram is centred at θ₀ with thermal spread consistent with the equipartition round-trip in `ac/weave/branch_angle.py:143` — an internal-consistency check on the k_θ = kT/σ_θ² setting rule, no external magnitude.
validation_steps.negative_control: (i) Keep the one-endpoint signature ⇒ the adjoint test must FAIL, proving the protocol change is load-bearing rather than cosmetic. (ii) Set bound fraction = 1 with rest length 0 ⇒ relative displacement collapses to 0 and the gate must report WELD, not PASS — the co-location trap made explicit. (iii) Build the filopodium with `FASCIN_K_CROSSLINK_PN_PER_UM = None` ⇒ must RAISE, so the bundle gate is explicitly BLOCKED on card F1 rather than silently inheriting the filamin value the constant's comment forbids. (iv) Rigid-angle Arp2/3 (σ_θ = 0) ⇒ (d) must FAIL, distinguishing the angle-harmonic-with-thermal-fluctuation mechanism from a rigid 72° hinge.

validation_steps.what_is_measured: The full component-to-component transmission matrix T_ij = |Δ_j,COM| / |F_i| over {sf_arc, microtubule, intermediate_filament, nucleus, cortex-port}, its ZERO PATTERN, and its symmetry.
validation_steps.protocol: One transaction with all five Track-3 edges force-real (T3-4, T3-6, T3-7 plus a new `mt_sf_spectraplakin` cytolinker connector). Load each component in turn at a small amplitude verified to be in the linear-response regime (halve the load; T must be unchanged), converge, and measure every other component's displacement response. Assemble T and compare its zero pattern to the transitive closure of the connector adjacency graph, computed and WRITTEN DOWN BEFORE the run. Run the reciprocity check with MOTORS OFF (a passive conservative frame), and separately verify that a motor edge BREAKS symmetry.
validation_steps.pass_criterion: (a) CONNECTEDNESS AS A ZERO PATTERN: T's zero pattern EQUALS the connector adjacency's transitive closure — the machine-checkable, entirely magnitude-free statement of 'every part is mechanically connected'. No zero where the graph says there is a path; no nonzero where it says there is none. (b) MAXWELL–BETTI RECIPROCITY: with motors off and in the verified linear regime, T is symmetric within solver tolerance — one check that simultaneously catches one-sided connectors and mismatched adjoint interpolation weights. (c) GRID-INVARIANCE: the zero pattern is unchanged across a 2× refinement. (d) ACTIVE ASYMMETRY: with `nmii_sf_motor` on, T becomes asymmetric — a motor connector MUST break reciprocity, so this is a positive control on the gate's discriminating power.
validation_steps.negative_control: (i) Disable exactly ONE edge: the zero pattern must change to precisely the new transitive closure, predicted before the run. (ii) Disable ALL Track-3 connectors: T must be exactly DIAGONAL — the block-diagonal state deliberately reproduced as the reference failure, so the gate is anchored at both ends. (iii) Perturb one connector's adjoint scatter weight by 1%: (b) must FAIL, proving symmetry is measured and not imposed by construction.

risks: LOAD PATH THAT SUMS TO ZERO — the highest-probability Track-3 failure. An MT aster is radially symmetric and an IF cage is radially symmetric, so a radial load transmits per-edge and cancels globally, exactly as the crawl traction did (isotropic radial grip, lateral cancellation, F_net one quarter of one clutch). Mitigation: every gate reports |Sigma f| AND Sigma|f| separately, every drag gate carries a SYMMETRIC-load control that must return net ~0, and connectedness is judged on a NET displacement, never on Sigma|f|.

CO-LOCATION MISTAKEN FOR COUPLING, now with a new and more convincing disguise. build_microtubule_compartment(reach_R_um=7.4) puts MT tips exactly AT the cortex radius; on the current lanes both would live on cell.pos_d/cell.f_d. Tips touching plus one shared array reproduces the 39.8 nm / 0.0 nm / 0.0 nm bit-identical result while LOOKING connected in every render. FORCE-APPEARS MISTAKEN FOR MOTION. The existing IF coupling test (tests/ac/solid/test_intermediate_filament.py:33) displaces cortex nodes and asserts force appears on the IF spokes — but its own comment concedes 'Single force-eval only stretches bonds whose endpoints moved (full transmission to the far side needs relaxation = the outer solver)'. Mitigation: the drag gate measures far-component DISPLACEMENT from a CONVERGED state; the single-force-eval metric is run alongside and reported as the counter-example.

TAUTOLOGICAL ANALYTIC GATE, already present in the tree. tests/ac/solid/test_microtubule.py:31 test_euler_buckling_load_matches_analytic asserts euler_buckling_load(20,5) approx pi^2*20/25 — the closed form against itself. Same shape as the Young-Dupre gate returning 120.0000 deg by construction and the A/A0 = V/V0 = 1.000 tautology. Mitigation: F* must come from a measured bifurcation of the discrete constrained solve, and the oracle comparison must test RATIO INVARIANCE across L and mesh, never a value; retire the tautological test explicitly.

MT HAS NO AXIAL FORCE TERM AT ALL. MicrotubuleCompartment.accumulate launches only cytosim_bending_kernel (ac/solid/microtubule.py:88-92); axial load lives entirely in the NF2007 inextensibility constraint. A compression gate run on a bare force eval reads exactly 0, and that zero could be misreported EITHER as 'MT feels nothing, therefore decoupled' OR as 'no residual, therefore fine'. Mitigation: the compression observable is the constraint multiplier and the gate runs through the projected solver.

CONVERGENCE, NOT CONNECTEDNESS, WILL BE THE ACTUAL FAILURE MODE. The SF GATE-B tension was withdrawn as a relaxation transient at 15.5% residual, where a 10x longer relax moved T_max by 3.4x at an identical bound population. Alpha-actinin at 4.6e5 pN/um already gives lambda_max ~ 3.7e6 and a CFL step ~1.4e-7; adding MT (kappa ~300x actin) and plectin makes conditioning worse. An unconverged drag gate reports a transient as a transmission ratio. Mitigation: every drag/transmission number is gated on the converged projected-force triple test, the artifact carries residual AND residual/signal, and a 10x longer solve must move the result inside the PI-set tolerance.

A GATE A BROKEN BUILD CANNOT FAIL. The project already shipped one (largest-fragment vs 2nd-largest instead of absolute connectivity). Every Track-3 step therefore carries a does-the-metric-respond-to-the-mechanism control: alpha_bend = 0 must kill F*, k_connector -> 0 must kill drag continuously, DI growth rate = 0 must freeze length, the linear adapter must FAIL the stiffening test, rigid Arp2/3 must FAIL the angle distribution. Any step whose control cannot be constructed should be treated as an unwritable gate, not a passing one.

UNRATIFIED PROXIES SILENTLY DRIVING A RUN, then reading as evidence. Track 3 is full of them: DynamicInstabilityRateCard(ratified=False), keratin wall EA = None, FASCIN_K_CROSSLINK_PN_PER_UM = None, linc_per_node = 1 (grid-dependent), eps_rupture = 0.50 which the owning parameter gate explicitly says not to keep. RECIPROCITY GATE MISAPPLIED. Maxwell-Betti holds only for a conservative, linearized frame; motors and catch bonds break it LEGITIMATELY. Reporting a genuine active asymmetry as a bug would be a self-inflicted false finding. Mitigation: run reciprocity with motors OFF at a load amplitude verified linear (halve the load, T unchanged), then test motors separately for the OPPOSITE property — a motor edge MUST break symmetry.

BREADTH ACCUMULATING FASTER THAN CONVERGENCE, again. Four Track-3 components already sit at KERNEL_BOUND with kernels that have never been codegen'd; the LINC module is 1,581 lines with zero callers and is not even exported. Because IF has no cortex and no ECM edge among the 32, the keratin-versus-vimentin EMT contrast — the most publishable-sounding Track-3 result — is unreachable today, and keratin's EA is None. Bind it as the `nucleus` CORE_BODY owner via `interior_column_slice.build_core_surface_owner` but with the PRIVATE arrays, not `cell.pos_d`/`cell.f_d`. (2) With the omit-mask on, the sum of the engine-owned nucleus channel forces equals the incumbent's nucleus contribution node-by-node to <1e-12 relative (pure refactor parity — no physics change). validation_steps.step: N2 — STANDALONE shell indentation: Reissner regime, exponents and analytic-oracle ratio
validation_steps.what_is_measured: Indenter reaction F vs prescribed depth δ on the nucleus alone with volume and chromatin channels OFF (vented shell): the small-δ linear stiffness k_lin = dF/dδ|₀, and the dimensionless ratio k_lin·R/√(κ·K_soft).
validation_steps.protocol: Build a rigid spherical indenter of radius R_ind ≪ R_nuc acting only on nucleus-owned nodes, driven by PRESCRIBED displacement with the contact nodes Dirichlet-pinned (not a penalty spring) so no probe stiffness enters. Solve to a converged residual with the new nucleus-block implicit CG (see new_code_needed) and report the NUCLEUS-BLOCK max|PF|, not the whole-cell max. Sweep δ over the sub-knee range (max face areal strain < knee, verified per run). Then sweep κ_NE ×{0.25,0.5,1,2,4}, K_soft ×{0.25,0.5,1,2,4}, R_nuc ×{0.5,1,2} and fit log-log slopes. Repeat the whole sweep at subdiv 3/4/5.
validation_steps.pass_criterion: (1) log-log slope of k_lin in κ = 0.50 ± 0.05, in K_soft = 0.50 ± 0.05, in R = −1.00 ± 0.10 (the Reissner point-load exponents — pure exponents, no biological magnitude). (2) The dimensionless ratio k_lin·R/√(κK) equals the analytic Reissner constant within 15% at subdiv 5 and its error DECREASES monotonically subdiv 3→4→5. (3) k_lin changes <5% between subdiv 4 and 5 (grid-invariance). (4) Admissibility: the measured indentation boundary-layer width must exceed the mean mesh edge length at the reported subdivision — otherwise the run is declared UNRESOLVED and reports no stiffness.
validation_steps.negative_control: Set κ_NE = 0: the √κ exponent gate must FAIL and the response must not be Reissner-like (it becomes a floppy tension sheet). Second: keep κ but replace the prescribed-displacement pinning with a soft penalty probe — the fitted k_lin must drop (series compliance) and the Reissner-ratio gate must FAIL, proving the protocol, not the shell, is being measured. Third: rotate the indentation axis by an arbitrary angle — F(δ) must be unchanged within a mesh-anisotropy tolerance measured on the UNDEFORMED mesh, and that tolerance must shrink with refinement.

validation_steps.step: N3 — Build the EXPLICIT chromatin polymer net and gate it as a population, not a modulus

(2) As δ grows, the max per-link r=x/L increases monotonically and the chromatin channel stiffens superlinearly (dF_chrom/dδ increasing), i.e. WLC finite extensibility is visible, with no link exceeding r=0.999999 (the kernel guard must never be the active limiter — if it is, the run is declared invalid). (3) Σf_chrom = 0 to 1e-10 (internal net). (4) IDs disjoint; no filament counted twice.
validation_steps.negative_control: Build the net with links whose contour length far exceeds any achievable extension (fully slack): the chromatin channel reaction must be identically 0 at every δ and the extensivity slope gate must be reported as N/A, not as a pass. Second: build the net NOT tethered to the envelope (free-floating interior net): the chromatin contribution to the INDENTER reaction must be exactly 0 — this is the co-location trap in miniature (links present in the same array but not connected).
validation_steps.est_effort: 4–5 dev-days (this is the largest genuinely-missing physics piece; also needs the PI decision on double-counting vs the lumped k_chrom)

validation_steps.step: N4 — COMPOSITE separation: shell-dominated small δ vs chromatin-dominated large δ, with a measurable crossover and two different mode shapes
validation_steps.what_is_measured: (a) Per-channel share of the indenter reaction vs δ; (b) the crossover depth δ* where the chromatin share exceeds the shell (bending+lamina) share; (c) the displacement field mode shape — decay length of |u(r)| away from the contact, and the FAR-POLE displacement |u(antipode)|/δ.
validation_steps.protocol: Run the full composite (bending + lamina + volume + chromatin) at a δ ladder from the N2 linear range up to just below the max face strain that would trigger rupture (rupture channel OFF for this step). At each converged δ, decompose the indenter reaction by channel using the N0 ledger, and after removing best-fit rigid translation+rotation (Procrustes) measure the radial displacement profile and the antipodal displacement. Repeat with chromatin OFF as the paired ablation arm at identical δ. Establish the mesh-noise floor for |u(antipode)| from an UNLOADED converged run.
validation_steps.pass_criterion: (1) Channel shares: at the smallest δ, shell share > chromatin share; the chromatin share is monotonically increasing in δ and crosses 50% at a single δ* inside the pre-rupture range (existence + monotonicity + ordering only — δ* itself is reported and explicitly BLOCKED as a magnitude). (2) Mode shape: with chromatin OFF, |u(antipode)|/δ is at or below the unloaded mesh-noise floor at every δ (near-field-only shell response); with chromatin ON it exceeds that floor by ≥10× at δ ≥ δ*. (3) The ablation ΔF(δ) = F_on − F_off is ≥ 0 at every δ (sign-sense: an added internal net cannot soften) and ΔF/F is monotonically increasing in δ. (4) All three findings hold at subdiv 4 and 5 with the crossover ordering unchanged (grid-invariance of the ORDERING, not of δ*).
validation_steps.negative_control: The N3 free-floating (untethered) net arm re-run here: it must produce ΔF ≡ 0 and NO crossover, and the far-pole gate must stay at the noise floor. Second: swap the chromatin channel's force for a same-magnitude isotropic radial field about the nucleus centroid (a lumped proxy): the far-pole displacement gate must still pass but the extensivity slope (N3) and the local per-link tension histogram must FAIL — proving the two gates together distinguish an explicit net from a lumped stand-in.

validation_steps.step: N5 — Incompressibility, path-independence, and rupture emergence (three conservation/reversibility gates)
validation_steps.what_is_measured: Enclosed nucleoplasm volume V/V0 during indentation vs K_vol; Young-Laplace consistency p_vol = 2σ_mean/R; loading/unloading hysteresis; per-face rupture count vs eps_rupture; total work closure.
validation_steps.protocol: Arm A (incompressible): sweep K_vol ×{0.1,1,10,100} at fixed δ, recording V/V0 from `nucleoplasm_volume_reduce_kernel` and the device p_vol, and the mean lamina tension from the lamina channel. Arm B (reversibility): quasi-static load to δ_max then unload on the same ladder with rupture OFF. Arm C (rupture): with rupture ON, ramp δ past the strain that exceeds eps_rupture and count torn faces per accepted step. Arm D (work closure): accumulate indenter work Σ F·dδ and compare to ΔU_bend + ΔU_lamina + ΔU_vol + ΔU_chrom from the N0 energy reductions.
validation_steps.pass_criterion: (A) |V/V0 − 1| decreases with K_vol with log-log slope −1.00 ± 0.15, and p_vol = 2σ_mean/R_eff to within 10% at every K_vol (the `young_laplace_pressure` oracle, already implemented and CPU-green). (B) With rupture OFF, load and unload retrace: max |F_load(δ) − F_unload(δ)| / max F < the solver residual tolerance (all four channels are conservative ⇒ zero hysteresis is a theorem, not a fit). (C) Torn-face count is exactly 0 for every face whose peak areal strain stayed below eps_rupture and strictly > 0 once exceeded; tearing is monotone non-decreasing across accepted steps and a REJECTED step leaves the tear count bit-identical. (D) Work closure |W_indenter − ΔU_total| / |W_indenter| < 1e-3.
validation_steps.negative_control: (A) Set K_vol = 0: V/V0 must change measurably — this is the explicit guard against the documented A/A0 = V/V0 = 1.000 tautology, where volume looked conserved because it could not vary. (B) Turn rupture ON in the reversibility arm: the retrace gate must FAIL (irreversible channel), proving the gate is sensitive to path dependence. (C) Lower eps_rupture below the resting strain: the entire envelope must tear at step 1, and the resting-state gate must FAIL rather than reporting a plausible number. (D) Scale one channel's force by 1.5 without changing its energy: the work-closure gate must FAIL.

validation_steps.step: N6 — MT standalone at CUDA: the strut must actually bear compression (dependency check before in-situ)
validation_steps.what_is_measured: Axial compressive load at which a single pinned-pinned MT buckles, vs the analytic Euler load π²EI/L²; lateral deflection amplitude and half-wavelength; MT axial force sign under end-loading.
validation_steps.protocol: Instantiate `ac/solid/microtubule.py::MicrotubuleCompartment` with `node_off=0` component-private arrays behind the `microtubule_rig.py` owner (its kernels have never been codegen'd — this is their first CUDA run). Compress one MT axially with prescribed end displacement; ramp the load; record the deflection amplitude and the axial force. Sweep seg 0.5 / 0.25 / 0.125 µm and L ∈ {3,5,8} µm.
validation_steps.pass_criterion: (1) Buckling threshold matches π²EI/L² (`ff/microtubule.euler_buckling_load`) with relative error ≤5% at seg 0.5 and DECREASING linearly in ℓ₀ (the ff Sanity Gate already established 5.0%→2.5%→1.3%); the 1/L² exponent recovered with slope −2.00 ± 0.10. (2) Below threshold the deflection amplitude is at the mesh-noise floor; above it, it grows. (3) An MT pushing on an obstacle registers a NEGATIVE (compressive) axial force — sign-sense.
validation_steps.negative_control: Raise EI ×100: no buckling at the same load and the MT must remain straight to the noise floor. Lower EI ×0.01: buckles at a proportionally lower load with slope 1.00 ± 0.10 in EI. Third: report a positive (tensile) axial force while the MT is being compressed — the sign-sense gate must FAIL.
validation_steps.est_effort: 2 dev-days (may be owned by the MT track — see dependencies)

validation_steps.step: N7 — IN SITU: nucleus inside membrane+cytosol with `mt_nucleus_linc` live — the connectedness gate, designed so failure cannot be missed
validation_steps.what_is_measured: Simultaneously and separately: (a) Σ|f| on the nucleus from the LINC channel alone; (b) the vector sum Σf on the nucleus from that channel; (c) nucleus centroid displacement; (d) nucleus DEFORMATION (per-face areal strain field and polar-height change) after removing best-fit rigid translation+rotation; (e) Newton-3rd closure Σf_filament + Σf_nucleus; (f) virtual-work closure f_socket·(Jδq) vs F_q·δq.
validation_steps.protocol: Build the in-situ column by extending the existing native interior-column slice (membrane → cortex → cytosol → nucleus in ONE `CellTransaction`, `interior_column_slice.py`, already runs natively) with: the MT owner from N6; a nuclear socket factory (face id + barycentrics from the live envelope topology); an MT segment `PortRef` factory (plus end = terminal segment with u=1); and one `LincJointPopulation` for `mt_nucleus_linc` with all joints in the BOUND state (kinetics BLOCKED and declared — see open questions). CRITICALLY, anchor the MT's far end: either `mt_cortex_capture` or a Dirichlet MTOC, so the MT is a strut between an anchored reaction and the nucleus. Apply a controlled directional load (prescribed MTOC/cortex-capture displacement). Converge the candidate, then evaluate all six observables in the same accepted step.
validation_steps.pass_criterion: (1) Σ|f_nucleus| from the LINC channel > 0 AND nucleus per-face areal strain field has a nonzero, spatially LOCALIZED signature at the socket faces (connectedness). (2) Newton-3rd: |Σf_filament + Σf_nucleus| / Σ|f| < 1e-10 (equal-and-opposite). (3) Virtual work closes to <1e-10 relative. (4) Sign-sense: an MT in compression pushes the envelope INWARD at its sockets; the nucleus centroid displaces along +Σf. (5) Connectedness and net translocation are reported as TWO SEPARATE verdicts and never combined into one number. (6) Rejected-step bit-exact restore of the nucleus surface, the tear flags, and the LINC binding SoA.
validation_steps.negative_control: PRIMARY (the PI's requirement): disable `mt_nucleus_linc` (all joints UNBOUND) at the identical MT load — the nucleus position array must be BIT-IDENTICAL to the unloaded state and the connector reaction must be exactly 0.0. This deliberately reproduces the historic 0.0 nm / bit-identical failure ON DEMAND; if we cannot reproduce it, the harness is not measuring the same thing and the gate is void. SECONDARY (proves the gate can fail): keep LINC bound but Dirichlet-pin every nucleus node — the displacement/deformation criterion must FAIL while the force criterion PASSES, showing the two observables are independent. TERTIARY (aliasing): alias the MT and nucleus position arrays — the pointer-identity assertion from N0 must FAIL before any force is assembled.
validation_steps.est_effort: 5–7 dev-days (the largest integration step: two port factories, the LINC caller, and the MT owner's first CUDA run)

validation_steps.step: N8 — Load-path attribution: which channel actually carries cortex/MT load to the nucleus (4-arm ablation), and the sum-to-zero discrimination
validation_steps.what_is_measured: Nucleus deformation and reaction under the SAME applied load across four arms — {LINC on/off} × {cytosol pressure coupling on/off} — plus the monopole/scalar ratio |Σf| / Σ|f| for a directional vs an isotropic MT configuration.
validation_steps.protocol: Four arms at one load: (i) LINC on, cytosol on; (ii) LINC off, cytosol on; (iii) LINC on, cytosol off; (iv) both off. Record the per-face strain field, volume, centroid displacement, and per-channel reaction in each. Separately run a symmetric isotropic MT aster with statistically identical capture on all sides at the same total Σ|f|, and compute |Σf|/Σ|f| and centroid displacement.
validation_steps.pass_criterion: (1) Arm (iv) produces EXACTLY zero nucleus reaction and bit-identical nucleus position — if it does not, an undeclared channel is loading the nucleus and the run HALTS to PI (this is the direct guard against the SettlingForce-class hidden-proxy confound). (2) Arm (ii) shows a near-uniform, volume-coupled compression signature with NO localized socket dent; arm (iii) shows a localized socket dent with a much smaller uniform component; the two signatures are distinguishable by the ratio of the strain field's localized-to-uniform decomposition. (3) Arm (i) reaction lies between and is bounded by (ii)+(iii) within the nonlinearity of the composite (reported, not thresholded). (4) Isotropic-aster run: |Σf|/Σ|f| ≈ 0 and centroid displacement at the noise floor WHILE Σ|f| > 0 and the per-face strain field is nonzero — and the report must classify this as CONNECTED-BUT-NET-ZERO, not as a connectedness failure. This is the exact distinction the crawl-traction failure missed.
validation_steps.negative_control: Take the isotropic-aster result and evaluate it with a single-scalar 'net force on nucleus' metric only: that metric must return ≈0 and would wrongly read as 'not connected' — the gate must demonstrate that its own scalar-only variant fails, forcing the two-verdict reporting. Second: in arm (iii) (cytosol off) verify the fluid boundary connectors dispatch nothing, so a residual nonzero uniform component would indicate the fluid channel is still live.

validation_steps.step: N9 — Grid-, parameter-, and seed-invariance of the transmission result
validation_steps.what_is_measured: The dimensionless transmission ratio T = (nucleus peak areal strain) / (applied MT-end strain), and the LINC-channel share of the total nucleus reaction, across discretizations and across the k_linc / LINC-density plane.
validation_steps.protocol: Repeat N7 at nucleus subdiv 3/4/5, MT seg 0.5/0.25, and 3 build seeds. Then sweep k_linc over ×{0.01,0.1,1,10,100} of its TEST value and LINC areal density (joints per µm² of envelope, which today is silently the vertex count — `linc_per_node=1`, the same defect as `erm_density_per_um2=None`) over a decade, reporting the dimensionless weld parameter W = (k_linc · N_linc) / k_lin_shell from N2.
validation_steps.pass_criterion: (1) T converges under refinement: |T(subdiv5) − T(subdiv4)| / T < 0.1, and the sign and the arm-ordering from N8 are unchanged at every refinement. (2) Across seeds the across-seed standard deviation of T is reported and the connectedness verdict is seed-independent (no verdict may rest on a within-realization SEM — the documented '+131 pN 16σ' failure). (3) The weld parameter W is reported for every run and any run with W ≫ 1 is labelled RIGID-WELD REGIME and cannot support a transmission claim. (4) LINC density is an explicit parameter in the run manifest, never an implicit function of mesh subdivision.
validation_steps.negative_control: Push k_linc to a value giving W ≫ 1: the nucleus must move rigidly with the MT (deformation share collapses, centroid share → 1) and the run must be auto-labelled RIGID-WELD rather than reported as strong transmission. Second: leave LINC density unset (the current default) and show the reported density changes with subdivision — the manifest gate must FAIL, exposing the mesh-knob defect.

validation_steps.step: N10 — NATIVE full-population role-by-ablation: what the cell gains from the nucleus, and reproducing the historic failure as the control
validation_steps.what_is_measured: Whole-cell indentation reaction F(strain) at the full native population, with and without the nucleus, and with and without the nucleus↔cytoskeleton connectors (LINC + MT), specifically BELOW the geometric contact strain 1 − R_nuc/R_cell.
validation_steps.protocol: At 70,686 filaments / 494,802 actin nodes with membrane, cytosol, monomer field and turgor at their setpoints, run four arms at matched numerics (identical probe stiffness, identical dt, identical step count — the documented 0.98 artifact came from letting these differ): (A) no nucleus; (B) nucleus, no LINC/MT; (C) nucleus + LINC + MT; (D) nucleus + LINC + MT, MT far end unanchored. Report ΔF/F vs strain for each arm relative to (A), plus the per-compartment displacement table (cortex / MT / nucleus mean |Δ| between rest and load) that the 2026-07-16 diagnosis used.
validation_steps.pass_criterion: (1) Arm (B) reproduces the historic result: below the geometric contact strain, cortex force is bit-identical to arm (A) (rel diff < 1e-14) and nucleus mean |Δ| = 0.0 nm. Reproducing this on demand is a PASS condition — it validates the harness. (2) Arm (C) BREAKS it: below the contact strain, ΔF/F is strictly nonzero and nucleus mean |Δ| is strictly nonzero, with a per-compartment displacement table in which no compartment is 0.0 nm. (3) Sign-sense: adding a load-bearing nucleus stiffens (ΔF ≥ 0), and the onset strain of nonzero ΔF in arm (C) is strictly BELOW the geometric contact strain (that is the whole point — sub-contact transmission). (4) Arm (D) shows a smaller |Σf| than (C) at the same Σ|f| (an unanchored strut cannot transmit net load) — the explicit sum-to-zero check at native scale. (5) Every quantitative ΔF value carries an explicit BLOCKED label.
validation_steps.negative_control: Arm (B) IS the negative control and must fail the transmission criterion while passing bit-identity. Additional: run arm (C) with matched numerics deliberately broken (different probe stiffness between arms) and show the ΔF becomes a flat multiplicative ratio across ALL strains — the fingerprint of a setup offset, which the gate must detect and reject (this is exactly how the historic 0.98 artifact was caught).

validation_steps.step: N11 — Visualization checkpoint (isolation + connector + cumulative) and the BLOCKED-labelled report
validation_steps.what_is_measured: That the physics is visually correct: strain localization, lamin-knee engagement region, chromatin link tensions, MT compression sign, LINC socket reactions, and the set of nodes that moved between rest and load.
validation_steps.protocol: Extend `ac/cell/dump_state.py` to emit chromatin links, indenter geometry, per-face areal strain, per-face rupture flags, MT axial force per segment, and per-joint LINC tension; extend `scripts/ac_viz_common.py` scenes accordingly (it is already data-driven for the nucleus mesh and LINC stubs, `:239-253`). Render one self-contained interactive WebGL HTML at FULL native resolution via `scripts/ac_cell_assembled_viz.py`, then verify in a real browser with `scripts/browser_check.py` (a grep of the HTML is not verification) and eyeball the screenshot.
validation_steps.pass_criterion: (1) Isolation scene: nucleus alone, envelope coloured by per-face areal strain with a discrete colour break at the lamin knee (shows WHERE lamin-A/C engages), chromatin links drawn and coloured by WLC tension, indenter drawn, and paired small-δ / large-δ scenes in which the far pole is visibly still in the first and visibly displaced in the second. Mean mesh edge length drawn to scale against the measured boundary-layer width so a reader can see whether it is resolved. (2) Connector scene: MT coloured by axial force SIGN (compression vs tension), LINC stubs coloured by tension, nucleus coloured by the LINC channel's contribution ONLY, with the LINC-OFF negative control rendered side by side so the 0.0 nm case is a visible scene and not just a number. (3) Cumulative composed render refreshed, plus a 'nodes that moved between rest and load' overlay in which no compartment is uniformly zero. (4) Browser-verified, no downsampling. (5) REPORT.md carries a BLOCKED status line on every quantitative claim and names the seven open PI GAPs.
validation_steps.negative_control: Render the arm-(B) (LINC/MT off) native run through the same pipeline: the 'nodes that moved' overlay must show the nucleus and MT blocks as empty — i.e. the visualization must be able to display the failure. If both arms look the same in the render, the viz is not diagnostic and the gate fails.
validation_steps.est_effort: 2–3 dev-days (dump on gbook, render + browser check on the Mac)

dependencies: Frozen-incumbent seam (Card 5 / the _accumulate_all omit-mask) must land FIRST. Until the driver can be told to skip its own nucleus accumulation (ac/cell/driver.py:157-158), binding an engine-owned nucleus double-counts every nucleus force. This is a PI-gated decision, not an implementation choice, and it blocks N0 and therefore everything after it.

A de-aliasing mechanism for component-private arrays. The nucleus, membrane and cortex all live in one global array (assemble.py:754) and the engine already contains the guard that rejects this (surface_body.py:349-353) — bypassed only because the facade is never constructed. Whichever track lands owner-private arrays for membrane/cortex should land the same mechanism for the nucleus; duplicating it three ways is how the guard gets bypassed again.

MT to CUDA_UNIT (step N6). The MT rig's kernels have never been codegen'd. If a separate MT/IF track owns that first CUDA run, Track 6 consumes it; if not, N6 is inside this track and adds ~2 days. Either way the in-situ gate (N7) cannot start before it.

Implicit-solver track for the nucleus tangents. The nucleus bending/areal/volume Hessians are in the regularizer, not in K_analytic (implicit_mechanics.py:1430-1446), which is why the nucleus block dominates the residual. If the solver track is adding tangents anyway, the nucleus tangents belong there; if not, NucleusImplicitCG must carry them. Cytosol/membrane interior-column track for the in-situ environment. The slice already runs natively, but its nucleus owner is a NoOpSurfaceMechanics over global arrays and the fluid connectors' force pass is deliberately not invoked. The in-situ gate needs real nucleus mechanics on private arrays plus the fluid boundaries actually dispatching, with an adjoint-work closure test that does not exist yet.

PI parameter decisions gate only MAGNITUDE, not any gate in this design. All eleven steps are exponent / conservation / symmetry / sign-sense / bit-identity / analytic-oracle-ratio gates, so the seven open I0-B2 GAPs (lamin split, eps_rupture, η_nucleoplasm, k_linc, oblate aspect, knee strain-measure, E_nuc method) block only the labelled quantitative claims. k_linc is the one that comes closest to being structural, because at large k_linc the tether becomes a rigid weld — handled explicitly by the N9 weld-parameter gate rather than by waiting for the value.
