validation_steps.what_is_measured: Three reductions over the projected residual PF, per run, at each seg_um rung: (1) IMPLIED DISPLACEMENT delta_i = |D_ii^-1 (PF)_i| in um, where D is the Jacobi diagonal WITHOUT the regularizer floor (a is a numerical device, not a stiffness); reported as max, count above reference, and the full distribution. (2) SIGNED COHERENT RADIAL BIAS S = sum_i (PF_i . rhat_i), and gamma_spur = S/(8 pi R), reported as the dimensionless ratio gamma_spur/gamma_target. (3) THERMAL CEILING ratio max_i |PF_i| / sqrt(kBT * D_ii). Plus the runtime's own computed bound F_pred = tolerance_um / dt_mu, replacing the frozen literal.
validation_steps.protocol: New device reductions in a diagnostics module; delta_i needs NO new physics — apply_preconditioner_kernel (implicit_mechanics.py:798-806) already computes D^-1 r, so this is a reduction over an array the solver builds every iteration. F_pred is read from the two fields already present in every report JSON (inner_tolerance_um, inner_dt_mu; derivation and 9/9 verification in docs/v2_audit/GATE_A_THRESHOLD_DERIVATION_2026-07-25.md + scripts/ac_gate_threshold_derivation.py). Run at seg_um {0.5, 0.2, 0.1} and PRINT the scaling exponents alongside the values. SCALING, stated explicitly because a per-node and a total gate behave oppositely under refinement: max|PF| is a force DENSITY x ell, so it scales as ell^+1 for extensive load and ell^-3 against a fixed geometric kink (measured ell^-2.845 over the fine rungs); sum_i|PF_i| scales as N*ell = total contour length, formally invariant but it double-counts cancelling residuals and is rejected; a MAX over N nodes additionally drifts upward with N by extreme-value statistics, so the max must never be replaced by a percentile (that would be gate-loosening) but must be reported with the count-above-reference and the distribution. delta_i = |PF_i|/D_ii is the grid-invariant one: for the dominant fixed-kink mode it equals (kappa*delta/ell^3)/(kappa/ell^3) = delta, returning the GEOMETRIC imperfection length independent of mesh, and for extensive load on a crosslink-held node it scales as ell^+1 (tightens under refinement). S/gamma_target contains neither N nor ell.
validation_steps.pass_criterion: Gate on the run's OWN computed bound: max|PF| / F_pred < 1 (this is a no-op at ell=0.5 um where F_pred=0.2107 vs the frozen 0.21, and a TIGHTENING at every finer mesh — it cannot loosen anything, and it eliminates the magic number). Report, and do not yet gate on, gamma_spur/gamma_target and the thermal ratio. The physical companion: max_i delta_i < delta_ref with delta_ref a length that cannot matter — 2.7 nm actin monomer rise (structural) or the mode-matched thermal x_th,i = sqrt(kBT/D_ii). NOTE HONESTLY: the mode-matched form is algebraically identical to |PF_i| <= sqrt(kBT*D_ii), which is LOOSER than 0.21 by x9.8 at a crossbridge node and x210 at an alpha-actinin node — so it may be adopted only as a CEILING ON WHAT MAY BE CLAIMED (a residual below it may not be called a physical non-equilibrium, only an unconverged athermal minimisation), never as a pass criterion. Choosing delta_ref is a PI decision, listed below.
validation_steps.negative_control: (1) Inject a deliberately wrong kmax (e.g. the filamin 8.2e5 instead of the WCA near-core 2.83e6) — F_pred must move to 0.0611 and the gate must FAIL; this exact control already exists as scripts/ac_gate_threshold_derivation.py --assume-kmax and was watched failing 4/9 checks. (2) Score the SAME committed fine-mesh runs against the frozen 0.21 and against F_pred(ell): the 0.2 um rung (max|PF| 0.21) must flip from PASS to FAIL by 2.49x and the 0.075 um rung from 'plateau' to FAIL by 108x — if it does not, the per-run computation is not wired. (3) Compute delta_i WITH the regularizer in the diagonal: soft modes get capped at |PF|/a and the field goes artificially flat — the gate must detect and reject that assembly.
validation_steps.est_effort: 1.5 dev-days (reductions are small; the rungs are the cost)

validation_steps.step: T2-5 — Cut-plane TRANSMITTED-force conservation with per-family decomposition (the load-path gate that catches sums-to-zero)
validation_steps.what_is_measured: For each of >= 20 planes at increasing distance from the load point: the summed axial force of every load-bearing element crossing the plane, sum over crossings of T * |uhat . nhat|, decomposed by family — actin backbone constraint tension, crosslink tension, WCA contact, bending — versus the applied load resolved on the same plane normal. Also: the per-filament net force at equilibrium (must be ~0), and the agreement between the TWO independent actin-tension extractions (the running-sum method already implemented, and the Lagrange multiplier lambda read straight out of the projector).
validation_steps.protocol: Reuse ac/cell/assembled_cortical_stress.actin_axial_tension (:42) and crosslink_tension (:78) and the plane math in ff/gamma_estimator.method_of_planes_gamma (:61) via ac/cell/cortical_tension.py — but sweep the plane POSITION instead of averaging over diametral planes, so the output is a transmitted-force profile T(s), not a single gamma. Add a readout kernel for rhs_lambda_work from ac/cell/inner_mechanics.project_constraint_forces_kernel (segment tension = 2*lambda_k*|g_k|) and cross-check it against the running-sum extraction. Run under the T2-2/T2-3 point load and, separately, under a purely isotropic radial load.
validation_steps.pass_criterion: (a) EQUILIBRIUM/CONSERVATION: |sum_crossing - F_applied| / F_applied <= the achieved residual tolerance, for every plane between the load and the support — a conservation identity, no magnitude. (b) COMPLETENESS: the family decomposition must sum to the total with zero remainder, and removing any single family must break (a) by that family's share — proving nothing is missing and nothing double-counted. (c) CROSS-METHOD: the Lagrange-multiplier and running-sum actin tensions must agree to solver tolerance (two independent measurements of the same physical quantity). (d) per-filament net force ~ 0 at equilibrium.
validation_steps.negative_control: (1) The measured crawl failure reproduced deliberately: apply an ISOTROPIC radial load. F_applied is then 0 and sum_crossing must also be 0 on every plane while individual element tensions are large — the artifact must be visible and labelled, not read as a load path. (2) Omit the crosslink family from the crossing sum: (a) must fail by exactly the crosslink share. (3) Include the backbone Lagrange tension in a raw |F| metric as well (the historical metric bug) and show it inflates the answer — the gate reports the projected quantity only.

validation_steps.step: T2-6 — Nonlinear indentation: F(delta) exponent, crossover, and unload reversibility / energy balance
validation_steps.what_is_measured: Quasi-static force-displacement curve for a normal indenter on the cortex: log-log slope d(log F)/d(log delta) in the small-delta regime and beyond; the crossover indentation delta_c; the loading/unloading hysteresis area; and the energy balance W_ext (integral of reaction force over indenter displacement) versus the change in stored elastic energy Delta U.
validation_steps.protocol: Add an external-probe instrument (see new_code_needed) with adjoint reaction accounting: the probe scatters -f onto the cortex and accumulates +f as the measured reaction, so F(delta) is a Newton-third-law bookkeeping quantity rather than a re-derived guess. Ramp delta in small increments, converge each increment with the existing inner solve (make_inner_solve, inner_solver='analytic_implicit'), then unload along the same increments. Compare shape only against validation/oracles/mechanics/thin_shell.reissner_point_stiffness (F = k0*delta, linear) and the Pogorelov mirror-buckling softening beyond delta ~ h; use validation/oracles/mechanics/hertz.valid_small_strain for regime validity. CONVERT UNITS EXPLICITLY: the oracle is SI (Pa, m, N/m), the engine is pN/um (1 pN/um^2 = 1 Pa exactly) — the DCM-meters vs FF-microns 1e6 slip has bitten this project twice.
validation_steps.pass_criterion: (a) EXPONENT: log-log slope = 1.00 +/- 0.15 in the Reissner regime delta << h — a dimensionless exponent, no modulus needed. (b) CROSSOVER: a single monotone softening of the exponent begins at delta_c, and delta_c/h is of order 1; report delta_c/h rather than delta_c. (c) REVERSIBILITY/CONSERVATION: with no dissipative element declared in the static solve, the unload must retrace the load curve and the hysteresis area must be <= the accumulated solver residual work; and W_ext must equal Delta U to the same tolerance. (d) SIGN SENSE: inward load gives inward deflection, outward gives outward (the existing S2 sign-reversal check, ported to the ac cortex). No absolute modulus is compared to literature; the modulus is REPORTED as BLOCKED.
validation_steps.negative_control: (1) Adjointness: scatter the probe force one-sided (onto the cortex but do not accumulate the reaction, or vice versa) — the W_ext = Delta U balance must FAIL. This is the direct analogue of the crawl failure where the only polarised channel dumped its reaction on the movable matrix. (2) Turn on a lumped body-force proxy at the historical SettlingForce magnitude (1e4-5e4x real buoyant weight, which was ON in every committed spreading run and mislabelled proxy_off): the F(delta) curve must be visibly offset/exponent-corrupted and the gate must FAIL — a regression test against the exact confound the old gates locked in. (3) Run with 2 nodes carrying the entire load (crosslinks deleted): the exponent must leave the Reissner band.
validation_steps.est_effort: 3 dev-days (probe instrument + ramp + unload + oracle plumbing)

validation_steps.step: T2-7 — Cross-component transmission audit (the gate that would have caught MT 0.0 nm / nucleus 0.0 nm)
validation_steps.what_is_measured: Under the identical probe, per-COMPONENT displacement statistics (n, mean|u|, max|u|, and an exact-zero flag) for every component present in the build; and for each declared connector, the transmitted force as an adjoint PAIR (sum of the two endpoint scatters must be equal and opposite) plus the ratio max|u| on the far side to max|u| on the near side.
validation_steps.protocol: Port the pattern of scripts/ff_internal_displacement_diag.py from the ff engine to the ac build. Take the composed build (cortex + membrane + nucleus, adding MT/IF when those components land), apply the probe, and classify each component into one of three verdicts: MOVED (max|u| > sqrt(eps64)*ell), FROZEN (max|u| == 0.0 exactly, i.e. bit-identical rest vs load), or SUB-RESOLUTION. Cross-tabulate the verdict against the connector graph: a component with a declared force-real connector to a loaded component must be MOVED; a component with NO connector must be FROZEN. Reuse ac/cell/preload_force_probe._node_family (:42) for population blocks and ac/engine/contracts.reference_cell_architecture() for the declared edges.
validation_steps.pass_criterion: For EVERY component: verdict == the graph's prediction. Concretely, zero components are simultaneously (a) connected in the declared graph to a loaded component and (b) FROZEN. Every declared force-real connector reports an adjoint pair summing to zero within round-off, and a non-zero transmitted force. Any FROZEN component is reported by name with its node count and its declared connectors — the failure must be named in the artifact, not averaged away. Pure sign/zero/adjointness logic, no magnitude.
validation_steps.negative_control: Reproduce the exact 2026-07-16 failure: merge the MT aster and nucleus nodes into cell.pos_d/cell.f_d WITHOUT registering their connectors, load the cortex, and confirm the gate reports MT and nucleus as FROZEN (0.0 nm, bit-identical) and FAILS — the same configuration that previously passed as 'coupled because co-located'. Positive control: a hand-built two-node connector double must be reported MOVED with an exactly adjoint pair. Second negative control: keep the connector registered but scatter only one side; the adjoint-pair limb must FAIL while the displacement limb still passes.

validation_steps.step: T2-8 — Load-path visualisation: isolation + cumulative, browser-verified
validation_steps.what_is_measured: Nothing new numerically; this is the mandated checkpoint that renders the T2-2..T2-7 fields so a wrong-sign / hotspot / interpenetration / frozen-component bug is visible. Fields rendered: |u| under the probe with the load point and the lambda isoline; per-node implied displacement delta_i; per-node von Mises sigma_vm from the COMPLETE family set; per-SEGMENT axial tension drawn on the segments; crosslinks drawn as explicit bonds coloured by tension; the T(s) cut-plane profile as an inset.
validation_steps.protocol: Extend scripts/ac_viz_common.build_scenes (:379) with the new data-driven scenes (it auto-generates a scene per component/connector family present in the dump, so the new arrays only need to be in the dump). Fix the stress denominator first: node_vol for cortical nodes must come from the SHELL volume 4*pi*R^2*h/n_actin, not cell_vol/n_actin (assemble.py:931-933) — otherwise sigma_vm is ~12x low. Export kxl_d, r0xl_d, node_vol, segment lambda and the probe reaction in dump_state.py. Render on the dev Mac (numpy/matplotlib, no CUDA), full native resolution, NO downsampling, one self-contained HTML; verify with scripts/browser_check.py AND look at the screenshot.
validation_steps.pass_criterion: browser_check.py exits 0 (non-blank frame, no uncaught JS) for both the isolation and the cumulative scene sets, AND a human confirms in the screenshot: the stressed set forms a CONNECTED backbone of segments from the load point outward (not isolated hot nodes), the displacement field is a smooth decaying patch (not a single spike and not a uniform translation), signs are correct (inward load -> inward dimple), and any FROZEN component from T2-7 is rendered in the explicit 'did not move' colour. Every absolute stress/modulus value in the caption carries an explicit BLOCKED label.
validation_steps.negative_control: Grep the HTML instead of rendering it — that is exactly what missed the silently dead viewer in 2026-07-08 and is not verification. Also render the crosslink-deleted build: the stress backbone must visibly fall apart into per-filament stripes, and the composed scene with an unregistered MT population must visibly show it grey/frozen. If the deliberately broken build looks the same as the good one, the scene is not showing what its caption says.
validation_steps.est_effort: 1.5 dev-days (render on Mac; the dump comes from the native runs above)

validation_steps.step: T2-9 — Turn the gates into the correctness fixture for the speed program
validation_steps.what_is_measured: Wall time and iteration counts for the incumbent solver versus (a) cg_check_every > 0 and (b) mg_assembled_coarse=True, both currently default-off pending exactly this native A/B; measured on the T2-2/T2-3/T2-6 fixtures rather than on a bespoke benchmark. Simultaneously: whether each speed lever preserves the exact invariants the gates measure.
validation_steps.protocol: Run the T2-2 reciprocity solve and the T2-6 indentation ramp at native population with each lever off, on, and both on, on the A5000. For cg_check_every, diff the returned dx bitwise. For mg_assembled_coarse (which changes the preconditioner, so bit-identity is NOT expected), compare the reciprocity residual, lambda, the exponent, the cut-plane conservation error, and the energy balance.
validation_steps.pass_criterion: cg_check_every: dx BIT-IDENTICAL to the incumbent (its own docstring claims this; verify, do not assume) with a measured speedup. mg_assembled_coarse: every T2-2..T2-6 pass_criterion still met, and the reciprocity residual and cut-plane conservation error no worse than the incumbent's — i.e. a preconditioner may change the path but must not change an exact invariant. Report the speedup as measured, not as the remembered ~40x.
validation_steps.negative_control: Deliberately break the assembled coarse operator (e.g. use a non-symmetric restriction/prolongation pair) — reciprocity and the energy balance must FAIL while the wall time still improves. This is the point: a speedup that breaks an exact invariant must be caught by the gates, and if it is not, the gates are not load-bearing.

Nothing may claim a rung without this artifact.

observables_missing: Per-node IMPLIED DISPLACEMENT delta_i = |PF_i| / D_ii — the physically meaningful replacement for max|PF|. The array is already computed every CG iteration (apply_preconditioner_kernel); no reduction, no report, no gate exists.

SIGNED coherent radial residual S = sum_i (PF_i . rhat_i) and gamma_spur = S/(8 pi R) — specified in GATE_A_THRESHOLD_DERIVATION §6.4 as the only grid-invariant candidate tied to the observable, and explicitly noted as computed in NO committed artifact.
Per-run F_pred = tolerance_um / dt_mu — the two inputs are in every report JSON but the ratio is never formed; instead 54 hand-copied 0.21 literals in 22 files stand in for it.
Per-segment actin axial tension from the inextensibility multiplier — lambda exists on device in rhs_lambda_work and is thrown away every iteration.

GEODESIC (on-network) distance from a load node. Without it the decay profile is binned by Euclidean distance, which mixes nodes that are mechanically far apart across the shell.

Absolute connected-component count and crosslink degree distribution ON THE BUILT CELL. Only an ad-hoc 2026-07-23 audit script and a synthetic prototype exist; the fixes were never turned into a standing gate.
Rigid-body-mode amplitude of a displacement field (and its removal). Without it a uniform drift reads as long-range load sharing.
External-work / reaction-force ledger for an applied load, so W_ext vs Delta U can be checked at all. There is currently no applied load in ac to have a reaction for.
Per-component displacement classification with an EXACT-ZERO flag (bit-identical rest vs load) cross-checked against the declared connector graph.
Correct cortical-shell node volume for the virial denominator (today cell_vol/n_actin, ~12x too large for a 0.2 um shell).
Reissner boundary-layer LENGTH oracle (only the point stiffness is in thin_shell.py) — the modulus-free geometric prediction the decay-length gate compares against.

connectors_involved: NONE newly force-real by Track 2's core content, stated honestly: intra-cortex load sharing is a COMPONENT-internal property (the cortex's own segments, crosslinks and steric contacts), not a connector. Claiming a connector here would be exactly the overclaim the 2026-07-25 audit flagged.

The probe/indenter is NOT one of the 32. It is best expressed as a world_boundary-owned contact on the cortex; whether it is registered as a 33rd connector (probe_cortex_contact, world_boundary<->cortex) or kept as an out-of-graph instrument is a PI decision (below). Either way its reaction accounting is bidirectional+adjoint, so it is built to connector standard.

T2-6/T2-7 press a probe through the membrane onto the cortex and check the adjoint pair and the transmitted force, which is the first test of the ERM path as a LOAD PATH rather than as an existing force.

nmii_cortex_motor (MOTOR) — force-real today; Track 2 runs myosin OFF for the isolation gates and provides the passive baseline the motor's emergent tension is measured ON TOP OF. Its aliasing (actuator and port are both cell.pos_d/cell.f_d) is exactly what T2-7's exact-zero/adjoint-pair audit is designed to expose.
surface_porous_transfer (cortex<->cytosol) — exercised, and its FROZEN/MOVED verdict measured, when with_pressure=True; today its being a real load path is untested.

mt_cortex_capture, actin_cap_linc, mt_nucleus_linc, if_nucleus_linc, nucleus_cytosol_boundary — T2-7 does not make these force-real; it NAMES which of them are dead. That is the deliverable: the audit that would have caught MT 0.0 nm / nucleus 0.0 nm before it was reported as coupling.
dependencies: MOSTLY INDEPENDENT and safe to start first: T2-0 through T2-6 need only the cortex, which is buildable standalone today (with_membrane/with_nucleus/with_pressure/with_myosin=False). T2-1 needs no GPU at all. This makes Track 2 the natural lead track under the new PI priority (prove one compartment actually works, standalone, first).

T2-7 (cross-component transmission audit) DEPENDS on at least one other component's isolation gate landing — there must be something to transmit into. It is worth running early anyway with membrane+nucleus only, because its value is naming the dead paths, and it gets strictly more valuable as MT/IF/SF tracks land.

The fine seg_um rungs (0.1, 0.075) of T2-3 and T2-4 DEPEND on the solver/multigrid track (ac/cell/fiber_arclength_mg.py, mg_assembled_coarse): CORTEX_MESH_FIDELITY §9 measured that 75 nm does not converge on one A5000 (weak plateaus 3.46-4.4, strong OOMs at 2.9 M nodes, fq-coarse too slow). Mitigation that removes most of this dependency: the LINEAR-response gates (T2-2, T2-3) do not require a converged resting state, only a tangent at a defined configuration, so they can run at fine mesh now; only the NONLINEAR indentation gate T2-6 needs convergence and is therefore capped at ~200 nm until multigrid lands.

T2-4 DEPENDS on PI ratifying G1 (compute the route-c bound per run instead of the frozen 0.21). Without it the grid-invariance rungs cannot be scored — the frozen literal is 2.49x loose at 0.2 um and 6.64x loose at 0.075 um, so a refinement series scored against it silently passes runs that fail the runtime's own criterion.

The PI's stated baseline (adherent on 2D collagen-coated ECM) DEPENDS on the ECM + focal-adhesion tracks. Track 2's oracle comparison (Reissner point load on a free spherical shell) is only valid for the free-floating-in-media configuration; on an adherent cell the boundary conditions and the analytic oracle both change. Recommendation: run Track 2 first in the free-sphere configuration where the oracle is exact, then re-run the same gates on the adherent state once ECM/FA land, and report both.
T2-9 (speed A/B) DEPENDS on T2-2..T2-6 existing, since it uses them as the correctness fixture. Doing it earlier means optimising against no invariant.

Making the cortex a genuine engine COMPONENT (not an aliased port) depends on the engine de-aliasing work (INTEGRATION_surface_body.md steps + the Card-5 omit-mask). Track 2 does not require it, but T2-7's adjoint-pair limb will keep reporting the aliasing until it lands.

risks: LOAD PATH THAT SUMS TO ZERO — the exact crawl failure. A radially symmetric probe, or measuring the NET force on the cortex instead of the TRANSMITTED force across cut planes, gives zero by symmetry while every element is loaded. ac/cell/cortical_tension.py already documents the ~1015x self-cancellation of the naive radial sum. Mitigation: self-equilibrated dipole loads, and T2-5 measures sum over plane crossings of T*|uhat.nhat| versus the applied load, per plane, per family — never a net vector sum.

THE REGULARIZER IS A SPRING TO GROUND. The operator is (aI + PKP); a is a per-node stiffness with no bond behind it, so it screens the response and sets a spurious decay length. For a cortex-only build a = sqrt(eps64)*kmax ~ 0.042 pN/um, only ~14x below the softest real mode (bending kappa/ell^3 = 0.582 pN/um) — a ~7% contamination of exactly the mode the decay length lives in. Mitigation: mandatory a, a/10, a/100 sweep with an invariance requirement; the result is VOID if lambda tracks a. Note a cannot simply be set to 0 — it is what makes the operator SPD against the 6 rigid modes, which is why the loads must instead be self-equilibrated.

STERIC CONTACT FAKING A CROSSLINKED NETWORK. WCA excluded volume transmits compression between filaments that merely touch. A fragmented network can therefore still 'share load' under an indenter — proximity-mediated coupling that looks like a network. Mitigation: the crosslinks-off / steric-off ablation is a required arm of T2-2/T2-3, and T2-5 attributes the transmitted force by family.

RECIPROCITY PASSES TRIVIALLY ON A DECOUPLED SYSTEM. The 2026 co-location failure (block-diagonal stiffness) is symmetric — 0 == 0 satisfies Betti perfectly. A reciprocity-only gate would have PASSED the exact build where MT and nucleus moved 0.0 nm. Mitigation: symmetry and non-trivial transmission are one inseparable two-limb criterion, and the crosslink-deleted negative control is designed to make the trap visible on the real build.

RIGID DRIFT READ AS LONG-RANGE TRANSMISSION. A uniform translation gives every node the same |u|, which looks like perfect load sharing and an infinite decay length. Mitigation: project the 6 rigid modes out before measuring and REPORT the removed amplitude; T2-3's negative control is to show the un-projected field failing.

THE BACKBONE IS NOT A SPRING. Actin in ac is an inextensible Lagrange rod; there is no k(L-r0) backbone term. ff/ff_virial_stress.py handles only Hookean bonds and constant myosin and explicitly excludes bending, so wiring it unmodified would silently omit the dominant tension carrier. Separately, raw |F| that includes the Lagrange constraint force was already a metric bug in this project. Mitigation: extend the virial with the multiplier-derived segment tension, and measure PROJECTED forces consistently everywhere.

STRESS DENOMINATOR OFF BY ~12x. ac/cell/assemble.py:931-933 sets node_vol = cell_vol/n_actin (whole-cell volume) for cortical nodes in a ~0.2 um shell. Any sigma_vm in Pa is ~12x low. Mitigation: shell-derived node volume, and BLOCKED labels on absolute stress regardless.

UNIT SLIP. The Reissner/Hertz oracles are SI (Pa, m, N/m); the engine is um/pN (1 pN/um^2 = 1 Pa exactly, but lengths are not). This project has already eaten two 1e6 unit slips (DCM meters vs FF microns). Mitigation: an explicit exponent-tuple dimensional check in the gate script, like the one in scripts/ac_gate_threshold_derivation.py.

SCORING A REFINEMENT SERIES AGAINST THE FROZEN 0.21. The literal is 2.49x loose at 0.2 um and 6.64x loose at 0.075 um; two rungs of the existing fine-mesh series are re-opened by arithmetic alone. Running T2-3/T2-4 without G1 would repeat the error at higher confidence.

A MAX-BASED GATE DRIFTING WITH N. max_i |PF_i| over 494,802 nodes and over 2,898,126 nodes are not the same statistic even at identical physics (extreme-value growth), on top of the ell^-2.845 measured family scaling. Mitigation: normalise per-node by the local stiffness (delta_i) and report the distribution and count-above-reference — but never substitute a percentile for the max, which would be gate-loosening.

THE BUILD ARTIFACT MASQUERADING AS PHYSICS. cortex_overlap_mode='transverse' (the committed default) knocks nodes off their great-circle arc, creating a bending kink whose force blows up x288 at 75 nm (assemble.py:255-259); the measured ell^-2.845 residual scaling is the fixed-kink signature. Under a point load these kinks will appear as stress hotspots that look exactly like load concentration. Mitigation: run the refinement rungs in 'radial_span' and report both arms.

CONCLUDING FROM A STRIPPED CONFIGURATION. This project has been contradicted natively six times after reasoning from coarse or stripped runs. The cortex-only isolation build IS a stripped configuration by design. Mitigation: label every isolation result as isolation-scope, and re-run T2-2/T2-3/T2-6 on the composed build before any statement about the cell; never let an isolation number stand in for a composed one.

A GATE A BROKEN BUILD CANNOT FAIL. The precedent is the largest-vs-second-largest fragment test that a fragmented cortex passed. T2-0 must gate on n_components == 1 absolutely; any ratio or comparative formulation reintroduces the hole.

NONLINEAR HYSTERESIS FROM SOLVER TOLERANCE, NOT PHYSICS. The load/unload retrace check will show hysteresis simply because each increment converges only to tolerance. Mitigation: the pass criterion is hysteresis area <= accumulated solver residual work, computed per run, not a chosen number — and the tolerance itself must come from G1, not the literal.

AN EXPLICIT UNKNOWN: whether the current cortex can pass ANY of these gates. Nothing above CUDA_UNIT exists, cortex is a SEAMED-with-aliasing port, and the structure audit's 5 defects have only partially been re-measured. A first-run FAIL on T2-0 or T2-2 is a plausible outcome and should be treated as the deliverable, not as a setback.
open_questions_for_pi: RATIFY G1: replace the 54 hand-copied 0.21 pN literals with the run's own F_pred = inner_tolerance_um / inner_dt_mu, and report max|PF|/F_pred as a dimensionless ratio. It is a no-op at ell=0.5 um and a strict TIGHTENING at every finer mesh, so it cannot loosen anything — but it is still a gate-contract change and it re-opens the 0.2 um and 0.075 um rungs. T2-3/T2-4 cannot be scored without it.

CHOOSE delta_ref for the implied-displacement companion gate max_i |PF_i|/D_ii < delta_ref: (a) 2.7 nm actin monomer rise (structural resolution — tight on soft bending modes, loose on crosslinked nodes), (b) the mode-matched thermal x_th,i = sqrt(kBT/D_ii), which is algebraically identical to |PF_i| <= sqrt(kBT*D_ii) and is x9.8 to x210 LOOSER than 0.21, so it may only be a claim ceiling and never a pass, (c) a fixed reporting precision such as 1 nm. Also: gate on the max, or on the count of nodes above delta_ref? I recommend (a) as the pass with (b) reported as the claim ceiling, but the choice re-allocates strictness across modes and is a contract change.

IS THE INDENTER A 33rd CONNECTOR OR AN INSTRUMENT? Options: (a) register probe_cortex_contact (world_boundary<->cortex) in reference_cell_architecture(), which lets the track claim a connector force-real and forces the probe to meet full connector standard; (b) keep it an out-of-graph diagnostic instrument with adjoint reaction accounting, claiming no connector. I lean (b) for honesty, but (a) is defensible since an AFM tip is a real mechanical boundary.

MAY THE FROZEN ac/cell/driver.py:141-167 _accumulate_all TAKE ONE ADDITIVE PROBE HOOK (default None, bit-identical when absent) as instrumentation, or must the applied load go entirely through the ac/engine driver seam / Card-5 omit-mask? The linear-response gates need no hook at all; only the nonlinear indentation gate does.

INDENTER PROTOCOL for the shape gate: sharp point (Reissner, cleanest oracle), spherical bead of stated radius (matches AFM practice and the existing Hertz harness), or the PI's own tip geometry. And ramp rate / quasi-static increment size — the S2 saturation trace suggests creep is possible, and 'is it an elastic equilibrium or still creeping' changes what the curve means.

BASELINE CONFIGURATION for Track 2's first run: free spherical cell in media (where the Reissner oracle is exact and the geometry is clean) or already adherent on 2D collagen (the PI's stated baseline, where the oracle no longer applies and ECM/FA must land first)? I recommend free-sphere first for the oracle, then re-run identically on the adherent state — but that is two runs of everything.

IS CORTEX THICKNESS h A BUILD KNOB? The modulus-free decay-length prediction is sqrt(R*h), so the strongest form of the T2-3 oracle gate is 'lambda scales as sqrt(h)'. That needs h exposed and varied. Today the ~0.2 um shell is a byproduct of overlap_free_cortex, not a parameter.

SWITCH cortex_overlap_mode TO 'radial_span' FOR THE REFINEMENT RUNGS? It avoids the great-circle kink that dominates the fine-mesh residual (x288 at 75 nm) but it changes the committed byte-identical build, so the coarse baseline would no longer reproduce bit-for-bit.

SEG_UM RUNGS: accept {0.5, 0.2} now as the grid-invariance evidence and defer {0.1, 0.075} until the multigrid lands, or block the grid-invariance gate entirely until the fine mesh converges? Note the LINEAR-response limbs can run fine-mesh today; only the nonlinear indentation cannot.

MAY mg_assembled_coarse BECOME DEFAULT if T2-9 shows every gate invariant preserved? cg_check_every is bit-identical so it is an easy yes; mg_assembled_coarse changes the preconditioner and so changes numbers within tolerance, which is a different kind of decision.

WHAT IS THE PASS/FAIL POLICY IF T2-0 FAILS on the current default build (a real possibility — the 5 structural defects were only partly re-measured)? Specifically: halt Track 2 and reopen the cortex reconstruction lane, or proceed with the gates on a knowingly-imperfect network while labelling every downstream result?

The decay criterion must then FAIL (sustained non-zero reaction), which is exactly the fake-load-path signature this gate exists to detect. Also `--nc mask-none` (both groups) must reproduce M1 bit-identically, proving the mask itself injects no physics.

validation_steps.step: M3 — FREE pair: the abscissa->shortening identity (the direct answer to 'does the motor move one filament relative to another')
validation_steps.what_is_measured: Per accepted step, with NO anchor anywhere: (a) sarcomere shortening = decrease in the barbed-end-to-barbed-end distance of the two filaments; (b) the sum of the two head groups' mean abscissa advance over that step; (c) the system centroid; (d) the partition of the sliding between filament A and filament B when their node counts (hence their pseudo-drag) are made unequal.
validation_steps.protocol: Same single-pair build with the FA pins removed. At converged equilibrium of a free chain there is nothing to resist the motor, so every crossbridge tension must relax to zero and the geometric shortening must equal exactly the accumulated power stroke. Measure over 20+ accepted steps, several seeds. Repeat with n_per_fiber unequal between A and B to change the relative mobility.
validation_steps.pass_criterion: (a) == (b): per-step shortening equals the summed mean abscissa advance to <= 1e-6 relative (this is a measured-vs-measured IDENTITY, no literature magnitude enters). (b) residual crossbridge tension at convergence <= 1e-9 * k_xb * mean abscissa. (c) system centroid drift == 0 to 1e-12 per step (no self-propulsion of an isolated dipole). (d) the A:B slide ratio equals the inverse ratio of their node counts to 1e-6 (overdamped uniform per-node mobility) — a scaling gate, no constant needed. (e) shortening direction: barbed ends approach, i.e. sliding is barbed-ward for each head — sign-sense.
validation_steps.negative_control: `--nc freeze-abscissa` (v0 = 0): shortening must be EXACTLY 0. If the pair still shortens, the motion is a placement/passive artifact, not the motor — this is the control that would have caught the SettlingForce class of confound. `--nc flip-polarity`: (e) must FAIL — the pair must LENGTHEN. `--nc one-node-pinned`: (c) must FAIL (centroid drifts), proving the momentum check can fail.

validation_steps.step: M4 — load-clamp sweep: recover the ensemble force-velocity SHAPE and the duty-vs-load non-monotonicity
validation_steps.what_is_measured: Steady sliding velocity per accepted step and steady bound fraction, as a function of an imposed external compliance: one linear spring of stiffness k_ext from each barbed end to a fixed ground, swept over >= 4 decades from free (k_ext -> 0) to clamped (k_ext -> stiff). Also the per-head Hill velocity ratio v/v0 and the bound-target-lifetime distribution.
validation_steps.protocol: Add an explicit external-spring boundary (declared as a MEASUREMENT FIXTURE, not biology, and named as such in the artifact) to the single-pair driver. For each k_ext, run to a steady bound population, average over the settled window and over seeds. Plot v/v0 against F/F_stall_ensemble where F_stall_ensemble is the measured load at which sliding stops. Cross-check the curve against `hill_fv_analytic.hill_velocity` and `ensemble_stall_analytic.ensemble_stall_meanfield` evaluated with the SAME GAP constants — a code-correctness cross-check, never a physiology claim (project rule: oracle = cross-check, not truth).
validation_steps.pass_criterion: (1) v(F) is strictly monotone decreasing across the sweep (rank correlation = -1). (2) LIMITS, which are exact: v/v0 -> 1.000 +/- 0.01 as k_ext -> 0, and v/v0 -> 0 (<= 1e-3) at the stiff end. (3) Normalised curve COLLAPSE: the (F/F_stall_ens, v/v0) points from all decades fall on one curve to within the seed-ensemble SEM, and the curve is convex with the sign of curvature set by kappa (compare the measured curvature sign against the analytic Hill kappa branch — sign only). (4) Duty vs load is NON-monotonic with a single interior maximum, and the measured peak load agrees with `catch_slip_peak_force(k_catch0,x_catch,k_slip0,x_slip,kT)` computed from the same constants to within the ensemble SEM. (5) The absolute stall force vs the mean-field oracle is REPORTED with status BLOCKED and its discrepancy attributed (series compliance + load sharing), never used as a PASS/FAIL — this is exactly the check that made NG-1 read 4/6 at L_p = 0.13 um.
validation_steps.negative_control: `--nc detach-slip-only`: switch the detach law to pure Bell slip; criterion (4) must FAIL (duty becomes monotone decreasing, no interior peak). `--nc kappa-linear` (kappa -> 1e6): the curvature-sign check in (3) must FAIL to distinguish Hill from the linear-stall law — this proves the shape gate is actually sensitive to the mechanism the hard rule demands.

validation_steps.step: M5 — the convergence discriminator: dense host equilibrium oracle for the FROZEN-KMC state
validation_steps.what_is_measured: The device converged positions vs the exact equilibrium of the same frozen-KMC linear system solved densely on the host.
validation_steps.protocol: With the KMC binding state and walk_dir frozen (which is precisely the state the inner solve sees), the r0bind crossbridge force is EXACTLY linear in position (rank-one k_xb*w w^T per head, `implicit_mechanics.py:336-343`), and the SF axial links are linear Hookean, so the whole single-pair inner problem is a linear SPD system of only a few hundred DOF once the Dirichlet rows are eliminated (the angle-harmonics are the only nonlinear terms; run the oracle both with them linearised at the current configuration and with them disabled, and report both). Assemble that matrix in NumPy on the host, solve directly, and compare node-by-node with the device solve. This replaces the uninformative residual/T ratio with an absolute answer.
validation_steps.pass_criterion: max nodal position difference between the device solve and the host dense solve <= 1e-8 um relative to the sarcomere overlap length, and the resulting transmitted anchor reaction agrees to 1e-6 relative. Additionally: the device answer must be INVARIANT to solver path — explicit relax (long budget) and `sf_implicit.SFImplicitCG` must agree to the same tolerance, and the implicit answer must be invariant to the mobility scale `--implicit-step-scale` over 2 decades (a convergence-rate knob must not move the equilibrium).
validation_steps.negative_control: `--nc relax-1` (one relaxation iteration): the agreement criterion must FAIL by orders of magnitude — a convergence gate nobody has watched fail is not a gate. `--nc wrong-tangent` (isotropic instead of rank-one): the implicit path must then either fail to converge or converge to a state that DISAGREES with the host dense oracle built from the true force, proving the oracle discriminates operator errors.

validation_steps.step: M6 — the abscissa/slide decomposition and the energy ledger (what abscissa can and cannot tell you)
validation_steps.what_is_measured: Per bound head, the EXACT identity slide_h = loads_hill[h]/k_xb - abscissa[h] (from the r0bind definition; needs no new device array, only a readback). Reported as two population sums: total accumulated power stroke A = sum(abscissa) and total mechanical yield S = -sum(slide), plus the dimensionless realisation fraction rho = S/A in [0,1]. Plus a work-energy ledger per accepted step: motor work W = sum(F_h * delta_abscissa_h) accumulated AT COMMIT TIME BEFORE the detach reset; elastic potential U computed by an INDEPENDENT potential-energy evaluator over every bond/angle/crossbridge family (not from the force kernels' own increments); dissipation D = sum over inner iterations of F . dx measured along the ACTUAL displacement path. Closure error e = |W - (dU + D)| / W.
validation_steps.protocol: Add a device accumulator for lifetime abscissa and per-step delta-abscissa that is incremented in the commit kernel before the detach reset, plus a host-side independent potential-energy function and a dissipation accumulator inside both inner-solve paths. Run on the M1 (clamped) and M3 (free) configurations and contrast. WHAT THIS DISTINGUISHES: (a) regime — clamped gives delta-abscissa/(tau*v0) -> 0 (abscissa plateaus, tension sustained, rho -> 0), free gives delta-abscissa/(tau*v0) -> 1 (abscissa runs at the unloaded rate, tension ~ 0, rho -> 1); the two limits are opposite and neither needs a force magnitude. (b) whether a collapsed tension is PHYSICAL yielding or a SOLVER artifact — if the fiber genuinely yielded, the work went into D and the ledger closes; if the solver is wrong, W - dU - D does not close. WHAT IT CANNOT DO: rho -> 0 is identical for 'truly rigid boundary' and 'unconverged relax', so the decomposition alone can never certify convergence — it must be paired with M5's independent equilibrium oracle or with the clamped/free boundary contrast. It also cannot detect an error that is itself energy-consistent (e.g. a correct-magnitude force applied along a wrong direction), and it says nothing about the spatial distribution of the residual.
validation_steps.pass_criterion: (1) The identity slide_h = loads_hill/k_xb - abscissa holds to 1e-12 for every bound head (it is a definition; a violation means the load kernel and the crossbridge kernel disagree). (2) Ledger closure e <= 1e-3 on the CONVERGED configuration, for BOTH the clamped and the free run, and e must be shown to decrease with inner-solve budget (if e is flat in the budget, the ledger is tautological and must be rejected). (3) W >= 0 on every accepted step (myosin cannot absorb net mechanical work under a v>=0-clamped Hill law) — sign-sense. (4) The clamped/free contrast: delta-abscissa/(tau*v0) differs between the two configurations by at least a factor of 10 in the settled window, with clamped < free.
validation_steps.negative_control: `--nc reset-abscissa-before-ledger`: accumulate work AFTER the detach reset; closure (2) must FAIL with energy appearing from nowhere — this is a real bug the ledger must be able to see. `--nc dissipation-modelled`: compute D from the assumed |F|^2 * dt/gamma form instead of the measured F.dx; the budget-refinement test in (2) must then close trivially, which is the tautology signature the gate must reject.

validation_steps.step: M7 — grid invariance of the pair result
validation_steps.what_is_measured: Every M1/M3 observable (transmitted reaction, shortening-per-step, rho, ledger closure, cross-binding count) as a function of n_per_fiber.
validation_steps.protocol: Sweep n_per_fiber over 5, 9, 17, 33 (and hence axial segment length from ~1.7 um down to ~0.2 um). This matters acutely here: the whole 0.301 um minifilament sits INSIDE a single 1.7 um segment at n_per_fiber=5, so all 20 crossbridge reactions are barycentrically smeared onto two nodes almost a micron away; refinement localises them. Report each observable against segment length with a fitted exponent.
validation_steps.pass_criterion: Transmitted anchor reaction and shortening-per-step converge with refinement: successive-rung relative change decreases monotonically and the finest two rungs agree to <= 2%. Cross-binding count == 0 at every rung. The abscissa->shortening identity (M3) must hold at EVERY rung to 1e-6 — an identity may not degrade with the mesh. If any observable instead scales as a power of segment length with a non-zero exponent, the result is declared MESH-BOUND and surfaced to PI rather than quoted at a chosen resolution.
validation_steps.negative_control: Deliberately report the n_per_fiber=5 value as the answer and check that the harness itself flags it as the coarsest rung with a non-converged banner. Plus `--nc segment-length-scaled-k`: scale k_axial with segment length in the wrong direction; the convergence criterion must FAIL, proving the sweep is sensitive.

validation_steps.step: M8 — two-pair superposition: prove pairs do not leak into each other through a shared array
validation_steps.what_is_measured: The transmitted reaction of two spatially separated single pairs run in ONE slice, versus twice the single-pair result run alone, at identical seeds and identical bound populations.
validation_steps.protocol: Build n_ventral=2 with the bundles placed far apart (separation >> capture radius), same seed per pair; compare against two independent n_ventral=1 runs. Also assert the population-ledger disjointness that already exists and add an explicit check that no node index is shared between the two bundles and no head's bound segment belongs to the other bundle.
validation_steps.pass_criterion: Per-pair reaction in the joint run equals the isolated run to 1e-9 relative, and the joint total equals exactly 2x. Zero cross-bundle head bindings. This is the motor-lane instance of the co-location-is-not-connection failure: at 494,802 nodes a merged array made the stiffness block-diagonal and the MT aster moved 0.0 nm; here the inverse leak (unintended coupling through a shared array) must be shown absent by measurement, not by reading the code.
validation_steps.negative_control: `--nc merge-arrays`: run with the two bundles' minifilaments aliased into one particle block with overlapping indices; the per-pair equality must FAIL. `--nc bundles-adjacent`: place the two bundles within one capture radius; cross-bundle bindings must become non-zero, proving the check can fail.

validation_steps.step: M9 — visualisation checkpoint: isolation render + cumulative render, browser-verified
validation_steps.what_is_measured: Whether the geometry, the load path and the kinetics are visibly correct at single-motor magnification, and whether the pair is visible in the composed cell scene.
validation_steps.protocol: Extend `ac/engine` with a state dump for this slice (positions + forces + per-head bound/abscissa/slide/load/walk_dir/seg_a/seg_b/bound-filament-id) and extend `scripts/ac_sf_arc_vis.py::_motor_zoom_scene` from host placement to native dynamic state; refresh the cumulative composed scene via `scripts/ac_cell_assembled_viz.py` (data-driven from the dump, so a new component's scene appears automatically); verify in a real browser with `scripts/browser_check.py` and eyeball the screenshot. Full native resolution, no downsampling. Isotropic magnification only (no per-axis stretch), no axis truncation, units annotated, per-realisation thin lines plus mean for the seed ensemble.
validation_steps.pass_criterion: The isolation scene shows, and a human confirms in the browser screenshot: (1) the two filaments side by side at 2*head_offset with barbed stubs pointing OUTWARD; (2) the backbone between them; (3) EVERY head arm drawn, each head coloured bound/unbound; (4) the crossbridge drawn from the head to its ACTUAL attachment point INCLUDING the abscissa offset (this is the quantity nothing currently renders); (5) the head force arrow together with its two barycentric reaction arrows, so Newton's third law is visually checkable; (6) the two anchor reaction arrows pointing inward. The cumulative scene must show the nmii component present, coloured by per-node force, with the pair distinguishable. A grep of the HTML is explicitly not verification.
validation_steps.negative_control: Render the `--nc flip-polarity` and `--nc ghost-anchor` runs through the SAME scene builder; the reversed barbed stubs / outward anchor arrows and the pinned backbone must be visually obvious. If the two runs look identical, the render is decorative and does not satisfy the viz checkpoint.

validation_steps.step: M10 — gate-contract authoring with observed negative-control flips
validation_steps.what_is_measured: That every claim above is pinned (observable definition + threshold + configuration + derivation) and that each one has been OBSERVED to fail on a wrong input.
validation_steps.protocol: Author `docs/v2_audit/gate_contracts/GATE_M_single_pair_motor.yaml` in the existing v1 schema (`gate_id`, `claims[].observable/threshold/measure/verdict_path`, content hash), extend the schema with a per-claim `negative_control` block (control name, expected direction of failure, observed flip boolean, artifact path), extend `outputs/tag_kb/gate_contract.py` / `verify_gate_contracts.py` to require the flip for every claim, and stamp the hash into the run artifact as GATE-B already does. Split the claim sets explicitly into `mechanism` (PASS/FAIL) and `magnitude` (REPORTED, status BLOCKED).
validation_steps.pass_criterion: Every mechanism claim carries `negative_control.observed_flip: true` from a real run artifact; the verifier refuses the contract otherwise. No magnitude claim is in the blocking set. The artifact carries an explicit BLOCKED banner on every quantitative number and names each PI-GAP constant it used.
validation_steps.negative_control: Submit a contract in which one claim's negative control was never run; the verifier must refuse it. Submit a claim whose threshold makes it structurally unfailable (the historical largest-fragment-vs-second-largest pattern); the flip requirement must expose it because no wrong input can flip it.

FA/ECM track (fa_actin_anchor + integrin_collagen_clutch + ff/substrate.py + ff/ecm_library.py) — NOT a blocker for the pair gate, but required to retire the Dirichlet-pin stand-in and to place this motor into the PI's adherent-on-2D-collagen baseline. Head exclusivity across MOTOR edges (one head may bind only one target) — blocker for composing nmii_cortex_motor and nmii_sf_motor in one cell (REPORT.md open item 4), NOT a blocker for the single-pair gate, which has exactly one target.

The speed-optimisation track (cg_check_every early-exit, assembled per-fiber coarse; both default-off pending a native A/B) — must NOT be enabled during M1-M8. The pair gate is small enough that neither is needed, and enabling an unvalidated coarsening inside the gate that is supposed to certify the mechanism would repeat the coarse-configuration failure. Run the A/B afterwards, using the pair gate's own bit-identity as one of the checks.

PI decisions listed in open_questions_for_pi — in particular the capture-radius reconciliation and the backbone L_p choice — gate whether any magnitude may leave BLOCKED status. They do not gate the mechanism claims.

risks: LOAD PATH THAT SUMS TO ZERO — the primary risk, and the one the committed record already hints at. A bipolar minifilament is a force DIPOLE: its net force is zero BY CONSTRUCTION, so any 'net force' metric is guaranteed zero and proves nothing (the mirror of the crawl failure where isotropic radial traction cancelled laterally). Meanwhile the GATE-B record shows 301/320 heads bound with max head load 0.0546 pN but T_max only 0.254 pN — roughly five heads' worth of transmitted load from 301 bound heads. That is either legitimate load sharing plus heterogeneity, or massive internal cancellation. Mitigation: the cancellation ledger (transmitted anchor reaction vs sum|f_head| per filament) is mandatory, and a ratio below 0.05 with many heads bound must raise a flag to PI rather than pass.

CROSS-BINDING and BOTH-GROUPS-ON-ONE-FILAMENT. SegmentQuery takes the nearest segment within capture with no filament filter, so a + head can in principle bind the - filament (self-cancelling internal load) or, if straddle_frame degenerates, both groups can land on the SAME filament — which produces filament tension while the pair does not contract at all, i.e. a metric that looks like success. Excluded today only by the derived inequality capture 0.210 < lateral 0.400 um, never verified at runtime.

METRIC MEASURING THE WRONG THING #1: k_axial*(L-r0) is not the transmitted load. k_axial is an admitted modelling GAP (NF2007 treats the backbone as inextensible and rejects an axial penalty spring), and at n_per_fiber=5 the 'segment' whose stretch is being read is ~1.7 um long while the whole motor is 0.301 um. Use the Dirichlet anchor reaction as the primary transmitted-load observable and report k*(L-r0) as secondary.

METRIC MEASURING THE WRONG THING #2: NG-1's transmission ratio |reaction_B|/|reaction_A| is a SYMMETRY measure, not a transmission measure — it reads ~1 even when both sides are commonly wrong (it read 0.918 PASS in the very run whose reactions were 3x under the analytic). It cannot detect common-mode loss. The one-sided-binding test (M2) is the asymmetric probe that actually tests the path.

TAUTOLOGICAL ENERGY LEDGER. If elastic energy and dissipation are computed from the same increments the solver uses, closure is guaranteed and the ledger measures nothing — the A/A0 = V/V0 = 1.000 failure in a new costume. Mitigations: an independent potential-energy evaluator, dissipation MEASURED as F.dx along the actual path, and a mandatory check that the closure error DECREASES with inner-solve budget (a budget-independent closure is rejected).

POSITIVE FEEDBACK BETWEEN NON-CONVERGENCE AND APPARENT TENSION. The stall cap da_max = (f_stall - F)/k_xb uses loads computed before the step; an unconverged solve underestimates F, so the cap fails to bind, the abscissa overshoots, and the next step's tension is inflated. Non-convergence therefore systematically INFLATES both motor work and tension — the opposite of a conservative error, and consistent with the withdrawn 1.92 pN.

ABSCISSA RESET ERASES MOTOR WORK. abscissa is zeroed on detach, so any ledger that samples after the commit sees energy appear from nowhere. Must accumulate before the reset; there is a dedicated negative control for exactly this.

TORQUE IS NOT CONSERVED by the directional crossbridge. Momentum is exactly conserved, but the couple (x_head - x_att0) x f is nonzero whenever the head sits off the actin line (max measured offset 0.055 um). A gate that checks only sum of forces will report a clean pass on a system that is quietly gaining angular momentum. Must be measured, bounded, and shown to scale linearly with the offset.

A GATE THAT CANNOT FAIL. 'reactions are equal and opposite' is guaranteed by the symmetric bipolar construction; 'tension exceeds a single head's load' is close to structurally guaranteed once several heads bind (the GATE-B adversarial pass already flagged a structurally-guaranteed bound-vs-tension correlation). Every claim must be shown to flip under a specific wrong input, and the flip recorded in the artifact.

SMALL-N STOCHASTICITY. One minifilament has ~20 heads; Binomial noise on the engaged count is large, so a single-seed pair result is not a result. Ensembles with per-realisation lines plus mean are mandatory, and any claim must survive the seed spread.

COARSE-CONFIGURATION CONCLUSION, the failure this project has made six times. The single-pair gate is BY DESIGN not the full native population, and it deliberately omits the alpha-actinin joint that blocks the population lane. Nothing it proves may be presented as a population or physiological result; its scope limit must be written into the contract, and the grid-invariance sweep (M7) must run before any number leaves it.

REGIME CONFUSION. A converged free pair legitimately shows near-zero tension and fast sliding, while a converged clamped pair shows sustained tension and no sliding. Reporting one regime's number as 'the' myosin force — or comparing across regimes — is a category error. Every artifact must name its boundary condition next to every number.

SCOPE CREEP INTO MAGNITUDE. f_stall, N_side, k_on, v0, kappa, k_xb, the catch-slip constants and the backbone L_p are all GAP (params_i0b3.yaml:44 lists the native-run blockers). Any pass criterion that quietly depends on one of them is not a mechanism gate. The whole design is built so the blocking claim set is conservation / identity / sign / symmetry / limit / scaling / grid-invariance only.
open_questions_for_pi: GOVERNANCE, and the one that must be answered first: CLAUDE.md requires validation and debugging at the FULL native population, while your instruction today is smallest-scale-first (one motor, one pair). These are in direct tension. How should a deliberately small-scale mechanism gate be recorded on the evidence ladder — as a new named rung below CUDA_UNIT, as a prerequisite artifact that does not itself promote nmii, or as an explicit ratified exception with a written scope limit? I will not decide this myself.

NMII capture radius: 0.05 vs 0.210 um (ROLLING_ROADMAP.md:75 records the code-vs-yaml conflict). ac/cell/assemble.py:177 derives 0.210 as r0_head 0.200 + 10 nm slack. The straddle placement's measured max head-to-filament-line residual is 0.055 um — inside 0.210, outside 0.05. Which value is production? The answer decides whether some heads are out of reach by construction.

NMII backbone persistence length: the 1.0 um fixture (at which NG-1 read 6/6) versus the 0.13 um single-coiled-coil literature proxy (at which NG-1 read 4/6 with reactions 1.74/1.60 pN vs 4.96 pN analytic). Which is the production value, or do we accept shape-only gating until a mature multi-tail measurement exists? The magnitude half of every motor gate hangs on this.

SF axial mechanics: NF2007 treats the actin backbone as INEXTENSIBLE and rejects an axial penalty spring, yet the SF component carries a Hookean k_axial that is an admitted GAP and that sets the scale of the tension observable. Should the pair gate switch to the inextensibility constraint and read the Lagrange multiplier as tension (the physically cleaner observable), or keep the penalty spring and rely on the anchor reaction as primary? This is a mechanism choice, not a tuning one.

Is a Dirichlet pin on the two barbed ends an acceptable STAND-IN for the pair gate's boundary, or must the pair gate wait for the FA/ECM clutch so that the boundary is a modelled adhesion on 2D collagen from the start? Your physiological-baseline rule points one way; smallest-scale-first points the other.

Torque: the directional crossbridge is not couple-balanced when a head sits off the actin line. Do we (a) accept the residual as physically carried by the lever arm and simply measure and bound it, (b) add a compensating couple on the backbone, or (c) require the placement to drive the perpendicular offset to zero so the residual vanishes by construction? Option (c) also implies a tolerance on the placement.

Curved-sarcomere motor placement remains open: the perinuclear cap is excluded by construction (bipolar dot -0.600, scale-invariant), so it currently carries NO motor. Does the arched cap get its own placement geometry, a different motor primitive, or a documented no-motor status?
Head exclusivity across MOTOR edges: may one head bind two targets (e.g. cortex and SF)? Needed before nmii_cortex_motor and nmii_sf_motor compose in one cell. Not needed for the pair gate.

Confirm that a mechanism-only closure is what you want here: every magnitude in this track stays BLOCKED, no cortical-tension or per-head-force number is quotable, and the artifact says so in every caption. If you want any magnitude to become quotable, the GAP constants above must close first.

Ratify the negative-control requirement as a gate-contract SCHEMA change (a required per-claim negative_control block with an observed flip, enforced by verify_gate_contracts.py). This changes the contract format, which is a gate-contract change and therefore yours to sign, not mine.

result.summary: The strategic core (Part B/C/D) is the strongest part and survives attack: "no magnet at the cell-ECM interface, rigid BC only at the dish, KINETICS_FROZEN as the Stage-1 scaffold" is correct, is argued on build-cost rather than dogma, and the indictment of the live `fa_traction_is_inward` verdict (scripts/ac_gate_b_sf_motor_native.py:584 reading a Dirichlet reaction from :171 and calling it traction) is exactly right. The validation TRACK, however, is over-optimistic in ways I could confirm in code. Four load-bearing defects: (1) The design's factual premise "measured: ac/ imports NONE of these" is FALSE — ffn_sim/ac/solid/adhesion_clutch.py:37 already imports ff.fa_ecm, and that existing ac/ primitive throws the Newton reaction away (:78, :88 "rigid substrate -> discarded"), i.e. the one-sided clutch the design says must be avoided is already resident. (2) A3's central connectedness gate is provably blind to the failure it names: from ffn_sim/ac/engine/ecm_world.py:396 (R = -f over pinned nodes) and ledger.py:265 (traction fed from the ECM-side scatter), R + T = Sum(free-node residuals) - B_ecm, so a cell-side-only clutch gives R=0, T=0, residual 0/0 -> negative control (c) cannot fire, and a symmetric unconverged solve passes because residuals cancel in the resultant. (3) A8's perturbation channel is inert: FarFieldDirichletBoundaryRuntime.accumulate_boundary (ecm_world.py:518) ignores `pos` entirely and `target_position_d` appears only in the work kernel, so a "prescribed dish displacement" moves nothing while the boundary-work criterion re-derives the kernel's own formula (:445). (4) A0 cannot run as written: forces_manifest.py is hard-wired to ac/cell (_ACCUM_SITE at :214, AST parse of ac/cell/driver.py at :289, imports of ac.cell.assemble at :355) and has zero visibility into an ac/engine ComposedNativeCell — while ac/cell is feature-frozen. Plus a real order-of-operations bug (ecm_world.py:983 boundary BEFORE :988 clutch) that both invalidates R+T=0 and lets a clutch bound to a pinned collagen node inject unbalanced force. Two headline pass criteria are tautologies (the joint-count guard is a dataclass default that no code path can change; trace(M_sym)<0 for a closed ventral dipole is the same by-construction check the design condemned), and A2's catch-extremum gate FAILS on the track's own sourced chemistry (alpha2beta1-collagen is documented slip-only, adhesion_clutch.py:13-15). Effort is low by roughly 2-3x. All defects are local and fixable; the staging and the anti-confound instincts are keepers.
must_fix: A1 negative control (c) CANNOT FIRE — the design's one claimed double-count guard is dead code. `MechanicalGroupResolution.mechanical_joint_count` is a dataclass field defaulting to 1 (ffn_sim/ac/engine/load_path.py:271) and `resolve_fa_series_group` constructs it WITHOUT ever passing that field (:293-297), so the check `if resolution.mechanical_joint_count != 1: raise RuntimeError` (:373-374) is literally `1 != 1`. Two `CompositeFAJointSpec`s over the same sf_port/ecm_port pair each resolve fine, and `LoadPathJointRuntime` enforces uniqueness only on `joint_id` (:639-641) — not on (port_a, port_b) or `fa_cluster_id`. So two springs on one FA cluster is achievable TODAY and undetected. Correct the design's risk text ('Only the last is currently guarded (load_path.py:274)' is false — ZERO of the four paths is numerically guarded) and replace the criterion with a device-checked per-(fa_cluster_id, port-pair) uniqueness invariant plus a measured `load_pn` doubling test.

A3 pass criterion (c) and its negative control (c) are void. Derived from the code: `_far_field_reaction_ledger_kernel` records R_k = -f_k over pinned ECM nodes (ecm_world.py:396-413) and `add_cell_traction` is fed from the ECM-side scatter (ledger.py:265-271). ECM body sum: Sum_all f = 0(internal pairs) + T + B, and Sum_pinned f = T + B - Sum_free r, hence R + T = Sum_free r - B_ecm. The residual therefore measures only (i) the RESULTANT of free-node solver residuals and (ii) an ECM body force. A cell-side-only clutch gives T=0, no ECM load, R=0 -> residual 0 with denominator sum|traction|=0. Fix: feed the traction channel from the CELL-side scatter (so one-sidedness produces R=0, T!=0), OR replace the criterion with a per-joint device assertion that |f_scattered_on_A + f_scattered_on_B| = 0 joint-by-joint, which is the only numeric statement that actually tests two-sidedness.

ORDER-OF-OPERATIONS BUG: `ECMWorld.accumulate_mechanics` runs `boundary_anchor.accumulate` at ecm_world.py:983, BEFORE `membrane_contact` (:984) and BEFORE `alpha2beta1_clutch.accumulate()` (:988). Two consequences: (a) the recorded reaction R structurally EXCLUDES the clutch traction, so R + T = 0 is not the right identity in the current dispatch order; (b) `_far_field_reaction_ledger_kernel` zeroes the pinned node's force at 983 and the clutch then adds force to it at 988 with nothing to remove it — a clutch bound to a pinned collagen node injects unbalanced force and the 'Dirichlet' node moves. With a thin-slab dish (pinned face) and nearest-node capture (`attach_clutches_to_ecm`, ff/fa_ecm.py:100-109) basal FA will preferentially bind near the pinned face, so this is likely, not hypothetical. The design's anti-double-count assertion covers pin-intersect-clutch on the CELL side but NOT on the ECM side. Add the ECM-side case and reorder the boundary application to last.

A8's perturbation channel injects no displacement. `FarFieldDirichletBoundaryRuntime.accumulate_boundary(pos, force)` IGNORES `pos` (ecm_world.py:518-525) — the Dirichlet is enforced by force-zeroing alone — and `target_position_d` is consumed ONLY by `_far_field_reaction_commit_kernel`'s work term (:428-448). A 'prescribed far-field dish displacement via the moving target' therefore moves nothing: the ECM will not respond, the chain-continuity matrix reads DISCONNECTED for reasons unrelated to connectedness, and the boundary-work criterion still passes because it re-derives line 445. `ac/engine/INTEGRATION_ecm_world.md:45` already says the prescribed-motion path 'remain[s] future'. Either author a real prescribed-motion boundary (write pinned positions) as budgeted new physics, or drop perturbation (i) and use two independent motor perturbations at opposite ends of the chain.

A0 cannot be executed against the adherent baseline. `forces_manifest.py` is hard-wired to the ac/cell incumbent: `_ACCUM_SITE = 'ffn_sim/ac/cell/driver.py::_accumulate_all'` (:214), `assert_force_channels_cover_accumulate` AST-parses ac/cell/driver.py against a HARDCODED literal declared-set (:289, :311-318), and the runtime path imports `ac.cell.assemble` / `ac.cell.compartments` (:355-356). It has zero visibility into an ac/engine `ComposedNativeCell`, and ac/cell is feature-frozen so the clutch cannot be added there. Also A0(d) — 'classify each of the 32 by whether its runtime scatters into two distinct owner force arrays' — is NOT statically decidable from Python objects; you cannot know which arrays a Warp kernel writes without running it. A declaration walk reproduces the design's OWN named risk ('PROTOCOL FLAG-CHECK MISTAKEN FOR EVIDENCE'). A real census requires a GPU perturb-and-observe probe (zero all force arrays, launch one connector, diff which arrays changed), so A0 is neither needs_gpu:false nor 0.5 day.

A4(b) re-imports the exact tautology the design condemned. A ventral SF is a CLOSED DIPOLE with both ends at FA sites (ac/engine/sf_population.py:169; the gate script's own comment at scripts/ac_gate_b_sf_motor_native.py:176-179 spells it out), so contraction drives trace(M_sym) < 0 by construction and the criterion can fail only on a motor sign error — precisely the reason the design declared `fa_traction_is_inward` (:584) illegitimate in Part C. Keep it explicitly labelled as a SIGN check, and make the load-bearing evidence the deviatoric/orientation response with a PRE-REGISTERED bias operator.

A2's pass criterion fails the track's own sourced chemistry. `ac/solid/adhesion_clutch.py:13-15` documents alpha2beta1-collagen as a PURE SLIP bond (k_off0 = 0.44 /s, x_beta = 0.7 nm, Attwood 2013, DOI 10.3390/ijms14022832) and states 'The alpha5beta1-fibronectin catch bond, Kong 2009, is a shape PROXY only — not used here.' A2 REQUIRES a catch extremum to exist and lists pure slip as the FAILING negative control — so the gate penalises the sourced law and rewards the unsourced proxy. Decide the physics: either run Attwood slip and delete the catch-extremum criterion, or run the alpha5beta1 proxy and label the artifact PROXY-CHEMISTRY. Note `load_path.py:291` hard-requires the card string 'alpha2beta1_collagen', so the mislabel would be stamped into the resolved joint.

trace(M_ij) is origin-dependent and the origin is never specified. trace(M) = Sum x_k . f_k; shifting the origin by a gives trace - a . Sum(f). With Sum(f) permitted up to the balance tolerance and Mikado box coordinates of order 10-100 um, the SIGN of the contractility readout can be flipped by the coordinate origin. Pin the origin (traction-weighted centroid), and report trace at two origins so the sensitivity is visible.
tautological_gates: A1 'joint count == 1': `mechanical_joint_count` is a dataclass default of 1 (load_path.py:271) never set by any code path (:293-297); the check at :373 is 1 != 1. Cannot fail.

A1 'sum(f) = 0 to 1e-12': `_segment_joint_force_kernel` writes +wa0*f, +wa1*f, -wb0*f, -wb1*f with wa0+wa1=1 and wb0+wb1=1 forced at load_path.py:532/:534. Force closure holds for ANY weights, so it is blind to the very 0.5/0.5 weight bug negative control (a) injects (only moment closure and virtual work catch that). It is a change-detector, not a validation.
A1 'load_pn == k*extension (not 2x)': load_path.py:548 literally computes `wp.abs(stiffness[t] * extension)`. The assertion compares the expression to itself.

A1 series identity '1/k = 1/k1 + 1/k2 and k <= min(k1,k2)': you write the harmonic mean and then assert the harmonic mean. Both statements are algebraic identities and cannot detect a physically wrong decomposition (e.g. N integrins in parallel inside one cluster).

A2 'numerically located minimum matches analytic F*': the numerical argmin of a closed form compared against the analytic argmin of the SAME closed form. And 'kernel agrees with clutch_off_rate_np to float64 round-off' compares `_pereverzev` (fa_clutch_warp.py:29) with `pereverzev_off_rate` — the same algebra transcribed twice. Transcription check only; the 3-ratio variation and the x_catch=0 control are the only falsifiable parts.

A4(b) 'trace(M_sym) NEGATIVE whenever any bond is loaded': guaranteed by the closed-dipole geometry of a ventral SF (sf_population.py:169; ac_gate_b_sf_motor_native.py:176-179). Same by-construction shape as `fa_traction_is_inward` (:584), which the design itself rejects.

A5(c) 'rejected step leaves state/age/rng_epoch bit-identical': `_commit_joint_state_kernel` writes those arrays ONLY inside `if active[t] != 0 and accepted[0] != 0` (load_path.py:563-571). Bit-identity on rejection is structural. The design provides a negative control for the RELEASE claim but NONE for the rollback claim — it needs a control kernel that writes committed state outside the acceptance guard.

A7(a) 'k_series monotone non-decreasing in N_vin, never exceeds the parallel bound': `k_int_effective = k_int*(1 + alpha*N_vin)` (fa_maturation.py:127-130) with alpha=0.03 and N_max=5 gives at most 1.15x bare against a ~2x parallel bound. Both criteria are algebraic identities.

A7(b) as it stands in-tree: fa_maturation.py:43-44 ships FA_KG0=0.01 and FA_KD=0.005, i.e. k_g0 = 2*k_d EXACTLY, and the module docstring (:19-20) declares the fixed point 'at F = F_th = 5.0 pN exactly' as a 'KB constraint'. The module's own verification gate IS the tautology A7's negative control (b) names. The design correctly identifies the class but does not note that its 3-ratio sweep must depart from the sourced KB constraint, nor label that sweep synthetic.

A8 'boundary work equals sum(reaction . delta_target) to round-off': that IS the kernel, `dwork = wp.dot(reaction[t], target[t] - committed_target[t])` atomically summed (ecm_world.py:445-446). It can fail only on a reduction bug.

A6(a) grid-invariance evaluated on the traction RESULTANT: ~0 at every discretization for a self-equilibrated cell, so 0 ~= 0 ~= 0 passes by construction. Use sum|f|, per-clutch mean load, and trace(M).
hidden_magnitude_deps: A2's catch-extremum gate needs k_c0*x_c > k_s0*x_s, which is only satisfied by the alpha5beta1-fibronectin preset (hand_kmc.py:150-156). The track's declared chemistry (alpha2beta1-collagen) is documented slip-only with sourced constants (adhesion_clutch.py:13-15, Attwood 2013). So the gate is evaluable only on an unsourced proxy and FAILS on the sourced law — the inverse of a usable connectedness gate.

A7's dA/dt zero-crossing requires the achieved per-clutch load range to bracket F_fix = F_th*(k_d/(k_g0-k_d))^(1/n). Every load-setting input (f_stall, k_xb, duty, k_series, k_axial) is a declared PI-GAP (ac_gate_b_sf_motor_native.py:42-47). If the achieved range does not bracket the crossing there is nothing to locate, and choosing F_th so it does is fitting a constant to make a gate evaluable. Marked needs_gpu:true, implying an in-loop measurement rather than a prescribed-load unit sweep; the design never disambiguates. Fix: run A7 as a prescribed-load host/unit sweep in units of F_th (magnitude-free), and drop it from the native path.

A6's rigid-limit criterion needs a magnitude that does not exist for the chosen substrate. `resolve_substrate` k_sub = 2*E*a/(1-nu^2) (substrate.py:48-55) carries the admitted-absent patch radius `a` (:33-34, A_ADHESION_UM_DEFAULT=0.05 explicitly flagged), and it is the WINKLER-anchor representation the track decided NOT to use. For a live Mikado network there is no analytic effective stiffness at a collagen material point, so 'k_ECM/k_clutch -> infinity' is not a single-parameter sweep and 'converge to the fixed-anchor path within solver tolerance' has no computable target. Also, stiffening the ECM degrades convergence exactly where the project already sits at 15.5% residual, so the tolerance criterion becomes unreachable in the limit.

A0(b) demands that a REAL physiological force be off. `motility_warp.gravity_kernel` (:331-339) documents itself as 'REAL physics (a derived body force ~= 1 pN/cell at MCF7 size), NOT a tuned proxy'. Requiring enabled=False contradicts the physiological-baseline HARD rule (an adherent cell in media does sediment). The correct criterion is provenance + value (value == derived rho_delta*g*v_node, provenance DERIVED), not enabled==False. The design conflated 'the SettlingForce proxy was 19,000-47,000x too large' with 'body forces are forbidden'.

The force-balance TOLERANCE is load-bearing in A3(c), A4(a), A6 and A8 but is deferred wholesale to PI. `assemble_balance` takes a caller-supplied squared tolerance (ledger.py:329-342) and none exists in the tree (ac_gate_b_cortex_motor_native.py:506: the balance gate 'requires a GlobalCellLedger + tol_sq_d wired by the Lead'). Under the no-magic-number rule the design should PROPOSE the derivation (e.g. a stated multiple of the reported CG residual, or the assembled Gershgorin bound times displacement round-off) rather than leave four gates un-evaluable.

CompositeFAJointSpec.__post_init__ (load_path.py:312-318) only requires stiffness finite and positive. The series resolver removes the 'unaudited scalar' framing but BOTH sub-stiffnesses remain unsourced for alpha2beta1 in the engine path (k_int=800 pN/um is sourced in adhesion_clutch.py:49 and should be adopted; the actin-talin-integrin arm has no source). A1's algebra is magnitude-free — fine — but A3 onward runs on those numbers and every artifact must carry them with provenance.
sums_to_zero_risks: A3(c) itself: R + T = Sum(free-node residuals) - B_ecm (derived from ecm_world.py:396 and ledger.py:265). The FIRST term is a RESULTANT of residuals, which cancels for a symmetric unpolarised cell — so the documented 15.5% non-convergence can pass the balance gate. The design's claim that 'only the numeric balance gate with its denominator is [evidence]' is wrong: the gate is an ECM-body-force leak detector plus a weak convergence proxy, and is silent on two-sidedness.

One-sided clutch produces 0/0: with cell-side-only scatter, T=0 (channel fed from the ECM-side scatter) and the ECM is never loaded so R=0. Negative control (c) asserts a failure that cannot occur. The design half-noticed ('reported WITH its denominator so a zero field cannot pass silently') but did not follow the argument to its control.

Self-cancelling channels are invisible to every resultant gate in the design. `spreading_reaction_kernel` (motility_warp.py:397-405) exists precisely to subtract the net pushed vector so the spreading push 'exerts ZERO net force on the cell'. A confound of that family passes A3(c), A4(a) AND A4(c) untouched — yet that is exactly the historically dangerous shape (a push+reaction pair that did the flattening credited to the lamellipodium). A4's negative control (c) detects only a naive net-nonzero body force. Add a per-channel work/power ledger (each channel's f.v summed) — a net-zero force pair still injects non-zero power.

A4(a) 'sum(f) over cell+ECM+boundary reaches zero' is an identity of Newton's third law for a closed system once converged; it cannot fail except from an external force or non-cancelling residuals, i.e. it largely restates A3(c). Presenting it first as evidence inverts the weight: only the dipole/anisotropy parts (b)/(c) carry the anti-crawl-failure content.

'Motor activity biased along one axis' is undefined; for a population of closed ventral dipoles the deviatoric part of M is set by the bundle ORIENTATION distribution, so a global scalar myosin bias changes magnitudes, not orientation, and the anisotropy may not move at all. Pre-register the bias operator (e.g. activate only myosin on fibers within theta of x-hat) BEFORE the run, or an implementer will pick whichever bias makes the gate pass.

A3 negative control (a) creates a singular system the design does not acknowledge. Once the Dirichlet moves to the dish, the SF's only constraint is the clutch; setting all bonds FREE removes every boundary condition while myosin still drives it -> 6 rigid-body modes with non-zero net force -> the relax/CG drifts or diverges.
