R4 Step-count / accept-ratio axis (larger stable dt, fewer wasted rolled-back outers, better outer globalization) — 2-100x, and possibly the largest single-run lever | the project's own verdict, `FF_SINGLE_CELL_OPTIMIZATION_PLAN §0.8`: "the bigger win needs a DIFFERENT axis -- number/size of timesteps, or ~10x HBM bandwidth"; plus the measured 172 s spent on a step that committed 0.0 s. Physics-accuracy change -> needs a dt-convergence gate.
R5 Per-fiber kernel coalescing/occupancy (bit-identical layout transpose) — 1.3-3x on the two projector applies per operator apply | hypothesis from `inner_mechanics.py:79-140` structure; unmeasured.
R6 Conditional-graph capture (`wp.capture_while(self.active, ...)`) of the CG loop + the transaction fan-out — 1.05-1.15x on the non-MG path, 1.3-2x on the MG path, AND it removes FIX1's host readback so the zero-DtoH gate passes | launch-count arithmetic; Warp 1.14 API verified present.
R7 FIX1 as-is — ~1x on the production budget-exhausted path, up to 5.3x where the solve converges early | commit 09c14eb8; superseded by R6.
R8 FIX2 — may be REJECTED by its own A/B | commit 09c14eb8 requires a native reduction-factor A/B; the MG path is 2.6x slower in wall than the incumbent today.
R9 f32 PRECONDITIONER ONLY (never force, never position, never the accept predicate) — 1.1-1.4x on the precondition fraction | a preconditioner is an arbitrary SPD operator, so this cannot move a CONVERGED fixed point by construction; but see the open question, because the production path is NOT converged.
R10 Neural surrogate / SBI — 1e3-1e6x on sweep EVALUATION count, 1.0x on native decision latency | Arruda 2026 in-tree: NPE 32,100 sims vs ABC 66k-432k, ~1 s amortized inference.
R11 Device-scalar CG cadence — 1.09x | measured in ff (sc1); port to ac only if S0 shows the same sync fraction there.

validation_steps.step: S0 - Build the two missing observables: (a) accepted-step throughput, (b) per-kernel roofline/occupancy breakdown of the operator apply
validation_steps.what_is_measured: (a) committed physical seconds per wall hour = sum(dt_phys over ACCEPTED outer steps) / wall, plus the accept ratio (accepted / attempted outer steps) and wall wasted on rolled-back steps. (b) per-kernel CUDA-event time for every kernel inside one _operator apply and one _precondition apply, via wp.timing_begin(wp.TIMING_KERNEL); analytically-derived bytes-moved and f64-FLOP per kernel (from launch dim x arrays touched x dtype width, written down per kernel, never fitted); achieved GB/s and achieved GFLOP/s as a fraction of the device's published peaks; achieved occupancy; hot-loop DtoH count. (c) peak HBM per cell via the existing NVML accounting.
validation_steps.protocol: Extend the existing profiler site (driver.py:1059-1080) from TIMING_MEMCPY to TIMING_KERNEL|TIMING_MEMCPY, keeping the existing positive-control pattern. Add a per-kernel byte/FLOP table as a literal, reviewable data structure next to each launch (one entry per kernel, derived from its launch dim and its argument arrays; no measured constant). Run at the full native baseline (70,686 filaments / 494,802 actin / 551,434 total, physiological setpoints, adherent-on-2D-collagen once that config exists) on the A5000. Report peak HBM via ac/cell/gpu_memory_accounting.py. rm -rf ~/.cache/warp/<ver> before every arm (the project has a documented stale-kernel-cache false-positive).
validation_steps.pass_criterion: CLOSURE IDENTITY: the sum of per-kernel CUDA-event times inside a stage equals that stage's independently measured wall to within 5% (a conservation criterion on the profile itself - a profile that does not close is measuring something other than the step). AND the profiler's existing positive control fires (a deliberate post-loop scalar download is seen). AND the achieved-fraction-of-peak numbers are reported for BOTH roofs so the bandwidth-bound-vs-latency-bound question is decided by measurement rather than assertion. No pass/fail on any speed number at this step - S0's only job is to be non-vacuous.
validation_steps.negative_control: Insert a deliberately slow no-op kernel (a dummy launch with a 10x inner loop) into the operator apply and confirm (i) it appears as the new dominant kernel, (ii) the closure identity still holds with it included, and (iii) removing it restores the original ranking. Second control: run the same profiler on a 1-fiber cell and confirm the dominant kernel CHANGES - proving the ranking is data-dependent and not an artifact of the instrumentation order. Third control: run with profile_memcpy on and cg_check_every>0 and confirm hot_dtoh_copies > 0, i.e. the gate at driver.py:1201 actually detects the readback (this simultaneously proves the gate is live and documents the FIX1 conflict).

validation_steps.step: S1 - Land FIX1 correctly: prove bit-identity, then REPLACE the host readback with a device-side conditional-graph while-loop so the zero-DtoH gate passes
validation_steps.what_is_measured: Bit-identity of the returned dx (all 494,802 vec3d compared bit-for-bit, not to a tolerance) and of a hash of the whole committed post-step state; the distribution of iterations-to-latch per outer step (this is what decides whether FIX1 is worth anything on the production path); hot-loop DtoH count; launches per step; wall per committed physical second.
validation_steps.protocol: Arm A: cg_check_every=0 (default). Arm B: cg_check_every=K>0. Arm C: the loop re-expressed as wp.capture_while(self.active, body) with self.active updated in-device by the existing _cg_finalize_kernel, so the loop count stays data-dependent and no host read occurs. Verify wp.is_conditional_graph_supported() on the A5000 and record the driver/CUDA version in the artifact. Compare A vs B vs C: dx bit-identity, state hash, DtoH count, wall. Report the per-outer histogram of iterations-to-latch alongside, so the conditionality of the 5.3x is visible rather than implied.
validation_steps.pass_criterion: dx from B and C is BIT-IDENTICAL to A (bit-identity is the strongest possible acceptance test and is available here by construction, because every post-convergence kernel already gates on the device latch) AND the committed state hash is equal AND arm C shows hot_dtoh_copies == 0 with positive_dtoh_copies > 0 (arm B is expected to FAIL this, which is the point) AND arm C's launches-per-step is strictly lower than A's. Any throughput claim must be reported as wall per COMMITTED physical second with the accept ratio attached, never as ms/step.
validation_steps.negative_control: (a) Pin the device latch to always-active and confirm the early exit never fires and the iteration count equals the full budget - proving no spurious break. (b) Inject a NaN into the force array mid-loop and confirm the non-finite guard still latches, the loop exits, and the outer step is REJECTED - inside the captured graph as well as outside; a fixed-iteration-count unconditional capture must be shown to FAIL this control, which is the documented reason unconditional capture is forbidden. (c) Deliberately perturb one kernel's operand order and confirm the bit-identity comparison FAILS - proving the identity test is sensitive rather than trivially true. (d) Re-run arm A after rm -rf of the Warp kernel cache and confirm the same result, closing off the project's documented stale-cache false-positive.

validation_steps.step: S2 - FIX2 native A/B on residual-reduction-per-unit-wall, at TWO mesh resolutions, against the honest baseline (MG OFF)
validation_steps.what_is_measured: Per-outer residual reduction factor rho = max|PF|_{k+1} / max|PF|_k for three arms (MG off incumbent; MG with full-fine coarse applies; MG with assembled per-fiber coarse) at two mesh resolutions; wall per decade of residual reduction; the converged outer state; the preconditioner's minimum eigenvalue; full-fine applies per V-cycle.
validation_steps.protocol: Reuse the ac_cortex_mesh_ab.py thin-wrapper pattern (no new physics; drive existing drivers with different flags). Run all three arms at the medium and the fine cortex mesh. Because FIX2 DROPS the inter-fiber crosslink off-diagonal and the inextensibility projector from arclength levels >= 1, it is NOT bit-identical and must not be tested as if it were; the correct object is the reduction factor and the converged fixed point.
validation_steps.pass_criterion: (i) rho(FIX2) <= rho(full-fine V-cycle) within the measured run-to-run spread, AND rho is h-INDEPENDENT: rho at the two mesh resolutions agrees within that spread (grid-invariance - the criterion that makes a multigrid claim a multigrid claim, and it needs no physiological magnitude). (ii) wall per decade of residual reduction is strictly lower than BOTH the full-fine V-cycle AND the MG-off incumbent - the incumbent is the real baseline and it is currently 2.6x faster in wall at the fine mesh, so 'better than unfixed MG' is not a pass. (iii) SPD preserved: minimum eigenvalue of the preconditioner > 0 (the existing CPU Lanczos rig, test_fiber_arclength_vcycle.py:343,408). (iv) The converged outer state matches the MG-off arm within the outer convergence tolerance, i.e. the preconditioner did not move the fixed point. If (i)-(iv) do not all hold, FIX2 stays OFF and the negative is recorded - the project's own §11.3 go/no-go discipline is what saved it weeks on deflated PCG.
validation_steps.negative_control: Run FIX2 with the fiber-quotient coarsest level DISABLED. FIX2's whole justification is that the inter-fiber coupling it drops from the arclength levels is recovered additively by that coarsest level; with it off, nothing spans inter-fiber coupling, so rho MUST degrade measurably. If rho is unchanged, the A/B is insensitive to exactly what FIX2 removes and the gate is VACUOUS - this is the direct analogue of the gate that compared largest-fragment to 2nd-largest and could not fail. Second control: run the FIX2 arm at a third, coarser mesh and confirm the h-independence claim can actually break (a two-point 'h-independence' check with only two points is weak evidence).

validation_steps.step: S3 - ENSEMBLE batching of independent realizations: prove exact block-diagonality first, then measure the utilisation scaling
validation_steps.what_is_measured: Aggregate accepted-step throughput T(R) (committed physical seconds per wall hour summed over R concurrent realizations) for R in {1,2,4,8,...} up to the memory limit; per-realization bit-identity vs the standalone R=1 run at the same seed; peak HBM vs R (NVML); per-kernel occupancy vs R (does the 70,686-thread projector launch become R x 70,686 and fill the machine?); cross-block force leakage.
validation_steps.protocol: Two variants, measured separately because they exercise different hardware limits. Variant A: one process, R independent cells on R Warp streams (wp.ScopedStream) - tests latency hiding. Variant B: one process, R cells concatenated into ONE index-blocked array set so each kernel launch has R x the threads - tests occupancy directly, and is the variant the project already has an exactness precedent for (disjoint index blocks -> identical per-realization result, ENGINE_ACCELERATION_PLAN FF P1). For variant B every shared structure must be audited for accidental coupling: one HashGrid per block (never shared), per-block reduction scalars (never a global dot), per-block regularizer (never a global max), per-block accept predicate and per-block ledger. Run at the full native baseline; never reduce a biological density to raise R.
validation_steps.pass_criterion: GATE 1 (exactness, and it gates everything else): for every R, each realization's committed post-step state is BYTE-IDENTICAL to that realization run standalone at the same seed. GATE 2 (no implicit weld): displace realization 0's nodes by a finite amount, re-evaluate, and assert realization 1's force array is BYTE-IDENTICAL to before - this is the merged-array block-diagonal test the project already owns, run in the direction where block-diagonality is the DESIRED property instead of the bug. GATE 3 (scaling, a scaling criterion not a magnitude): T(R)/T(1) is > 1 and monotone increasing up to the memory limit; report the exponent. GATE 4: peak HBM is measured (NVML, not estimated) and R is chosen by that measurement. If T(2)/T(1) is within noise of 1.0, the 'a single native cortex already saturates the A5000' assertion is CONFIRMED, ensemble batching is closed as an honest negative, and R3/R4 become the only levers - that outcome must be recorded as loudly as a success.
validation_steps.negative_control: Deliberately SHARE one hash grid (or one global reduction scalar) across the concatenated block and confirm GATE 2 FAILS - i.e. reproduce the co-location-is-not-connection bug on purpose and show the gate catches it. If GATE 2 passes with a deliberately shared grid, the gate is measuring nothing. Second control: run R=2 with identical seeds for both blocks and confirm the two blocks are byte-identical to each other (symmetry), then with different seeds and confirm they differ (non-vacuity). Third control: run R=2 where block 1 is given a poisoned NaN force and confirm ONLY block 1's outer step is rejected - the accept predicate must not be global across realizations.

validation_steps.step: S4 - Per-fiber kernel memory-layout coalescing (bit-identical), targeting the two projector applies per operator apply
validation_steps.what_is_measured: Kernel time and achieved bandwidth of project_constraint_forces_kernel and apply_fiber_block_preconditioner_kernel before/after; bit-identity of their outputs; achieved occupancy; the resulting change in wall per committed physical second.
validation_steps.protocol: Add a segment-major mirror layout (index k*n_fibers + f instead of fiber-contiguous a+k) for the per-fiber WORK arrays and the gathered pos/force operands, so that at each of the p Thomas steps adjacent threads touch adjacent addresses. The per-thread ARITHMETIC ORDER is unchanged (same Thomas sweep, same operand order, same rounding), so the output must be bit-identical - which is what makes this the safest structural optimisation available. Measure with the S0 per-kernel profiler. If the win does not materialise, revert and record the honest negative in the same file as a do-not-retry note (the project's established practice).
validation_steps.pass_criterion: Projected output BIT-IDENTICAL to the fiber-contiguous version for every node, at the full native population AND at the fine mesh (so the claim is not resolution-specific), AND the measured kernel time strictly decreases, AND achieved bandwidth as a fraction of peak strictly increases (proving the mechanism claimed is the mechanism that acted, rather than an unrelated timing shift).
validation_steps.negative_control: Run the transposed kernel with a deliberately wrong stride and confirm the bit-identity test FAILS (proving the identity test can detect a layout error, which is the entire risk of this change). Second control: also time an arm with the transposed layout but the SAME uncoalesced access pattern (transpose the storage, keep the strided reads) and confirm it does NOT speed up - this separates 'coalescing helped' from 'I accidentally changed the arithmetic or the cache footprint'.

validation_steps.step: S5 - CUDA graph capture of the transaction fan-out and the inner loop, with mandatory capture invalidation on topology change
validation_steps.what_is_measured: Launches per step, wall per committed physical second, bit-identity of the committed state, whether the divergence / non-finite / rollback guards still fire from inside a replayed graph, and whether a graph is correctly invalidated and rebuilt when a kinetic event changes topology (bond counts, bound-head counts, clutch counts).
validation_steps.protocol: Capture in two nested scopes: (a) the CG iteration body via wp.capture_while(self.active, body) - the condition array is the existing device latch, so the loop count stays data-dependent; (b) the transaction's snapshot/propose/accumulate/rollback/commit fan-out, which is already device-resident with an in-device branch select (transaction.py) and therefore is a natural fixed launch sequence. Every array the graph touches must be preallocated and stable; no allocation, no HashGrid.build, no .numpy() inside the captured region (the grid build already sits outside the CG loop - verified at implicit_mechanics.py:1732-1737 which consumes a prebuilt steric.grid.id). Register a topology epoch counter; any change invalidates and rebuilds the graph.
validation_steps.pass_criterion: Committed state BIT-IDENTICAL to the uncaptured path AND launches per step strictly reduced AND all three guards demonstrably fire from inside the replayed graph AND the graph is provably rebuilt after a topology change (epoch counter increments, capture handle differs). Report wp.is_conditional_graph_supported() and the CUDA/driver version in the artifact; if False on the A5000, the CG-loop half is BLOCKED and only the transaction fan-out is capturable.
validation_steps.negative_control: (a) Disable capture invalidation, force a kinetic bind/unbind that changes bond count, replay the stale graph, and confirm the bit-identity test FAILS - proving the invalidation test is load-bearing and the failure mode (a graph replaying on stale topology) is detectable rather than silent. (b) Capture with a FIXED iteration count (no conditional node), inject a NaN, and confirm the divergence guard does NOT fire - documenting, by measurement, exactly why the 2026-07-07 dead-end entry was right about unconditional capture and why conditional capture is a different thing. (c) Confirm a same-seed uncaptured re-run is bit-identical to itself first, so any captured-vs-uncaptured difference cannot be blamed on run-to-run nondeterminism.

validation_steps.step: S6 - Mixed precision, PRECONDITIONER ONLY, with the force path and the accept predicate proven untouched
validation_steps.what_is_measured: Converged dx difference vs the f64-preconditioner run (relative to the linear-solve tolerance, not bit-identity - a different preconditioner legitimately changes the iterate path); CG iteration count; the f32 preconditioner's minimum eigenvalue; and critically the adjoint/Newton-third-law ledger residual |sum(reaction) + sum(traction)| that the accept predicate consumes.
validation_steps.protocol: Cast ONLY the preconditioner apply (Jacobi diagonal, per-fiber Cholesky block, MG smoother/coarse applies) to f32, keeping positions, forces, the operator apply, the projector, the ledger, and the accept predicate in f64 - a standard mixed-precision inner/outer refinement. Nothing in the force path changes, so the ledger residual must be byte-identical, and that byte-identity is the gate that protects the accept predicate. Measure with the S0 profiler to confirm the precondition fraction is actually large enough to be worth it before doing the work.
validation_steps.pass_criterion: (i) The ledger residual |sum(reaction) + sum(traction)| is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the f64-preconditioner run (a conservation criterion; nothing in the force path changed, so anything else means the change leaked out of the preconditioner). (ii) The converged dx agrees with the f64-preconditioner run to within the linear-solve tolerance the solver already contracts. (iii) Iteration count is not increased beyond the measured run-to-run spread. (iv) The f32 preconditioner is still SPD (min eigenvalue > 0). (v) The accept/reject DECISION is identical on every outer step.
validation_steps.negative_control: Cast the FORCE accumulation (not the preconditioner) to f32 and confirm criterion (i) FAILS - i.e. demonstrate that the gate detects a precision reduction that touches the load path and therefore the near-cancelling Newton-third-law sum. This is the single most important negative control in the track: the accept predicate is a difference of large opposing forces, which is precisely where f32 truncation would silently start accepting unbalanced steps. Second control: cast only the hash-grid index (already f32 in-tree) and confirm criterion (i) still passes, establishing that the gate distinguishes pruning-only precision from load-path precision.

validation_steps.step: S7 - The step-count axis: dt convergence plateau + accept-ratio accounting (probably the largest single-run lever, and the one that is a physics change)
validation_steps.what_is_measured: A chosen mechanical observable's dependence on dt_phys under successive halving; the accept ratio (accepted / attempted outer steps) and the wall consumed by rolled-back steps; inner iterations-to-convergence vs the fixed budget; and wall per committed physical second at each dt.
validation_steps.protocol: dt-refinement study at the full native baseline: dt, dt/2, dt/4 (and dt*2), holding everything else fixed. Report the observable and the accept ratio at each. Separately instrument rejected-step waste: an outer step that rolls back consumes wall and commits zero physical time (measured: 171.9 s of outer step committing 0.0 s). Do NOT change the inner iteration budget as a speed measure without reporting the residual actually achieved.
validation_steps.pass_criterion: The observable CONVERGES under refinement: successive-halving differences shrink monotonically and the production dt sits on the converged plateau (a convergence-order / grid-invariance-in-time criterion, evaluable with no physiological magnitude and no literature band). Any dt selected must be justified by lying on that plateau, never by being fast - a dt chosen for speed is a magic number. Additionally: any throughput improvement claim must be reported jointly with (a) the residual actually achieved and (b) the accept ratio; a throughput gain accompanied by a degraded accept ratio or a worse achieved residual is recorded as a REGRESSION, not a win.
validation_steps.negative_control: Deliberately run at a dt above the plateau and confirm the study detects it (the observable moves outside the plateau band) - proving the refinement study is sensitive rather than flat by construction. Second control: artificially cap the inner iteration budget to a small number, confirm wall per step drops sharply AND that the paired residual/accept-ratio reporting flags it as a regression - i.e. demonstrate that the gate cannot be passed by silently loosening convergence, which is the most likely way speed work fakes success.

validation_steps.step: S8 - Surrogate / SBI path with a MECHANICAL 'surrogate explores, native decides' firewall
validation_steps.what_is_measured: Simulation-based-calibration (SBC) rank-histogram uniformity of the trained posterior estimator; held-out native predictive coverage (do held-out native runs fall inside the surrogate's stated credible intervals at the nominal rate?); provenance-tag completeness of every number in every emitted artifact; and the static import firewall's verdict.
validation_steps.protocol: Train an emulator / neural posterior estimator on a few hundred native runs (parameters -> summary observables), used ONLY to propose candidate parameter regions. Enforce the discipline with three mechanisms, not intention: (1) PACKAGE FIREWALL - the surrogate lives in a new top-level package (e.g. ffn_sim/sweep/surrogate/) and an AST-based static test forbids any import of it from ac/, ff/, dcm/, mirroring tests/ac/test_warp_only_contract.py:19-60 exactly as validation/oracles/ is already forbidden from runtime paths. (2) PROVENANCE GATE - every emitted number carries evidence_source in {NATIVE_RUN, SURROGATE, COARSE} plus a run id and config hash; a new verify_provenance.py (sibling of verify_forces.py, reusing its DRIFT verdict machinery) makes it a BLOCKING finding for any artifact under outputs/**/production/ to contain a number whose provenance is not NATIVE_RUN with a resolvable run id. (3) CONFIRMATION RULE - every reported posterior mode and every credible-region boundary must be re-run natively at that point, and the native-vs-surrogate discrepancy must lie inside the surrogate's own predictive uncertainty; a discrepancy outside it invalidates the surrogate and forces retraining, never a reinterpretation of the native result.
validation_steps.pass_criterion: (i) SBC ranks are uniform against a pre-registered test at a pre-registered level (a distributional/symmetry criterion needing zero physiological magnitudes). (ii) Held-out native runs fall inside the surrogate's stated intervals at the nominal coverage rate. (iii) The static import firewall test passes. (iv) verify_provenance reports zero blocking findings across all production artifacts. (v) Every reported posterior point has a matching native confirmation run id. Note explicitly: the surrogate's speedup is on EVALUATION COUNT only; native decision latency is unchanged, which is why S3/S7 remain necessary rather than optional.
validation_steps.negative_control: (a) Train on SHUFFLED parameter-observable pairs and confirm SBC uniformity FAILS - proving the calibration test can reject a bad surrogate rather than rubber-stamping any flow. (b) Plant a SURROGATE-tagged number inside a production artifact and confirm the provenance gate emits a blocking finding (extend the existing _inject_defects self-test at verify_forces.py:384 rather than writing new machinery). (c) Add 'import ffn_sim.sweep.surrogate' to a scratch module under ac/ and confirm the firewall test FAILS. (d) Feed the confirmation rule a deliberately biased surrogate (trained on a restricted parameter slab) and confirm the native-vs-surrogate discrepancy check fires - this is the mechanical version of the six documented coarse-contradicted-by-native episodes, turned into a test.

validation_steps.step: S9 - Hardware / multi-GPU throughput decision, measured rather than assumed
validation_steps.what_is_measured: Aggregate accepted-step throughput per GPU-hour on the A5000 vs one FP64-class GPU (A100/H100 class) on byte-identical inputs; achieved fraction of each device's f64 and bandwidth roofs (the S0 profile re-run per device); peak HBM and the maximum ensemble R per device; and the accept/reject decision equality across devices.
validation_steps.protocol: Rent/borrow one FP64-class GPU for a bounded benchmark. Run the identical native baseline with the identical config hash. Cross-device bit-identity must NOT be expected (different reduction orders / different SM counts change floating-point summation order), so compare on the solver's own tolerance and on the accept/reject decision instead. Re-run the S0 roofline per device so the question 'is this solver f64-ALU-bound?' is answered by two points on the f64-rate axis rather than by architecture folklore.
validation_steps.pass_criterion: Same accept/reject decision on every outer step on both devices AND the converged observable agrees within the solver's convergence tolerance on both devices. Throughput and achieved-fraction-of-peak are RECORDED, not gated - this step exists to hand the PI a measured number for a procurement decision, and its pass criterion is only that the comparison is valid (same inputs, same config hash, same tolerance, no silent config drift).
validation_steps.negative_control: First establish that a same-device repeat run is BIT-IDENTICAL to itself; only then is a cross-device difference attributable to reduction order rather than to a bug or a config drift. Second control: deliberately change one config value between devices and confirm the config-hash comparison catches it - guarding against the failure where an environment difference is mistaken for a hardware speedup.

ffn_sim/references/analysis/25_simulation-based-inference-of-cell-migration-dynamics-in-com.md — in-tree, KB-registered SBI methods reference (NPE: 32,100 sims, NRMSE 0.20, ~1 s amortized inference vs ABC 66k-432k sims). Use as the design citation for S8 rather than sourcing anew.
new_code_needed: Per-kernel roofline instrumentation: a wp.TIMING_KERNEL wrapper around the operator/precondition/transaction scopes, plus a REVIEWABLE per-kernel bytes-and-f64-FLOP table derived from each launch's dim and argument arrays (one literal entry per kernel, hand-derivable, never fitted or calibrated), plus achieved-fraction-of-peak and occupancy reporting. Must emit the closure identity (sum of per-kernel times vs stage wall).

A throughput accounting module: committed physical seconds per wall hour, accept ratio, wall consumed by rolled-back outer steps, and inner-iterations-to-convergence vs budget. This replaces ms/step and steps/s as the reported metric everywhere in the track (the measured probe committed 0.0 s in 182 s, so ms/step is provably the wrong metric here).

Conditional-graph CG loop: re-express the ProjectedAnalyticCG iteration body as a wp.capture_while(self.active, body) callback, with the existing _cg_finalize_kernel updating the device latch. Includes a graph-invalidation epoch keyed to topology (bond/head/clutch counts) and a capture-scope audit asserting no allocation, no HashGrid.build, and no .numpy() inside the captured region.

Ensemble execution backend behind the existing EnsembleRunner interface: (A) a stream-parallel driver (wp.ScopedStream, R independent cells) and (B) an index-blocked concatenated driver (one launch of R x dim). B needs a per-block isolation audit and, critically, per-block HashGrid, per-block reduction scalars, per-block regularizer, per-block accept predicate and per-block ledger — the concatenation must be provably block-diagonal, not a shared array set.

The block-diagonality gate itself: a reusable 'perturb block i, assert block j byte-identical' harness. This is the merged-array/co-location test run in the direction where block-diagonality is desired; it should be a permanent test, not a one-off script, because every future batching change can silently break it.

Segment-major mirror layout for the per-fiber Thomas work arrays and gathered operands (project_constraint_forces_kernel, apply_fiber_block_preconditioner_kernel), preserving per-thread arithmetic order so the output stays bit-identical. Includes the wrong-stride negative-control fixture.

f32 preconditioner-apply variants of the Jacobi diagonal, the per-fiber Cholesky block and the MG smoother/coarse applies, behind a flag, with the force path / positions / operator / projector / ledger / accept predicate strictly f64. Includes the 'f32 force accumulation must FAIL the ledger byte-identity gate' negative-control fixture.

dt-refinement harness: run the full native baseline at dt, dt/2, dt/4, dt*2 and report the observable, the accept ratio, the achieved residual and the wall per committed physical second per dt, with the plateau determination explicit.

ffn_sim/sweep/ (new top-level package, deliberately OUTSIDE ac/ff/dcm): a native run registry (config hash -> run id -> artifact path), a work queue for multi-GPU/multi-host fan-out, and ffn_sim/sweep/surrogate/ for the emulator/NPE. Plus SBC and held-out-coverage diagnostics.

verify_provenance.py: sibling of verify_forces.py reusing its DRIFT verdict machinery. Every number in an emitted artifact carries evidence_source in {NATIVE_RUN, SURROGATE, COARSE} + run id + config hash; any production artifact number that is not NATIVE_RUN with a resolvable run id is a BLOCKING finding. Ships with an _inject_defects-style self-test.
tests/ac/test_surrogate_firewall_contract.py: AST clone of test_warp_only_contract.py forbidding any import of ffn_sim.sweep.surrogate from ac/, ff/, dcm/.

A Warp-kernel-cache hygiene step in every A/B protocol (rm -rf ~/.cache/warp/<ver> per arm), because the project has a documented stale-cache 'byte-identical' false positive that would silently validate a no-op change.
observables_missing: Per-kernel time inside the operator apply and the preconditioner apply. wp.timing_begin is used at exactly two sites in the repo and both pass TIMING_MEMCPY; TIMING_KERNEL appears nowhere. 88.8% of the native step is currently an undifferentiated block called 'CG'. Nothing else in this track is decidable without it.

Achieved memory bandwidth and achieved f64 FLOP rate as a fraction of the device peaks. The verdict 'this operator is memory-bandwidth-bound' (FF_SINGLE_CELL_OPTIMIZATION_PLAN §0.8) has never been measured against a roofline; my arithmetic suggests ~15% of BOTH roofs, which would mean latency/occupancy-bound instead — and that inverts the whole strategy.
Achieved occupancy per kernel, specifically for the 70,686-thread one-thread-per-fiber launches on a 64-SM part. This is the number that decides whether ensemble batching can fill the machine.

Committed physical seconds per wall hour, and the accept ratio. Today there is no metric that distinguishes 'fast' from 'fast at producing rolled-back steps'; the one committed native probe spent 171.9 s to commit 0.0 s.

Distribution of CG iterations-to-latch per outer step. Without it, FIX1's '5.3x' cannot be told apart from '1x on the production path', because whether the loop converges inside its budget is exactly what determines the win.
Launches per step (kernel launch count). Needed to size graph capture honestly; the MG path's launch count is expected to be an order above the incumbent's, which is where capture would pay.

Per-outer residual reduction factor rho as a first-class logged quantity at two mesh resolutions. It exists only as a max|PF| trace today; the h-independence claim that justifies multigrid needs rho itself.

Peak HBM per cell for the ac/ stack at the native baseline. The 84-132 MB figures are the ff/ engine; the ac stack adds membrane (40,962 nodes), nucleus (642), and myosin (15,028 particles), and the only in-tree ac figure is an explicit estimate ('order 3-6 GB for the fine full stack ... VERIFY empirically; this is an estimate, not a measured peak').
Cross-block force leakage in a batched configuration (currently unmeasurable because no batched configuration exists).

Provenance of every emitted number (native vs surrogate vs coarse). There is a forces-manifest declared-path gate for CONFIG values but nothing that tags a RESULT with the run that produced it — which is the mechanism the six coarse-contradicted-by-native episodes needed and lacked.

wp.is_conditional_graph_supported() on the A5000, plus its CUDA/driver version. Unknown today (False on this Mac only because the build has no CUDA); it gates the S1/S5 conditional-graph line entirely.
connectors_involved: NONE. Track 11 makes no connector force-real — it is the only track in the programme whose correct output is that every connector behaves EXACTLY as before, ideally bit-identically. Stated positively, its contract is: the accepted-step transaction's device-resident predicate, the Newton-third-law adjoint ledger, and the disjoint-population invariant must all survive every optimisation unchanged.

The connectors this track can most plausibly BREAK, and must therefore gate against, are the force-real ones whose runtimes I verified present as code: membrane_erm_cortex (ac/engine/erm_cortex_connector.py, erm_cortex_slice.py), nmii_cortex_motor (ac/engine/cortex_motor_slice.py), nmii_sf_motor (ac/engine/sf_motor_slice.py), the LINC family actin_cap_linc / mt_nucleus_linc / if_nucleus_linc (ac/engine/linc_connector.py), integrin_collagen_clutch + ecm_crosslink + ecm_far_field_anchor + membrane_ecm_contact (ac/engine/ecm_world.py, which already runs a multi-participant accepted-step transaction), surface_porous_transfer / monomer flux (ac/engine/monomer_flux.py, cytosol_connected.py), and dorsal_arc_crosslink (ac/engine/sf_population.py).

Two specific mechanisms by which speed work would break them, both gated above: (1) any precision reduction or reordering in the FORCE accumulation attacks the near-cancelling |sum(reaction) + sum(traction)| that every bidirectional+adjoint connector is validated by — hence S6's byte-identity criterion on the ledger residual and its f32-force negative control; (2) ensemble concatenation into shared arrays would re-create co-location-as-implicit-connection ACROSS CELLS (a shared hash grid means cell A's turgor silently loads cell B) — hence S3's GATE 2 and its deliberately-shared-grid negative control.
dependencies: S0 (the profiler + throughput observable) has NO dependencies and should land now, ahead of every other track's optimisation work. It is measurement-only, it changes no physics, and every speedup estimate in this document is currently un-decidable without it. Recommend landing it during the assembly tracks so that when assembly closes there is already a per-kernel baseline to optimise against rather than a cold start.

Everything from S1 onward depends on the compartment-standalone and connector-wiring tracks landing first, for a hard reason and not a stylistic one: optimising a step whose composition still changes means every measured baseline is invalidated by the next connector, and 'bit-identical' loses its meaning when the reference binary keeps changing. The PI's ordering (assemble, then optimise) is also the technically correct ordering.

S1/S2/S5 depend on the cortex solver being the settled inner solve. The fine-mesh plateau these were built for turned out to be an overlap_free WCA-relaxation kink, not a solver problem (CORTEX_KINK_AUDIT_2026-07-25.md: 3.42 -> 0.13 with smooth arcs), and the PI-gated smoothness-preserving overlap fix is still awaiting ratification. If that fix changes the operating point, S2's A/B must be re-run — so S2 should wait on it.

S3 (ensemble) depends on the baseline configuration track defining ONE canonical adherent-on-2D-collagen native config, because a batched throughput number is only meaningful against a fixed config hash. It also depends on S0 for the occupancy measurement that decides whether batching can win at all.

S6 (mixed precision) depends on S0 showing the precondition fraction is large enough to matter — the ff profile shows precondition folded inside the 88.8% CG block, so its own share is currently unknown, and doing the work before knowing it is the exact mistake the matrix-free rewrite made (attacking an 8.8% stage with an Amdahl ceiling of 1.12x).

S7 (dt axis) depends on the accepted-step transaction being live for the full composed cell, because the accept ratio is meaningless without it, and on the physiological-baseline configuration, because a dt plateau measured from an unphysical baseline is a plateau of the wrong problem.

S8 (surrogate) depends on S0/S3/S7 delivering enough native throughput to produce the few hundred training runs at all — at today's measured 172 s per outer step, generating a training set is itself infeasible. The surrogate is therefore LAST in execution order despite being the largest multiplier: it cannot bootstrap itself.

S9 (hardware) depends only on S0, since the roofline profile per device IS the measurement that justifies or refutes the purchase. It is otherwise independent and can run in parallel with the assembly tracks.
result.viz:
"Three renders, all browser-verified via scripts/browser_check.py (never by grepping the HTML), all at full native resolution with no downsampling.

(1) ISOLATION — the DIFFERENCE render, which is the only render that can catch a speed bug. For every optimisation arm, render the assembled cell colored by per-node |Delta position| and per-node |Delta force| between the baseline arm and the optimised arm, on the same colour scale, with the scale bar shown and never truncated. For a bit-identical optimisation (FIX1-as-capture_while, S4 layout transpose, S3 ensemble blocks, S5 graph capture) this field must be IDENTICALLY ZERO everywhere, and the render's real gate is that the dumped state hashes are equal — the picture is the human-legible confirmation of a hash equality, which is what makes it a checkpoint rather than a garnish. For a non-bit-identical arm (S2 FIX2, S6 f32 preconditioner, S7 dt change) the difference field must be spatially STRUCTURELESS and below the solver tolerance; a difference field with visible spatial structure (a hot band at the substrate contact, a hot patch at a steric crossing, a hot ring at a compartment seam) means the optimisation is not preconditioner-only or not tolerance-bounded, and that is exactly the class of bug the project's own steric-hotspot and plateau-localization renders caught by eye after bands missed it.

(2) ISOLATION — the ensemble block-isolation scene. Render R concurrent realizations side by side from ONE batched run, each colored by per-node force, plus a cross-block difference panel showing |Delta force| in block j after block i is displaced. That panel must be identically zero. This is the visual form of the merged-array failure (494,802 nodes where the cortex moved 39.8 nm and the MT aster and nucleus moved 0.0 nm and looked coupled) run in the direction where block-diagonality is the desired property — the same picture that would have exposed the original bug now certifies the batching.

(3) CUMULATIVE — refresh the composed-cell scene via ffn_sim/scripts/ac_cell_assembled_viz.py from the OPTIMISED binary and browser-check it. For a bit-identical optimisation the dump must be byte-identical to the baseline dump, so this refresh is a hash assertion with a visual witness. Alongside it, a throughput panel that reports the metrics that actually matter and no others: committed physical seconds per wall hour (not steps/s, not ms/step), accepted vs rolled-back outer steps as a stacked bar, achieved residual per arm, and the per-kernel time breakdown with the closure identity (sum of kernel times vs stage wall) printed on the figure so a non-closing profile is visible in the figure itself. Every arm's panel must state the config hash, the GPU, the Warp version, wp.is_conditional_graph_supported(), and a BLOCKED banner on every quantitative physiological claim, since no magnitude is being closed anywhere in this track."
risks: THE HEADLINE TRAP — reporting the in-tree '40x' as a production speedup. It is 40x fewer full-fine operator APPLIES relative to the UNFIXED MG path (commit 09c14eb8: 'Full-fine applies/V-cycle 27-43 -> constant 4'). The only native wall A/B in the tree says MG+FIX1+FIX2 takes 1463 s where the MG-off incumbent takes 568 s for the same 40 outers at the fine mesh — the fixed MG path is 2.6x SLOWER in wall than the production default. Reporting '40x landed' would be the eighth documented instance of a metric measuring something other than its name. Mitigation: the only reportable throughput metric in this track is committed physical seconds per wall hour against the MG-OFF incumbent baseline.

FIX1's 5.3x is conditional and currently near-worthless on the production path. It is a CPU-microbench iteration-count ratio (12 of 64 iterations used) and only pays when the linear solve converges inside its budget; the production path exhausts its budget (inner_iters = 400 = budget, inner_converged = False; ff measures 181-210 CG iters at max). Enabling it and reporting the microbench number as the native win would be a coarse-configuration conclusion — the seventh such episode.

FIX1 as written violates an existing hard gate. `int(self.active.numpy()[0])` at implicit_mechanics.py:2078-2080 is a DtoH copy inside the physical-time loop; driver.py:1201 requires hot_dtoh_copies == 0. Shipping it as default either fails the gate or requires someone to quietly weaken the gate — which is gate-loosening. Mitigation: implement it as wp.capture_while so the skip is device-side and the gate passes unchanged.

LOAD-PATH-SUMS-TO-ZERO, the highest-severity risk in this track. The accept predicate is |sum(reaction) + sum(traction)|^2 <= tol^2 — a near-cancellation of large opposing forces. ANY precision reduction, reordering, fusion, or reduction-tree change in the force path can shrink or inflate that residual without changing any single force visibly, so a speed change could silently start ACCEPTING unbalanced steps. A cell whose connectors each look right edge-by-edge and whose global balance is quietly broken is exactly the crawl failure (isotropic radial traction cancelling laterally, F_net one quarter of one clutch) with the diagnostic removed. Mitigation: force path, positions, operator, projector, ledger and predicate stay f64 forever; the ledger residual's BYTE-identity is a gate; and S6's negative control proves the gate detects an f32 force path.

ENSEMBLE CONCATENATION RE-CREATES CO-LOCATION-AS-CONNECTION, across cells. One shared HashGrid, one global reduction scalar, one global regularizer max, or one shared accept predicate across the concatenated block means cell A mechanically loads cell B while every per-cell diagnostic still looks sane — the merged-array block-diagonal failure inverted (there, co-location looked like coupling and was not; here, concatenation would be coupling and would not look like it). Mitigation: S3 GATE 2 perturb-block-i-assert-block-j-byte-identical as a permanent test, with the deliberately-shared-grid negative control proving the gate is live.

SPEED WORK FAKING SUCCESS BY LOOSENING CONVERGENCE. Capping inner iterations, raising the CG tolerance, cutting outer retries, or accepting a step that should roll back all make throughput look better while committing worse physics — and the measured baseline is ALREADY budget-exhausted and non-converged, so there is enormous room to look faster by converging less. Mitigation: every throughput number is reported jointly with the achieved residual and the accept ratio; a throughput gain with a degraded residual or accept ratio is recorded as a REGRESSION.

CUDA-GRAPH STALE-STATE. A captured graph holds pointers and launch dims; a kinetic bind/unbind that changes bond, head, or clutch counts makes a replayed graph either operate on stale topology or read freed memory — and it will do so SILENTLY at full speed. Mitigation: a topology epoch that invalidates the capture, with the negative control that disabling invalidation must break bit-identity.

WARP KERNEL-CACHE STALENESS PRODUCING A FALSE 'BIT-IDENTICAL'. The project has a documented instance where an edited @wp.kernel produced a byte-identical native result because the old cached kernel was reused — i.e. the strongest acceptance test in this track can be passed by a change that never ran. Mitigation: rm -rf ~/.cache/warp/<ver> per arm, recorded in the protocol.

MEASURING THE WRONG THING AT THE TOP LEVEL: ms/step and steps/s are both wrong here, provably. The one committed native probe spent 171.89 s on an outer step that was rolled back and committed 0.0 s of physical time. A 2x improvement in ms/step on a run whose accept ratio is zero is a 2x improvement in producing nothing.

THE ROOFLINE VERDICT MAY BE WRONG IN EITHER DIRECTION, AND THE STRATEGY DEPENDS ON IT. If the operator really is bandwidth-bound (the current in-tree assertion), then ensemble batching, coalescing and graph capture are all near-futile and the only levers are step-count and hardware bandwidth. If it is latency/occupancy-bound (my unmeasured arithmetic: ~15% of both roofs), the opposite. Committing engineering effort before S0 lands is precisely the mistake that cost weeks on the matrix-free rewrite (Amdahl-capped at 1.12x) and the deflated PCG (wall break-even).

SURROGATE LEAKAGE. A surrogate-derived number entering a REPORT.md, then being cited downstream as evidence, then anchoring a parameter — with six documented precedents of coarse conclusions later contradicted natively. Intention is not a control here. Mitigation: package-level AST import firewall + a provenance gate that blocks any production number lacking a native run id, both with defect-injection self-tests.

SURROGATE MIS-CALIBRATION THAT LOOKS LIKE A RESULT. A normalizing-flow posterior can be sharp and confidently wrong; a tight credible interval reads as a strong inference. Mitigation: SBC rank uniformity as a hard gate, held-out native coverage at nominal rate, native confirmation of every reported posterior point, and the shuffled-labels negative control proving the calibration test can reject.

OPTIMISING A MOVING TARGET. Every connector added during the assembly tracks invalidates every baseline measured before it, and 'bit-identical' is meaningless against a reference that keeps changing. Mitigation: S0 now (measurement only), heavy optimisation after assembly closes, and a config hash stamped on every arm.

HARDWARE CONCLUSION FROM A CONFOUNDED COMPARISON. An A100-vs-A5000 benchmark differing in driver, Warp version, or one config value would credit the hardware for an environment difference. Mitigation: config-hash equality gate, same-device bit-identical self-repeat established first, and cross-device comparison on the solver tolerance and the accept/reject decision rather than on bit-identity.
open_questions_for_pi: HARDWARE — probably the single largest lever in this track and not mine to decide. The solver is f64 everywhere (verified: 215 float64 sites in implicit_mechanics.py alone; the only f32 is the pruning-only hash-grid index). The RTX A5000 is GA102, which runs f64 at 1/64 of f32 (~0.43 TFLOPS f64, 768 GB/s, 16 GB); an A100 runs f64 at 1/2 (~9.7 TFLOPS, 1555 GB/s, 40-80 GB). If S0 shows the operator is f64-ALU-bound, a device change is worth more than every algorithmic lever in this document combined; if it is latency/occupancy-bound, it is still worth the bandwidth and SM count and it multiplies the ensemble R by 2.5-5x on memory alone. Question: is the project willing to move off the A5000 for sweep production, and does the hard rule 'the answer to native memory pressure is larger or multi-GPU hardware' extend to THROUGHPUT pressure?

SWEEP BUDGET — without this number, 'fast enough' is undefined and no optimisation can ever be declared DONE. Please state the target: how many cell types x how many cell states x how many replicates x how many physical seconds per run x acceptable wall per sweep. From that I can compute the required speedup and say honestly which combination of levers reaches it and which does not. Today's measured point is 0.05 s physical per 172 s wall, so the gap is currently ~4-6 orders of magnitude and the answer will certainly involve the surrogate — but the required factor determines whether S3+S7 alone could suffice for a reduced first sweep.

IS A HOST READBACK USED ONLY FOR LOOP CONTROL — no state read, no state mutation, bit-identical result — a violation of the zero-authoritative-GPU-to-CPU-roundtrip rule? This single ruling decides whether FIX1 can ship as written or must be re-implemented as a conditional graph. I recommend ruling it a violation anyway, because the conditional-graph implementation is strictly better (same skip, zero readback, fewer launches, guards still device-resident) — but the ruling is yours.

FIX2 CHANGES THE PRECONDITIONER on a solve that does NOT converge. A preconditioner change cannot move a CONVERGED fixed point, which is the usual reason preconditioner changes need no gate. But the production path is budget-exhausted (inner_iters = 400 = budget, inner_converged = False), so the emitted state IS preconditioner-dependent. Question: is a preconditioner change that alters a non-converged trajectory a gate-contract change requiring PI sign-off? The same question applies to S6's f32 preconditioner and is the reason I did not rank it higher.

IS A NEURAL SURROGATE ADMISSIBLE AT ALL under the fine-grained-mechanistic hard rule? A learned emulator is the most abstracted, most lumped object imaginable in a project whose first architectural principle is to prefer the mechanistic option even at higher cost. My proposed reconciliation is that the surrogate is not a runtime and not a model — it is a SEARCH POLICY over which native runs to perform, mechanically firewalled (package-level AST import ban, provenance gate blocking any production number without a native run id, native confirmation of every reported posterior point). But 'the surrogate explores, native decides' is a policy that needs your explicit ratification, not my inference, because it is the one place this track brushes against the project's founding rule.

DOES 'CO-LOCATION IS NEVER A CONNECTION' FORBID ensemble concatenation of independent cells into shared array sets even with a proven byte-identity block-diagonality gate? The letter of the rule is about physical connection within one cell; the spirit is that shared storage must never imply mechanical coupling. My reading is that a gated concatenation is admissible precisely because the gate proves non-coupling, and that stream-parallel separate cells (variant A) is the conservative fallback. Your call on whether the gate is sufficient.

PRECEDENT QUESTION on reduced precision: ac/solid/steric_warp.py:9-11,48-51 already builds the steric hash grid on an f32 copy of the positions, documented as safe because the grid only prunes far pairs while the force math stays f64. Is that (a) an accepted precedent that legitimises pruning-only reduced precision generally, or (b) something that needs retroactive gating? The answer sets the boundary for S6.

MAY I LAND S0 (profiler + throughput observable) NOW, ahead of the assembly tracks? It changes no physics, adds no constants, and is measurement-only — but it edits ac/cell/driver.py, which is feature-frozen (instrumentation is explicitly allowed, so I believe yes). The reason to do it now rather than after assembly is that every speedup estimate in this document is currently undecidable, and building the baseline incrementally as compartments land is far cheaper than reconstructing it cold at the end.

WHICH OBSERVABLE anchors the S7 dt-convergence plateau? A dt study needs one quantity to converge, and choosing it myself risks choosing one that is insensitive to dt and therefore produces a flat, vacuous plateau. I would propose the accepted-step force-balance residual plus one mechanical observable of the adherent configuration, but the choice is a measurement-protocol decision with gate consequences.

result.summary: The track's skeleton is right and its reuse map is unusually accurate (I verified build_sf_arc_population(n_ventral=1,...) really does yield exactly 1 bundle / 2 antiparallel filaments / 1 motor station / barbed-outward, and that dropping n_dorsal/n_arc really does remove the Gershgorin wall — lambda_max 3684001 pN/um in the committed record is exactly 8x460000 alpha-actinin + 1000, so the pair lane is genuinely tractable). But roughly half the pass criteria are unfailable, three of the seventeen negative controls provably cannot flip the gate they are attached to, and four headline premises are false against the code: (1) M5's "the whole single-pair inner problem is a linear SPD system, the angle-harmonics are the only nonlinear terms" is inverted — bending is LINEAR (F = alpha*(a-2b+c), sf_mechanics.py:194) while the axial links (k*(L-r0)/L*d, sf_mechanics.py:181), the head arms (k*(|r|-r0)*rhat, minifilament_warp.py:66-77) and walk_dir(x) (refreshed from live positions every force evaluation, cortex_motor_slice.py:505) are the nonlinear ones, so the "exact rank-one tangent" is not exact and the dense host oracle solves a different system than the device; (2) M1's primary observable, the Dirichlet anchor reaction, is claimed "independent of the GAP k_axial" but for an end node with one link it IS k_axial*(L-r0) of that link — the same number the design condemns; (3) M6's energy ledger closes identically by path algebra for any path, converged or not, so its stated discriminator cannot work and the design's own anti-tautology rule would reject its own nominal ledger; (4) M4's "v/v0 -> 1.000 +/- 0.01 as k_ext -> 0" is arithmetically false at the project's own committed constants — the DERIVED stall cap binds 2.4x even at zero load (dt 10 ms vs the 4.17 ms threshold), ceiling 0.4167. Separately, the design's #1 risk (massive load-path cancellation) rests on a ~40x unit error: 3.8 heads per fiber-half x 0.0546 pN = 0.205 pN vs T_max 0.254 pN, i.e. the committed record shows essentially NO cancellation. And it converts the PI's already-asked magnets-vs-full-adhesion-circuit question back into an open question for PI while ff/substrate.py already provides the KB-anchored compliant boundary M4 proposes to build from scratch. Effort is ~2x optimistic (10.5 d claimed, ~21-23 d realistic) and no dt-convergence step exists anywhere despite the dominant observable being dt-clamped.
must_fix: M5's premise is false and its oracle is not an oracle. The design says 'the whole single-pair inner problem is a linear SPD system of only a few hundred DOF ... the angle-harmonics are the only nonlinear terms.' Inverted: ffn_sim/ac/engine/sf_mechanics.py:194 shows bending is F = alpha*(pos[a]-2pos[b]+pos[c]), a constant-coefficient LINEAR Laplacian; the NONLINEAR terms are the axial links (sf_mechanics.py:181, f = k*(L-r0)/L*d, with a geometric-stiffness term), the 320 head arms (ffn_sim/ac/motor/minifilament_warp.py:66-77, F = k*(|r|-r0)*rhat), and the crossbridge itself because walk_dir is recomputed from live segment positions inside every force evaluation (_refresh_bound_walk_dir_kernel launched at ffn_sim/ac/engine/cortex_motor_slice.py:505, i.e. inside accumulate_candidate, which the inner loop calls every iteration at ffn_sim/scripts/ac_gate_b_sf_motor_native.py:438-439). The driver's own docstring says so: 'The geometry is nonlinear (the pair tangent and the crossbridge walk direction depend on position)' (ac_gate_b_sf_motor_native.py:449-452). Consequence: 'K = k_xb*w w^T is EXACT for the r0bind force' is false (it omits d(walk_dir)/dx), and a host dense LINEAR solve cannot agree with the device to 1e-8 um because it is the equilibrium of a different residual. Fix: make M5 a host dense NEWTON solve of the full nonlinear residual (still trivial at ~150 DOF for one bundle at n_per_fiber=9: 2*9 SF nodes + 34 nmii particles = 52 nodes, minus 2 pins), and state that the rank-one tangent is a PRECONDITIONER, not the derivative.

M1's primary observable is the observable it condemned. The design demotes k_axial*(L-r0) ('METRIC MEASURING THE WRONG THING #1') and promotes the Dirichlet anchor reaction as 'definitionally the force the boundary supplies and is independent of the GAP k_axial'. But the pinned FA node is a fiber END node with exactly ONE axial link plus a bending triple; force balance makes its reaction equal to minus that link's tension, i.e. exactly k_axial*(L01-r0_01) — the same quantity _sf_axial_tension computes at ffn_sim/scripts/ac_gate_b_sf_motor_native.py:158-167. The 'upgrade' is a relabeling. The only genuinely k_axial-free transmitted-load observable is the inextensibility Lagrange multiplier the design itself raises in open_questions_for_pi #4 and then declines to adopt. Either adopt it or drop the independence claim.

M6's energy-ledger discriminator is mathematically impossible. With D defined as 'sum over inner iterations of F . dx measured along the ACTUAL displacement path' and W = sum(F_h*delta_abscissa_h), the closure is a PATH IDENTITY: for the total nodal force F, sum F.dx = -dU + W_motor along ANY path, converged or not, correct or not. So e = |W - (dU + D)|/W is ~0 always, the claimed discriminator ('if the solver is wrong the ledger does not close') is false, and the design's own rejection rule ('if e is flat in the budget, the ledger is tautological and must be rejected') would reject the nominal ledger. An independent U evaluator does not help because the tautology lives in D, not U. Fix: either drop the ledger, or replace D with a physically-defined dissipation against a real per-node drag gamma (which this slice does not model at all — sf_cytosol_transfer is excluded), and make the discriminator the RESIDUAL FORCE at the reported state, not energy closure.

M4's exact-limit criterion is false at the project's own constants. da_max = (f_stall - F)/k_xb (segment_motor.py:172, :223) with f_stall = 0.5 pN and k_xb = 1000 pN/um gives 0.50 nm/step, while tau*v0 with the driver default --dt 0.01 (ac_gate_b_sf_motor_native.py:284) and v0 = 0.12 um/s gives 1.20 nm. The cap binds by 2.4x AT ZERO LOAD, so the unloaded v/v0 ceiling is 0.4167, not 1.000 +/- 0.01. The cap is not a 'stall-crossing guard' — it is a per-step velocity clamp v_max = f_stall/(k_xb*tau) that overrides Hill for any dt > 4.17 ms, i.e. a lumped rate limiter sitting on top of the mechanistic Hill law. Either add dt < 4.17 ms as an explicit precondition of M4, or make the criterion v/v_eff where v_eff = min(v0, f_stall/(k_xb*tau)) and say so.

There is no dt-convergence step anywhere in M0-M10, and the dominant observable is dt-set. head_load_max in the committed record is 0.0546 pN; one capped step through the real series stiffness (k_xb 1000 in series with k_head_arm 100 = 90.91 pN/um) gives 90.91*5.0e-4 = 0.0455 pN. The measured per-head load is one clamped step's worth of series strain, not motor stall physics. Given the project's own history ('collapses = DT ARTIFACT'), a temporal-refinement rung is at least as mandatory as M7's spatial one. Add it before M4/M6.

M3's central identity is contaminated by a stale-r0_bind rotation artifact that the design never considers, and the artifact is larger than the signal. r0_bind is captured once at attach with the then-current walk_dir (segment_motor.py:452-455) while walk_dir is refreshed from live positions every force evaluation. A segment rotation theta injects a spurious tangential strain ~ d_perp*sin(theta): at the measured max perpendicular offset 0.055 um, 1 degree of rotation gives 0.96 pN, i.e. 1.9x f_stall (0.5 pN) and 3.8x the entire committed T_max (0.254 pN). M3 is the FREE configuration, which has a nonzero net couple by the design's own analysis and therefore WILL rotate. So M3 measures the rotation artifact, not the power stroke. Fix: either freeze walk_dir per binding lifetime (and then the rank-one tangent IS exact, closing M5 too), or co-rotate r0_bind, or constrain M3's rotation and prove theta < the tolerance you derive from k_xb*d_perp << f_stall (that tolerance is ~0.03 degrees at d_perp = 0.055 um).

M3(d) and M5 contradict each other. M3(d) requires the A:B slide partition to equal the inverse ratio of node counts 'to 1e-6 (overdamped uniform per-node mobility)' — i.e. it makes the pseudo-mobility of the relaxation a PASS criterion. M5 requires 'the implicit answer must be invariant to the mobility scale over 2 decades (a convergence-rate knob must not move the equilibrium).' Both cannot hold. For a free system with rigid-body zero modes, the final position along the zero mode is set by the relaxation path, not by physics, so M3(d) elevates a numerical artifact to a gate — the SettlingForce failure class in a new costume. Drop M3(d) or replace it with a real per-node drag against a modelled medium.

M2's criterion is mis-specified and half-vacuous. With the + group masked, filament B carries NO bound head at all, so anchor B's reaction is IDENTICALLY ZERO from step 0 for a structural reason (crossbridge_segment_split_r0bind_kernel returns on bound==0, segment_motor.py:479) — there is no 'decay' and a constant-zero series has no 'last-decade negative slope', so the criterion as written can fail on correct code. Anchor A's reaction is also identically zero at every CONVERGED step, because the minifilament bound only to A is a free body (sf_implicit.py:71) and Newton's third law then forces the total head force on A to zero. Restate M2 as 'converged reaction is zero to solver tolerance in the one-sided configuration' (a spurious-pin detector) rather than a decay measurement, and stop calling it proof that the motor pulls filament against filament.

M8 is infeasible as written. It requires 'identical seeds and identical bound populations' between a joint 2-bundle run and two isolated 1-bundle runs, but the KMC RNG is keyed on the HEAD INDEX: wp.rand_init(rng_seed ^ rng_epoch[0], h) (segment_motor.py:397 region, :175, :227). In the joint run bundle 2's heads occupy different global h, so the draws differ and the populations diverge. Either key the RNG on a persistent head ID, or prescribe the bound set explicitly for M8.

The abscissa accumulator contradicts the reuse promise and has an unscheduled blast radius. new_code_needed item 4 adds device arrays incremented 'in the commit path BEFORE the detach reset', i.e. inside step_detach_segment_gated_kernel / ..._catch_slip_kernel (segment_motor.py:142-234) — the exact kernels the reuse list calls 'the production motor, untouched'. Those kernels are shared with nmii_cortex_motor (cortex_motor_slice.py) and with the landed GATE-B artifact, so bit-identity must be re-proven on BOTH native gates, and every kernel-signature change invalidates the Warp cache (this project has a recorded stale-kernel-cache false-positive trap requiring rm -rf ~/.cache/warp/<ver>). The design never mentions cache invalidation. Schedule the cortex A/B and the cache-clear discipline explicitly.

M10 breaks the two existing contracts with no migration path. ffn_sim/docs/v2_audit/gate_contracts/ contains GATE_A_resting_baseline.yaml and GATE_B_sf_motor.yaml; GATE_B_sf_motor.yaml declares enforcement: BLOCKING with contract_hash_declared 'gcv1:66ce3533e3a4fc26'. Making a per-claim negative_control block REQUIRED in verify_gate_contracts.py instantly invalidates both, and any schema field that enters the hashed subset (gate_contract.py:117 hashed_subset / :77 PI_SIGNATURE_REQUIRED) changes the declared hash and trips the stamped-artifact drift refusal. Specify: does the requirement apply to new contracts only, is negative_control inside or outside the hash, and who re-stamps GATE-A/GATE-B.
tautological_gates: M1(1) 'reaction at A and B equal and opposite to 1e-9' — guaranteed by global force balance with exactly two Dirichlet nodes, for ANY physics. The design's own risks list names this as 'A GATE THAT CANNOT FAIL' and then keeps it as pass criterion 1. Naming a tautology in the risk section is not fixing it. Also its stated negative control (--nc flip-polarity) does not flip it: flipping polarity keeps the reactions equal and opposite, merely outward. Split into two claims (equal-and-opposite = solver-convergence diagnostic, NOT a claim; inward-sign = the real claim).
M1(6) 'net force on the isolated system == 0 to 1e-12' is the SAME statement as M1(1) (net = R_A + R_B). Two of M1's six criteria are one tautology counted twice.

M1(2) 'transmitted reaction == 0 on every step where n_bound == 0' — the motor connector is the ONLY coupling between nmii and sf_arc in this configuration, and the crossbridge kernel early-returns on bound==0 (segment_motor.py:479). Zero heads therefore means zero coupling force by code structure. Worse, the committed record shows it is even weaker than that: at step 1 the trace has n_bound = 113 with T_max = 0.0 and head_load_max = 0.0, because r0_bind makes every head unstrained at bind. The observable is lagged, so 'tension is zero when nothing is bound' is satisfied even when 113 things ARE bound.

M0(b) torque identity '|tau|/(|f|*d_perp) = 1.000 +/- 1e-10 and scaling exponent 1.000 +/- 0.01' — pure cross-product algebra. Since f is constructed parallel to walk_dir (segment_motor.py:497) and |f| = k_xb*|dot(d,w) - r0_bind| has NO d_perp dependence at all, |tau| = |f|*d_perp is an identity and the exponent is exactly 1 by construction. A 1e4-draw randomized float64 sweep cannot make this fail. It is a one-line code read.

M0(c) '|f| at bind == 0 to 1e-12 for every draw' — r0_bind is DEFINED as dot(x_att - x_head, w) at bind (segment_motor.py:455) and the force kernel evaluates k_xb*(dot(d,w) - r0_bind) with abscissa = 0, so f is BIT-EXACTLY zero, not merely within 1e-12. Definitional.

M0(e) 'sign(dot(f_head, walk_dir)) == +1 for a positive stroke in every draw' — dot(f,w) = k_xb*(dot(d,w) - r0_bind) = k_xb*abscissa when the nodes have not moved. It is criterion (c) plus 'abscissa > 0'. Cannot fail across randomized geometries. M0 therefore advertises 5 checks and contains 2 that can fail (momentum scatter, tangent-vs-FD).

M1(4)/M7/M8 'cross-binding count == 0' — unfailable in this geometry, and not for the reason stated. SegmentQuery returns the NEAREST segment (segment_query.py:83-84 host, :123-141 device: out_seg_id = bi where bi is argmin over ALL segments). A + head sits ON filament A's line (perpendicular residual median 0.000, max 0.055 um) and 0.400 um from filament B. The nearest is always its own filament, so no capture-radius value can produce cross-binding. This makes the gate unfailable AND makes two negative controls inert (see reuse_errors / sums_to_zero_risks).

M3(c) 'system centroid drift == 0 to 1e-12 per step (no self-propulsion of an isolated dipole)' — in the explicit relax x += step*F with UNIFORM per-node mobility (ac_gate_b_sf_motor_native.py:442-445), sum(dx) = step*sum(F) = 0 exactly whenever forces come in equal-and-opposite pairs, which M0(a) already verifies. The same holds for the CG path because translation is in null(K). So every momentum/centroid gate in the track is structurally exact and can only re-detect a broken scatter. Note the irony: the design cites the crawl self-propulsion failure as its motivation and then picks the one check that cannot see it, because uniform-mobility relaxation makes momentum conservation an identity.

M6(1) 'slide_h = loads_hill/k_xb - abscissa to 1e-12' — compute_head_loads_segment_split_r0bind_kernel and crossbridge_segment_split_r0bind_kernel evaluate the SAME expression (segment_motor.py:518-522 vs :493-495). The identity cannot fail unless one of the two is edited. Keep it as a CPU unit test; do not count it as a mechanism claim.

M4(4) 'duty vs load is NON-monotonic with a single interior maximum' — the catch-slip law k_catch0*exp(-|f|x_catch/kT) + k_slip0*exp(+|f|x_slip/kT) (hand.py:104-107) has an interior lifetime maximum for ANY positive constants. Non-monotonicity is a property of the functional form, not of the simulation. Only the LOCATION of the peak is a test, and that half is magnitude-bound on four GAP constants.
hidden_magnitude_deps: M1's primary observable (Dirichlet anchor reaction) is k_axial-dependent twice over: it IS the end link's k_axial*(L-r0), and its magnitude is set by the series compliance K_series = (1/K_fiber + 1/K_xb_bank)^-1 with K_fiber = k_axial/n_seg. The design's explicit justification for choosing it ('independent of the GAP k_axial') is false. k_axial is a REQUIRED-no-default GAP (sf_mechanics.py:281-283, docstring line 41: 'NF2007 inextensible; no sourced EA_actin').

M4(4) 'the measured peak load agrees with catch_slip_peak_force(k_catch0, x_catch, k_slip0, x_slip, kT) to within the ensemble SEM' is in the BLOCKING set and depends on FOUR unsourced GAP constants. The committed record records detach = CATCH_SLIP_PROXY with 'every value is an I0-B3 GAP - PI' (hand.py:70-74). This directly contradicts the design's own closing statement that the blocking set is 'conservation / identity / sign / symmetry / limit / scaling / grid-invariance only'.

M4(2) 'v/v0 -> 1.000 as k_ext -> 0' silently depends on the ratio f_stall/(k_xb*v0*tau) through the DERIVED cap. Three GAP constants plus dt decide whether the criterion is satisfiable at all (it is not, at the committed values).

M4's F_stall_ensemble normaliser is not measurable as defined. With a finite external spring, sliding never 'stops' — it asymptotes. 'The measured load at which sliding stops' exists only in the k_ext -> infinity limit, where sliding is zero at all loads. So F_stall_ens becomes the steady load at whatever the stiffest swept k_ext happened to be, i.e. the normalisation of the entire collapse plot is set by an arbitrary fixture parameter.

M1(5) 'a value < 0.05 with >10 heads bound raises a LOAD-PATH-CANCELLATION flag' — 0.05 and 10 are undeclared empirical constants with no derivation, in violation of the Magic-Number Block. And it is a 'flag', not a verdict, so the criterion cannot fail.

M2 'final |reaction| <= 1e-3 of the two-sided value at equal bound count' requires matching the bound count between a masked and an unmasked stochastic run. The mask changes the load, which changes the catch-slip detach hazard, which changes the bound count. Not controllable without freezing the KMC.

M7's 2% convergence threshold on the transmitted reaction is itself a magnitude threshold on a quantity that is mesh-set by a magic constant (see arithmetic_corrections): with link_k a flat k_axial the successive-rung change is exactly 0.50x at every rung, so the criterion 'successive-rung relative change decreases monotonically' can never be met.

M6(4) 'clamped/free contrast differs by at least a factor of 10' — the factor 10 is undeclared. With the abscissa cap binding at 2.4x even at zero load, the free-regime delta-abscissa is pinned at da_max, so the achievable contrast is bounded above by whatever the clamped regime yields, not by 10.
sums_to_zero_risks: M2, both anchors. With one head group masked the OTHER filament has no bound head at all, so its anchor reaction is identically zero from step 0 by kernel early-return (segment_motor.py:479) — not a decay. And the loaded filament's anchor reaction is also identically zero at every converged step because the minifilament bound to only one filament is a free body (sf_implicit.py:71) whose net force must vanish. The design reads this as a physics result ('a one-sided motor cannot sustain load'); it is the free-body equilibrium condition restated, and it will read zero whether or not the motor works.

M3, all of it. The free pair has zero net force by construction (bipolar dipole) AND zero centroid drift by uniform-mobility algebra AND, at exact equilibrium, zero SUM of crossbridge force on each filament (the sum over a body's external forces must vanish). So the design's 'residual crossbridge tension at convergence <= 1e-9*k_xb*mean abscissa' is either (a) the SUM, in which case it is the definition of convergence and unfailable, or (b) PER-HEAD, in which case it must legitimately FAIL: heads bound at different steps hold different abscissa and different r0_bind, so at equilibrium they cancel INTERNALLY against each other on the same filament at O(k_xb * spread(abscissa)), which is nowhere near 1e-9. Pick one and derive the tolerance.

M3(a) the abscissa->shortening identity is only exact under three unstated conditions: frozen bound population, filament axially rigid relative to the crossbridge bank, and exact equilibrium. None holds. A head that DETACHES mid-step has its abscissa zeroed (segment_motor.py:182, :233), which changes the equilibrium slide of the remaining heads and therefore moves the filaments with ZERO abscissa advance; a head that ATTACHES captures a fresh r0_bind, silently re-zeroing its reference. With k_on = 50/s and the committed record's population climbing 0 -> 113 -> 184 -> 238 -> 266 -> 301 of 320, the population changes on essentially every step. So the headline identity will fail at 1e-6 for entirely legitimate reasons, and the design has no gate on the case it fails.

M1(6)'s couple comparison is a vector-vs-scalar error that guarantees mismatch: |sum tau_h| <= sum |f_h|*d_perp,h with equality only if all per-head couples are parallel. In a bipolar minifilament the + and - groups have opposite walk_dir, so their couples are not parallel and the 'to 1e-6 relative' comparison is mathematically wrong, not merely tight.

The M1 anchor-reaction observable itself is one array-write away from being structurally zero. The inner solve masks the force on pinned nodes every iteration (_pin_force_kernel, ac_gate_b_sf_motor_native.py:134-138, applied at :440) and the reaction is only visible because the driver deliberately runs one FINAL unmasked accumulate outside the loop (ac_gate_b_sf_motor_native.py:463-474). That discipline exists as a comment in a script, not as an invariant with a test. A reordering makes the track's primary observable read exactly 0.0 on every step and every gate above still 'passes'. Add a regression that the final accumulate is unmasked.

The design's OWN #1 risk (cancellation) is not supported by the evidence it cites and the real cancellation question is not where it looks. See arithmetic_corrections: the committed 301-heads-vs-0.254-pN alarm dissolves once you count per fiber-half. The cancellation that actually matters in this configuration is the INTRA-FILAMENT cancellation among heads with heterogeneous abscissa described above, which the proposed ledger (transmitted reaction / sum|f_head|) does measure — but the alarm threshold, the head-count normalisation, and the interpretation all need rebuilding on the per-fiber number.
reuse_errors: Builds an 'external-spring boundary fixture' from scratch (new_code_needed item 7) when ffn_sim/ff/substrate.py already IS one: resolve_substrate() at :46-55 gives a Winkler anchor stiffness k_sub = 2*E*a/(1-nu^2) from the substrate Young's modulus with the KB-1.5 range documented (0.1-100 kPa biological, PAA 0.1-50), plus substrate_anchor_relax_kernel (:59) and substrate_anchor_equilibrium_kernel (:74). Using it turns M4's arbitrary 'MEASUREMENT FIXTURE' sweep into a sweep over PHYSIOLOGICAL substrate stiffness on the PI's own PAA/collagen axis, and it is the cheapest available step toward the PI's adherent-on-2D-collagen baseline. The design's reuse list does not mention ff/substrate.py at all even though the prompt hands it over explicitly.

--nc capture-2x cannot flip the gate it is attached to. Setting capture_radius = 0.42 > lateral 0.40 does not create cross-binding, because segment_query returns the NEAREST segment (segment_query.py:79-86 host; device kernel picks argmin over all n_seg then applies the radius as a pass/fail at :137-141). The head's own filament is at perpendicular distance ~0 (measured median 0.000, max 0.055 um) and the foreign filament at 0.400, so the nearest is always the head's own filament for ANY capture radius. The correct control is to halve the lateral separation below the own-filament residual (~0.055 um) or displace the minifilament laterally.

--nc bundles-adjacent has the same defect: 'place the two bundles within one capture radius (0.21 um); cross-bundle bindings must become non-zero.' For a foreign segment to win the argmin it must be closer than the head's own filament, i.e. within ~0.055 um, not 0.21 um. The stated separation is ~4x too large for the control to fire.

M0(d) 'the deviation shown to fall as O(h^2)' is the wrong asymptotics for the operator the design proposes to test. With walk_dir FROZEN the split crossbridge force is exactly affine in (p_a, p_b, p_head), so central FD is exact for every h and the observed error is pure roundoff scaling as O(eps/h) — slope -1, rising as h shrinks. Correct code FAILS the stated criterion. With walk_dir LIVE (the real runtime path) the rank-one tangent is not the derivative, so there IS an O(h^0) floor — which the design pre-labels 'a bug' but is in fact the nominal code. Either way M0(d) as written mis-scores the truth.

Reuse of ng1_two_filament_stall.py is described accurately but its thresholds are not magnitude-free the way the design implies: TRANSMISSION_LO/HI = 0.80/1.25, REACTION_RTOL = 0.35, LOAD_LO/HI_FRAC = 0.50/1.15, V_RATIO_STALL = 0.15, BOUND_FRAC_LO = 0.70 (ng1_two_filament_stall.py:95-107). V_RATIO_STALL = 0.15 is an undeclared constant chosen to be 'robust across the backbone/arm GAP' — i.e. chosen for insensitivity, which is the mirror image of choosing one to make a gate pass. If NG-1's 'magnitude-free half' is preserved, that number needs a derivation too.
