sf_sarcomere_geometry_for(topology) takes a MinifilamentTopology (sf_motor_slice.py:126-142), so the design's protocol line 'build_sf_arc_population(..., **sf_sarcomere_geometry_for(topo))' requires the minifilament topology to be constructed BEFORE the population that hosts it. That ordering is correct in the existing driver but the design never names where topo comes from; state it, because reversing it is the natural mistake and the builder raises only on non-finite values (sf_population.py:391-397), not on an inconsistent lateral.

M6 claims the slide decomposition 'needs no new device array, only a readback'. ffn_sim/ac/engine/dump_state.py:19-21 states it performs NO device-to-host readback by design (it is a shape/count census), and ac/cell/dump_state.py serves only the legacy AssembledCell — which the design itself lists under ABSENT. So the readback path is new code, and it is a prerequisite of M6, not just of M9. Sequence it earlier.
arithmetic_corrections: The design's #1 risk evidence is a ~40x unit error. It reads the committed record as '301/320 heads bound with max head load 0.0546 pN but T_max only 0.254 pN - roughly five heads' worth of transmitted load from 301 bound heads', concluding 'either legitimate load sharing plus heterogeneity, or massive internal cancellation.' But T_max is max over ALL 320 links of 40 fibers (_sf_axial_tension, ac_gate_b_sf_motor_native.py:158-167) while 301 is the GLOBAL bound count over 16 minifilaments. Per fiber: 301/40 = 7.5 heads; per fiber-half (one head group) 3.8. 3.8 x 0.0546 = 0.205 pN vs the recorded T_max 0.254 pN. The record shows essentially NO cancellation. The cancellation ledger is still worth building, but its stated motivating anomaly does not exist.

Verified and CORRECT in the design: dropping the alpha-actinin arc really does remove the stiffness wall. The committed lambda_sf = 3684001.08 pN/um decomposes exactly as 8 x 4.6e5 (arc crosslinks meeting at one apex) + 1000 (k_axial); with n_dorsal = n_arc = 0 the SF Gershgorin bound falls to O(4e3) plus bending. Credit this — it is the load-bearing feasibility claim of the whole track and it holds.

Verified and CORRECT: n_ventral=1 does yield exactly one bundle = 2 antiparallel filaments, 1 motor station, FA at both outer ends, barbed OUTWARD. Cross-checked against the record (20 bundles -> 40 fibers -> 16 ready stations + 4 cap-excluded = 20, i.e. one station per bundle; 16 minifilaments / 320 heads = 20 heads each, matching the design's '20 heads'). And ventral geometry a0 = -0.9*7.5 = -6.75 to mid, half-overlap 0.1505, gives fiber length 6.9005 um: n_per_fiber=5 -> 1.7251 um/segment, n_per_fiber=33 -> 0.2156 um. The design's '~1.7 um down to ~0.2 um' is right.

M7 will fail its own convergence criterion, for a reason the design did not find, and its negative control mislabels the nominal. sf_mechanics.py:339 sets link_k = np.full(n_links, k_axial_pn_per_um) — a FLAT per-link constant, NOT EA/L. So the fiber's series axial stiffness is k_axial/n_seg: 250.00 / 125.00 / 62.50 / 31.25 pN/um at n_per_fiber = 5/9/17/33. The successive-rung relative change is exactly 0.50x at EVERY rung — it never decreases, so 'successive-rung relative change decreases monotonically and the finest two rungs agree to <= 2%' is unreachable. Meanwhile bending IS discretised continuum-consistently, alpha = kappa/seg^3 (sf_mechanics.py:95, :224): 0.01418 pN/um at n=5 rising to 7.265 at n=33, a 512x increase. Across the M7 sweep the fiber's bending-to-axial ratio moves by ~4000x. The real finding M7 would surface is a discretisation inconsistency inside one topology builder, and the design's --nc segment-length-scaled-k control presupposes the nominal already scales k_axial with segment length, which it does not.

Stall cap vs Hill advance, recomputed: da_max@F=0 = f_stall/k_xb = 0.5/1000 = 5.000e-4 um = 0.50 nm; tau*v0 = 0.01*0.12 = 1.200e-3 um = 1.20 nm; ratio 2.400, so the cap binds at zero load and the unloaded v/v0 ceiling is 0.4167. The cap stops binding only below dt = f_stall/(k_xb*v0) = 4.17 ms.

Series stiffness, recomputed: k_xb 1000 in series with k_head_arm 100 = 90.91 pN/um. The strain needed to reach f_stall through the real path is 0.5/90.91 = 5.50 nm, 11.0x the 0.50 nm per-step cap. So da_max = (f_stall - F)/k_xb is derived against the wrong stiffness and a head can never approach stall within a step. One capped step through the series path yields 90.91 x 5.0e-4 = 0.0455 pN, against the recorded head_load_max = 0.0546 pN — the observed per-head load is the clamp, not the motor.

Rotation artifact, quantified: spurious tangential force from stale r0_bind = k_xb*d_perp*sin(theta). At d_perp = 0.055 um (the measured max): 0.096 pN at 0.1 deg, 0.960 pN at 1 deg, 4.79 pN at 5 deg. Against f_stall = 0.5 pN and the recorded T_max = 0.254 pN. The implied placement/rotation tolerance for the artifact to stay under 10% of f_stall is theta < ~0.03 deg at d_perp = 0.055 um — which also answers the design's open question 6 quantitatively instead of offering PI three options.

M5's tolerance is achievable in principle but only for the right system: 1e-8 x 0.301 um = 3.0e-9 um = 3 fm, which against positions of order 6.9 um is 4.4e-10 relative, about 2e6 x float64 eps. Fine for a well-conditioned direct solve. It is NOT achievable against a linearised oracle of a nonlinear residual, which is the actual blocker (see must_fix 1).

Effort: claimed total 10.5 d (0.5+1.5+0.5+1+1.5+1+1.5+0.5+0.5+1+1). Realistic ~21-23 d. The steps that are underestimated by 2x or more: M1 (new driver + new diagnostics module + 8-seed ensemble + A5000 round trips, claimed 1.5 d), M2 (kernel signature change + Warp cache invalidation + bit-identity re-proof on BOTH the SF and cortex landed gates, claimed 0.5 d), M6 (two new device accumulators inside a shared production kernel + an independent PE evaluator + rebuilding the ledger after the tautology above, claimed 1.5 d), M7 (will surface the link_k discretisation defect, which is a design decision with unbounded follow-on, claimed 0.5 d), M10 (schema change + migrating and re-stamping 2 BLOCKING contracts + PI sign-off latency, claimed 1 d). 7 of 11 steps need the single remote A5000; the design budgets no sync/recompile overhead and never mentions the recorded stale-kernel-cache trap.

M4's collapse test is not testable with one point per condition. A sweep over >= 4 decades of k_ext yields ~4-8 (F, v) points, one per k_ext. 'Points from all decades fall on one curve' is trivially true for any monotone sequence — collapse requires MULTIPLE conditions mapping to the same normalised coordinate. Also, geometric spacing in k_ext clusters F/F_stall near the extremes; the sweep must be adaptive in F, not in k_ext. The curvature-sign half is salvageable: at kappa = 0.5, Hill gives v/v0 = 0.25 at F/F_stall = 0.5 versus 0.50 linear, a factor 2, comfortably above the ~4% seed SEM from 8 seeds of ~20 heads (binomial ~11% per realisation).
ducked_questions: The PI's central instruction — compartments must be connected 'so that they deform each other' — is not met and the design converts it into a question for PI instead of answering it. Both ends of the pair are Dirichlet pins, i.e. infinitely stiff boundaries that by definition do not deform. The design states this honestly ('fa_actin_anchor - explicitly NOT made force-real ... a STAND-IN, not a modelled focal adhesion') and then asks PI open question 5: 'Is a Dirichlet pin an acceptable STAND-IN, or must the pair gate wait for the FA/ECM clutch? Your physiological-baseline rule points one way; smallest-scale-first points the other.' The PI has already asked this in the magnets-versus-full-adhesion-circuits form. ff/substrate.py (Winkler k_sub from E, KB-1.5 range) plus ff/fa_clutch_warp.py plus ff/ecm_library.py exist and were handed to the designer. The answerable version: replace the pin with a compliant substrate anchor at a KB-1.5 collagen/PAA stiffness, run the pin as the k_sub -> infinity CONTROL, and the boundary both deforms and lands on the PI's baseline at near-zero extra cost. That also makes M4's 'MEASUREMENT FIXTURE' disclaimer unnecessary.

The PI's baseline (cell in media, adherent on 2D collagen) is deferred wholesale: 'FA/ECM track ... Sequence it after M1-M7.' No step touches ff/ecm_library.py or ff/fa_clutch_warp.py, and no M4 sweep endpoint is tied to a collagen stiffness. Given that the PI named this as THE configuration where comparable published data exists, the sequencing needs a justification, not a placement at the end of the list.

The PI's item 4 (after assembly, speed optimisation is the single biggest goal) gets one paragraph forbidding the two available 40x wins during M1-M8 — which is correct discipline — and then produces no speed data at all. No step measures wall-clock per accepted step, per inner iteration, or their scaling with n_per_fiber and n_heads, even though M7 already sweeps the mesh 5/9/17/33 and would yield the scaling for free. The later cg_check_every / assembled-per-fiber A/B has no baseline to A/B against. Add cost instrumentation to M7 at zero marginal effort.

The PI's item 5 (parameters are eventual OUTPUTS; the purpose is to infer molecular parameters from macroscopic data) is never operationalised. M4 is the natural place to state which pair observable identifies which GAP constant — curvature sign identifies kappa, the free-sliding rate identifies min(v0, f_stall/(k_xb*tau)), the duty peak location identifies x_catch/x_slip, the transmitted reaction identifies k_xb x N_bound x compliance — i.e. a sensitivity/identifiability table, plus the degeneracies (f_stall and k_xb enter the cap only as the ratio f_stall/k_xb, so they are NOT separately identifiable from this configuration). That table is the deliverable the PI's long-run purpose needs and it is absent.

Open question 4 (Hookean k_axial penalty versus NF2007 inextensibility with a Lagrange multiplier) is presented to PI as a coin flip, but the project's hard rule already decides it: prefer the fine-grained mechanistic option even at higher implementation cost, and sf_mechanics.py's own docstring line 41 records that NF2007 treats the backbone as inextensible and that k_axial has no sourced EA_actin. The multiplier is also the only transmitted-load observable that is genuinely k_axial-free — the exact property the design falsely claims for the anchor reaction. Recommend the constraint on the physics and let PI ratify, rather than asking PI to choose.

Open question 6 (torque) offers PI three options with no numbers. The tolerance is derivable: the spurious force from a stale r0_bind under rotation is k_xb*d_perp*sin(theta), so option (c) 'drive the perpendicular offset to zero' has a computable placement tolerance (theta < ~0.03 deg at the current d_perp = 0.055 um for the artifact to stay under 10% of f_stall). Give PI the number.

Open question 1 (which ladder rung a deliberately small-scale gate occupies) is escalated with 'I will not decide this myself' and labelled the thing that 'must be answered first'. Escalating a ladder-rung ratification is legitimate; making it a blocker is not. The design could proceed immediately with the artifact labelled 'prerequisite, non-promoting, scope-limited' — which is exactly what GATE_B_sf_motor.yaml already does in its own configuration_fixed.population.scope_note ('This is a SLICE ... CLAUDE.md's validate-at-full-native rule is NOT satisfied by this configuration'). The precedent exists in-tree.

Angular momentum is raised as a risk ('a gate that checks only sum of forces will report a clean pass on a system that is quietly gaining angular momentum') and then answered with a tautology (M0(b)) rather than a measurement. The step where it matters is M3, the free pair, whose criteria cover linear momentum (c) but not angular. Given the rotation-artifact magnitude computed above, M3 needs an explicit total-angular-momentum / net-rotation observable with a derived bound, and that observable is the one that would flip.

result.summary:
This is the most self-critical design in the programme — its two volunteered corrections (the "40x" is applies-not-wall, and the fixed-MG path is 2.6x SLOWER in wall than the incumbent) are both verified true against `FINE_MESH_MULTIGRID_DESIGN_2026-07-24.md:377-378` (OFF 568 s vs ON 1463 s), and its file/line reuse map is unusually accurate (26/26 cited paths exist). But three structural defects break it as written.

(1) THE HEADLINE EVIDENCE IS A SUPERSEDED PRE-FIX ARTIFACT. The design's "existential number, from a committed artifact, not an estimate" is `resting_native_probe_2026-07-23.json`, whose own config carries `"overlap_free_cortex": false` and `"residual_start": 2634.119`. 2634 pN is the EXACT pre-fix value that commit `81805535` ("make overlap_free_cortex the native DEFAULT") reduced to 47.4 pN by eliminating 64,517 t0 steric interpenetrations (`CORTEX_EMERGENT_AND_REMAINING_PLAN_2026-07-23.md:8`). The probe was committed at `82c263fa` 2026-07-23 14:29 JST; the fix landed 2026-07-23 16:29 JST and `git merge-base --is-ancestor` confirms the probe is the OLDER ancestor. The default is now `overlap_free_cortex: bool = True` (`ac/cell/assemble.py:244`). So the entire 3,438x-slower-than-real-time / 24-days-per-run / 65-GPU-years framing rests on a build defect that was fixed two hours later and is default-on today. The design cites `CORTEX_KINK_AUDIT_2026-07-25.md` for the MG line but never checked its own headline probe's overlap_free flag. This is the project's documented coarse/stripped-configuration failure, committed by a document whose own risk list names it.

(2) THE SOLVE IS STALLED, NOT SLOW — SO THE TRACK IS OPTIMISING A NO-PROGRESS LOOP. I computed the convergence predicate directly. `inner_mechanics.py:293-296` requires three legs; the probe passes two and fails only the force leg. `inner_max_displacement_um = 4.463e-15` against `inner_tolerance_um = 7.449e-9` (`driver.py:1026`) — the max node displacement is 2.7 ULP of the 7.4 µm radius (7.4 × eps64 = 1.64e-15), i.e. machine noise. Meanwhile the force leg needs `max|PF| ≤ tol/dt_mu = 7.449e-9/3.536e-8 = 0.2107 pN` and delivers 1483.1 pN — 7,040x over. The 400 iterations are not 400 useful iterations that need to be faster; the solver has stopped moving. Making them 40x faster produces 40x faster nothing. The design reads "budget EXHAUSTED" and correctly demotes FIX1, but for the wrong reason, and never names the stall as the prerequisite that gates every denominator in the track.

(3) BIT-IDENTITY — THE TRACK'S PRIMARY ACCEPTANCE INSTRUMENT IN S1, S3, S4, S5, S6 AND THE VIZ HASH GATE — DOES NOT EXIST IN THIS CODEBASE. `implicit_mechanics.py:1333` is `wp.atomic_add(out, 0, wp.dot(a[i], b[i]))`: a single-scalar float64 atomic reduction over 551,434 threads feeding alpha/beta into dx. `ledger.py:97-102` `_reduce_vec3_kernel` is the same shape for the reaction/traction resultants. Float64 addition is non-associative and atomic arrival order is nondeterministic, so dx and the committed state are not run-to-run reproducible at the last bits. The in-tree proof is a number the design itself quotes from: `sc1_70k_full.json` records `parity_nofloat = 2.296e-13` for removing a `float(g@v)` host sync — a mathematically exact no-op that did not reproduce bit-for-bit — and `parity_devscalar = 3.470e-07`. Every "BIT-IDENTICAL" pass criterion in this track will fail for a correct implementation, and S6's byte-identity gate on a near-cancelling atomic sum will fail with O(100%) jitter. The design needs either a deterministic-reduction prerequisite (fixed-order tree/segmented reduction) or a measured-noise-floor relative criterion; it asks for neither, while making bit-identity load-bearing eight times.

The skeleton is salvageable and worth salvaging: S0-first sequencing, a negative control on every step, preserved honest negatives (deflated PCG), and the refusal to report ms/step are all correct instincts. But it cannot be executed as written.
must_fix: HEADLINE ARTIFACT IS SUPERSEDED. `ffn_sim/outputs/ac/resting_native/resting_native_probe_2026-07-23.json` config `overlap_free_cortex: false`, `residual_start: 2634.119` — the exact pre-fix value that `81805535` reduced to 47.4 pN by removing 64,517 t0 interpenetrations (`docs/v2_audit/CORTEX_EMERGENT_AND_REMAINING_PLAN_2026-07-23.md:8`; count corroborated at `CORTEX_STRUCTURE_AUDIT_2026-07-23.md:23`). Probe commit `82c263fa` (2026-07-23 14:29) is an ancestor of fix `81805535` (2026-07-23 16:29); default is now True at `ac/cell/assemble.py:244`. RE-MEASURE the baseline on the default build before any of 172 s / 3,438x / 24 d / 65 GPU-years is quoted. Both probes on disk (`resting_native_probe2_capture0.6_2026-07-23.json` too) are pre-fix with identical residual_start.

NAME THE STALL AS THE HARD PREREQUISITE. `inner_max_displacement_um = 4.463e-15` = 2.7 ULP of the 7.4 µm radius vs `inner_tolerance_um = 7.449e-9` (`ac/cell/driver.py:1026`); the only failing leg of `update_convergence_kernel` (`ac/cell/inner_mechanics.py:293-296`) is `max|PF|·dt_mu ≤ tol`, needing max|PF| ≤ 0.2107 pN and getting 1483.1 = 7,040x over. The loop is at the f64 noise floor, not iteration-starved. Add an explicit gate: no S1-S6 speedup is reportable until accept ratio > 0 on the current default build. Otherwise every arm divides by zero.

REPLACE BIT-IDENTITY WITH A REPRODUCIBILITY-AWARE CRITERION, OR MAKE DETERMINISTIC REDUCTION A PREREQUISITE STEP. `ac/cell/implicit_mechanics.py:1330-1333` (`_dot_kernel`, f64 `wp.atomic_add` into a single scalar over n_total=551,434) and `ac/engine/ledger.py:97-102` (`_reduce_vec3_kernel`, same) make dx and the committed state run-to-run nondeterministic in the last bits. In-tree proof from a file the design cites: `outputs/ff_single_opt/sc0_profiles/sc1_70k_full.json` `parity_nofloat = 2.296e-13` for an exact no-op change. Note `max_force_kernel` (`inner_mechanics.py:192`, `atomic_max`) IS deterministic and `ac/solid/steric_warp.py:11-17` documents its own accumulation as atomic-free and deterministic — so the fix is targeted, not global: add a fixed-order/segmented f64 reduction for the CG dots and the ledger resultants, then bit-identity becomes a legal instrument. Until then S1/S3/S4/S5 must gate on `|Δ| ≤ measured same-config repeat noise floor`, with that floor measured first.

S6's TWO PRIMARY CRITERIA ARE MUTUALLY CONTRADICTORY. (i) demands the ledger residual be BYTE-IDENTICAL; (ii) concedes dx differs within the linear-solve tolerance. Forces are a function of position, so byte-identical forces at non-identical positions is impossible. In the only reading where (i) can hold — assembling the ledger at a FIXED input state — the f32 preconditioner is not in the measured code path at all, making (i) a tautology and its f32-force negative control a demonstration on code the gate never guards. Additionally the residual is `|reaction + traction|` where each term is an atomic f64 sum (`ledger.py:97-102, 128-145`): a near-cancellation of two nondeterministic sums has jitter of order the residual itself. Restate as a RELATIVE residual `|R+T|/max(|R|,|T|)` against the caller tolerance, on a deterministic reduction, with the same-config repeat spread reported alongside.

S0 CANNOT DECIDE THE QUESTION IT EXISTS TO DECIDE. I inspected the API: `warp._src.utils.TimingResult` exposes exactly `(device, name, filter, elapsed)` — no DRAM counters, no sector/request, no occupancy, and Warp exposes no occupancy API (`grep` for occup* in `warp` and `warp._src.context` returns empty). Analytic USEFUL bytes / event time yields achieved USEFUL bandwidth, and 10-15% of peak useful bandwidth is the expected signature of a BANDWIDTH-bound kernel with 4-32x sector amplification from uncoalesced access — indistinguishable from latency-bound. To decide it you need Nsight Compute (`dram__bytes_read.sum`, `l1tex__average_t_sectors_per_request`, warp stall reasons) or the strategy inversion stays an assertion. Since the design declares every other estimate 'un-decidable without S0', this defect propagates to the whole track.

S0's CLOSURE IDENTITY INVERTS ITS OWN HYPOTHESIS AND WOULD MISDIAGNOSE A REAL FINDING. sum(per-kernel CUDA-event times) < stage wall is the SIGNATURE of launch-gap / host-bound execution — precisely the hypothesis S0 is testing — yet the criterion labels non-closure 'measuring something other than the step'. Concretely, `ac/engine/transaction.py:154` calls `assert_disjoint_populations`, which at `ac/engine/population.py:194-195` runs a Python loop over `ledger.active_ids` (a host `frozenset[int]`, `population.py:91`) on EVERY accepted step — an O(N_filaments) host cost inside the step that no kernel timer can see. S0 would report non-closure and blame the instrument. Restate: report the gap explicitly as `wall − Σkernel = host+launch time`, and treat a large gap as a finding, not an instrumentation failure.

THE SOLE REPORTABLE METRIC IS A STRUCTURAL ZERO. 'committed physical seconds per wall hour' = Σdt_phys over ACCEPTED steps / wall. In the only committed native artifact `outer_accepted: false`, `outer_rolled_back: true`, `committed_time_s: 0.0`. So the metric is identically 0 for every arm of S1-S6 and every speedup evaluates 0/0. The design half-sees this (it quotes 171.89 s committing 0.0 s) yet elevates the metric to 'the only reportable throughput metric in this track' with no fallback. Add a secondary, always-defined metric (wall per unit residual reduction at fixed achieved residual, plus accept ratio) so the arms are comparable in the accept-ratio-zero regime.

S3 GATE 2 CANNOT DETECT THE COUPLING CHANNELS THAT MATTER, AND ITS NEGATIVE CONTROL IS FALSE. 'Perturb block 0, assert block 1's FORCE array byte-identical' is invariant to a shared global dot product, a shared regularization max, a shared convergence latch and a shared accept predicate — none of which changes the force at a fixed position; they change alpha/beta and the search DIRECTION. Only a shared HashGrid or a shared force accumulator would fail it. The design's stated control ('share one global reduction scalar → GATE 2 FAILS') therefore asserts a control will fire that provably will not. GATE 1 (standalone-equivalence) subsumes all of it; GATE 2 as written adds a false second opinion. Fix: perturb block 0 and assert block 1's ENTIRE per-iteration trajectory (direction, alpha, beta, latch, accept flag), not its force array.

S2's rho CRITERIA ARE SATISFIABLE BY A STALLED SOLVE. rho = max|PF|_{k+1}/max|PF|_k. A plateaued residual gives rho ≡ 1, which is perfectly h-independent at every resolution. Both measured arms ARE plateaued: `FINE_MESH_MULTIGRID_DESIGN_2026-07-24.md:377-378` records 'flat it5→39' (OFF) and 'flat it10→39' (ON). So criteria (i) rho(FIX2) ≤ rho(full-fine) and (ii) h-independence both PASS on a completely stalled solver. Add: rho must be < 1 by a stated margin, measured only in the pre-plateau iteration window, with the plateau onset iteration reported. Separately, criterion (iv) 'the converged outer state matches the MG-off arm' is UNEVALUABLE — neither arm converges (needs max|PF| ≤ 0.21 pN; arms sit at 4.07 and 3.42).
tautological_gates: S2 (i)+(ii): rho ≡ 1 under a plateau is perfectly h-independent. Both measured arms are flat (`FINE_MESH_MULTIGRID_DESIGN_2026-07-24.md:377-378`). The multigrid claim passes on a stalled solver.

S2 (iv): 'converged outer state matches within the outer convergence tolerance' — no arm converges, so the criterion can neither pass nor fail. The design flags the non-convergence in open_questions_for_pi but still writes (iv) as if a converged state existed.

THE REUSED CPU MG EVIDENCE IS TAUTOLOGICAL FOR EXACTLY THE COUPLING FIX2 DROPS. `tests/ac/cell/test_fiber_arclength_vcycle.py:21-23` states the synthetic operator is 'the exact per-fiber pentadiagonal NF2007 bending sub-operator + a I + ext' — NO inter-fiber crosslinks, NO inextensibility projector. `test_assembled_perfiber_operator_matches_the_fine_perfiber_block:378-387` then matches to 1e-11 and says so in its own docstring: 'a crosslink-free multi-fiber operator IS block-diagonal per fiber'. FIX2's whole content is dropping the inter-fiber off-diagonal and the projector from levels ≥1 — in this rig it drops nothing. `test_one_vcycle_energy_reduction_is_h_independent:361-371` and `test_assembled_coarse_vcycle_is_spd_and_h_independent:408-422` run on the same crosslink-free operator. `ac/cell/fiber_arclength_mg.py:604-605` asserts 'the CPU h-independence/SPD gates cover the True path'; they do not, and the design inherits the claim.

THREE CITED 'GATES' ARE PURE SOURCE-STRING GREPS AND CANNOT FAIL ON A PHYSICS REGRESSION. `test_cg_host_early_exit_is_bit_identical:497-505` literally asserts `"bit-identical" in _IMPL_SRC` and `"dx is unchanged; only the wasted post-convergence work is saved" in _IMPL_SRC`. `test_multigrid_is_preconditioning_only_same_fixed_point:487-495` asserts `"preconditioning-only, the fixed point + residual gate" in _IMPL_SRC`. `test_off_flag_is_inert_and_uses_incumbent_precondition:471-485` asserts source substrings. These fail only if someone edits a comment. The design's claim 'Every S1/S2 CPU-side criterion already has a test to extend' is false for these three, and citing them risks inheriting exactly the largest-fragment-vs-2nd-largest gate class. (Lines 343-352, 361-371, 378-392, 408-422 ARE genuinely numerical — eigvalsh, energy-norm reduction, NumPy reference, apply counts — but see the crosslink-free defect above.)

S6 (i) in the fixed-state reading: if the ledger is assembled at a fixed input state, the f32 preconditioner is not in the measured path, so byte-identity holds by construction and the gate cannot fail for the change it is guarding.

S6 (iv) 'f32 preconditioner still SPD (min eigenvalue > 0)': the existing SPD rig is pure CPU NumPy (`test_fiber_arclength_vcycle.py:343-352`, `_preconditioner_matrix` built column-by-column in NumPy). It cannot observe a CUDA f32 kernel's spectrum. No mechanism is proposed, so the criterion is unevaluable as written.

S4 states ONE criterion twice and calls it independent confirmation: 'measured kernel time strictly decreases AND achieved bandwidth as a fraction of peak strictly increases (proving the mechanism claimed is the mechanism that acted)'. With analytically-fixed useful bytes, achieved bandwidth = bytes/time, so it increases IFF time decreases. The second clause is algebraically the first and proves nothing about mechanism. The mechanism claim needs sectors-per-request from ncu.

S9's pass criterion is explicitly 'only that the comparison is valid' — throughput is 'RECORDED, not gated'. That is honest, but it means S9 is a procurement benchmark, not a validation step, and should not be listed among validation_steps without saying so.
hidden_magnitude_deps: The headline artifact's own config self-labels as non-physiological: `"resting_bound_myosin_source": "TEST-native-probe NOT physiological (Codex finding 7 verify)"`, `resting_bound_myosin_force_pn: 2.0`, `resting_bound_myosin_fraction: 0.3`, and every `erm_*` field null (`erm_density_per_um2`, `erm_k_on_s`, `erm_k_off0_s`, `erm_bell_force_pn`, `erm_capture_radius_um`) — i.e. the ERM connector's kinetics are OFF. The number the design calls a 'MEASURED FACT ... not an estimate' comes from a configuration the physiological-baseline HARD rule excludes from supporting a conclusion.

The throughput metric is LINEAR in dt_phys = 0.05 s. Doubling dt doubles 'committed physical seconds per wall hour' with zero physics gain. S7 correctly forbids choosing dt for speed, but S0-S6 all report the metric at the incumbent, unvalidated dt with no note that the denominator is an unconverged magnitude. Every pre-S7 throughput number is therefore conditional on a value S7 exists to validate.

S3's ensemble R is sized from the WRONG ENGINE. 'HBM 84-132 MB/cell measured (sc0), so 10-30 cells fit 16 GB' uses ff/ profiles (`sc0_native70k_full.json` 84.26 MB; the 131.76 figure is actually sc2_struct/sc2_wall2, not sc0). The in-tree ac/ figure is `docs/v2_audit/FINE_MESH_SOLVER_MEMORY_2026-07-24.md:65`: pathA `ProjectedAnalyticCG` + probe = ~5.5 GB at the fine mesh, i.e. R = 2 on a 16 GB A5000. That alone caps R2's '4-10x' at ≤2x. The design never states which mesh S3's 'full native baseline' means, and the two candidates differ by ~40x in per-cell HBM.

The dominant ac/ solver array scales QUADRATICALLY in an unstated discretization choice: `ac/cell/implicit_mechanics.py:1528` sizes `fiber_block_factor` as n_fibers × 3 × max_fiber_nodes², measured at 83 MB for 7 nodes and 2.85 GB for 41 (`FINE_MESH_SOLVER_MEMORY_2026-07-24.md:67`). R is therefore a function of segment length, not a property of the engine. Not stated anywhere in S3.

The accepted-step tolerance is caller-owned by design (`ac/engine/ledger.py:329-341`, `assemble_balance(tol_sq_d)`), which is the right architecture — but S6 criterion (v) 'the accept/reject DECISION is identical on every outer step' is then tolerance-dependent with no stated caller and no stated value. A loose tol makes (v) trivially pass; a tight one makes it fail on reduction noise alone.

S7's dt plateau needs 'one mechanical observable' and the design defers the choice to PI (open question 9). Declared rather than hidden, which is acceptable — but until it is chosen S7 has no evaluable pass criterion, and it is the step the design itself ranks as possibly the largest single-run lever.

S8's SBC needs 'a pre-registered test at a pre-registered level' — neither the test nor the level is named. Statistical rather than physiological, so it does not violate the PI priority, but it is an unspecified constant inside the gate.
sums_to_zero_risks: THE TRACK'S HEADLINE OBSERVABLE IS IDENTICALLY ZERO FOR A STRUCTURAL REASON. committed_time_s = 0.0 because outer_accepted = false; every arm of S1-S6 measured with 'committed physical seconds per wall hour' returns 0, so every ratio is 0/0. Every edge of the measurement is present (per-kernel times, bit-identity, HBM, launch counts) and the top-level number is nil — the exact crawl pattern (every clutch loaded, F_net one quarter of one clutch).

S6's ledger residual is a deliberate near-cancellation of two large opposing atomic f64 sums (`ac/engine/ledger.py:140-145`: `r = reaction_resultant[0] + traction_resultant[0]`). Both terms come from `_reduce_vec3_kernel` atomic adds (`:97-102`). The residual's own run-to-run jitter is of order the residual, so it is a quantity whose value is dominated by the summation-order noise the design intends to use it to detect. This is the highest-severity item because the design correctly identifies this as the load path most at risk from precision work and then proposes the one gate that cannot measure it.

S3 GATE 2 measures a quantity that is invariant to the failure it is meant to catch: force at a fixed position is unchanged by a shared global reduction scalar, a shared regularizer max, a shared convergence latch or a shared accept predicate. Every one of those is real cross-cell coupling with zero signature in the observable.
S4's 'achieved bandwidth fraction strictly increases' is algebraically identical to 'time decreases' when bytes are analytically fixed — a second criterion with zero independent information content.

The difference render for a bit-identical arm is a solid single colour by construction and conveys nothing beyond the hash comparison; the design admits this. With reduction nondeterminism the field is instead a 1e-13 speckle rendered on the viewer's log10 turbo ramp (`scripts/ac_cell_assembled_viz.py:22-25`), which fills the full colour range and is visually indistinguishable from a real bug. Both the zero case and the noise case defeat the render's stated discriminating purpose ('spatially structureless vs visible structure') unless an absolute scale anchored to a measured noise floor is imposed.
reuse_errors: 'wp.timing_begin is used at exactly two sites' (observables_missing) is wrong: there are FOUR — `ac/cell/driver.py:1061`, `:1076`, `ac/cell/native_gates/ng2_ng3_ng6.py:1165`, `:1169`. The design's own current_state section lists the ng2 site, so it contradicts itself. In a document whose authority rests on exact counts this matters. (TIMING_KERNEL genuinely appears nowhere; ScopedStream/wp.Stream genuinely have zero call sites; ScopedCapture only at `dcm/dcm_warp_hybrid.py:246,252` — all three verified.)

THE TRANSACTION IS NOT A FIXED LAUNCH SEQUENCE, so S5's 'natural first CUDA-graph capture scope' is not capturable as written. `ac/engine/transaction.py:154` calls `assert_disjoint_populations` on every accepted step; `ac/engine/population.py:194-195` iterates `ledger.active_ids` (a host `frozenset[int]`, `:91`) in a Python loop building a dict over the whole population. Uncapturable, and an O(N_filaments) host cost inside the step at native scale.

THE DIFFERENCE RENDER THE VIZ SECTION REQUIRES DOES NOT EXIST AND IS NOT BUDGETED. `scripts/ac_viz_common.py` `build_scenes(dump)` takes ONE dump; grep for diff/delta/baseline in that module returns zero hits. Twelve new_code_needed items are listed and none is a two-dump difference scene builder. The viz plan is the track's stated checkpoint and its central artifact has no implementation path.

THE ENSEMBLE PRECEDENT IS SCOPED AGAINST THE DESIGN'S USE OF IT. `docs/v2_audit/ENGINE_ACCELERATION_PLAN_2026-07-07.md:62-65` gives the 3-8x at n_fil~100 and says verbatim 'NOT at native 38k (single cortex already saturates)'; `:33-35` says 'At native N the force kernels already saturate the A5000, so ensemble-batching and launch-overhead (CUDA-graph) wins shrink to ~1.1-1.5x'. The design cites this as evidence for 4-10x AT NATIVE SCALE while calling the counter-statement an unmeasured assertion. n_fil~100 is 700x smaller than native — using it to estimate a native win is the coarse-configuration extrapolation the design's own risk list names.

'the merged-array block-diagonal test the project already owns' — no such test exists. It is a DIAGNOSIS document (`docs/v2_audit/INTERNAL_DISPLACEMENT_DIAGNOSIS_2026-07-16.md:13-22`, cortex 39.8 nm / nucleus 0.0 nm; restated at `TRAJECTORY_HOW_WE_GOT_TO_AC_2026-07-25.md:175`). A grep for block_diagonal across tests/ and scripts/ hits only `test_fiber_arclength_vcycle.py`, which means something mathematically unrelated. The design does budget the harness in new_code_needed, so this is an overstated provenance claim rather than a missing item.

`rm -rf ~/.cache/warp/<ver>` is the wrong path on the dev Mac — Warp 1.14.0 reports its cache at `/Users/sw1/Library/Caches/warp/1.14.0`, and no gbook path is given. `wp.clear_kernel_cache()` exists in 1.14 (verified) and is the correct, platform-independent call. A protocol step written as a literal shell command that fails silently on one of the two machines is a poor hygiene gate for a track whose worst failure mode is a false 'bit-identical'.

'A throughput accounting module' is largely a division of fields that already exist. `ac/cell/driver.py:1204-1215` StabilityReport already carries committed_time, outer_accepted, outer_rolled_back, outer_step_wall_s, wall_s, inner_iters, inner_attempts, inner_iteration_budget, inner_converged — all present in the probe JSON. Compute the ratio; do not build a module.

The design corrects the '~40x' in prose but leaves the machine-readable declared path uncorrected: `outputs/tag_kb/forces_manifest.yaml:496-499` still reads 'SPEED FIX2 (~40x with FIX1)'. That YAML is what a future session and `verify_forces.py` read. Correcting the manifest rationale should be a named deliverable.

S4's segment-major transpose is specified for fixed-length fibers only. sums_to_zero_risks: VERIFIED, not hypothetical. I ran build_sf_arc_population(cell_radius_um=7.5, nucleus_radius_um=3.0): fa_sites.size == 10, positions [(-6.75,-2.812,0),(6.75,-2.812,0),(-6.75,-0.938,0),(6.75,-0.938,0),(-6.75,0.938,0),(6.75,0.938,0),(-6.75,2.812,0),(6.75,2.812,0),(-1.5,-6.0,0),(1.5,-6.0,0)]. Every FA site has an exact x-mirror partner, INCLUDING the two dorsal basal ends. sf_population.py:481-486 constructs ventral SFs as closed dipoles with FA at both ends; :490-494 places the two dorsal SFs as an x-mirror pair. Consequence: the cell->ECM traction resultant vanishes by construction, per fibre for the ventrals and pairwise for the dorsals. A4(a) and A6(a) both gate on that resultant.

Because the ventral SF is a CLOSED dipole (both ends clutched), Sum f_clutch->ECM is exactly zero PER FIBRE at every instant, converged or not, for any stiffness, for any bond state, as long as both ends stay bound. So if A3(c) uses |traction| as its non-degeneracy denominator it divides by a structural zero. The design says 'reported WITH its denominator so a zero field cannot pass silently' - right instinct, wrong quantity: the denominator must be Sum|f| per endpoint, never the resultant.

A4(c)'s dipole evidence is not locomotory and cannot detect the failure it invokes. The deviatoric part of the SYMMETRIC first moment is even under front/rear exchange: a cell pulling +x at the front and -x at the rear with equal magnitude has a large deviatoric M_xx and moves nowhere. That IS the recorded crawl failure (isotropic/cancelling traction, F_net down to one clutch) in a new dress. A locomotory claim needs a POLAR (odd) observable - front-vs-rear traction asymmetry, or the time-integrated net force on the cell body over a bind/release cycle - which A4 does not have.

A4's negative control (a) is UNRUNNABLE on the named dependency. It requires 'isotropic radial grip with no polarity' so the anisotropy metric reads ~0 and prints DIPOLE ABSENT. But all four ventral SFs run a0=[-0.9R, y, 0] to b0=[+0.9R, y, 0] (sf_population.py:484-485) - every ventral traction is +/-x. The 'unpolarised' baseline is already MAXIMALLY anisotropic, so there is no ~0 reference and almost no headroom for the polarity-broken variant to rise into. Both the control and the criterion need a different population.

Third-order risk the design misses: the residual traction after the ventral pairs cancel comes ONLY from the 2 dorsal basal ends, whose partner ends terminate on FA-free transverse arcs (sf_population.py:497-501, anchor_kind 'none'). So the entire non-zero traction is carried by 2 of 10 clutches, both placed at y=-6.0 by a hard-coded scaffold constant. Any 'polarity' A4 reports is that placement artifact. This is numerically the same signature as 'F_net was one quarter to one clutch'.
reuse_errors: new_code_needed item 1 duplicates existing production code. It asks for 'ac/engine/fa_clutch_connector.py - the concrete CompositeECMClutch implementation (the class ecm_world.py:822 already demands and nothing provides)'. CompositeLoadPathECMClutchAdapter at ecm_world.py:229-258 IS that implementation: it declares mechanical_group / equal_opposite_required / adjoint_transfer_required / work_ledger_required and forwards accumulate / snapshot_candidate / rollback / commit_irreversible / accumulate_ledger, is exported at ecm_world.py:1173, and its __post_init__ (:222-227) already enforces that the joint borrows the LIVE ECM owner arrays by storage-pointer identity. It is exercised at tests/ac/engine/test_ecm_world.py:352-385. The design's supporting claim - 'Grep confirms NO class implements CompositeECMClutch anywhere outside test doubles (test_ecm_world.py:346)' - is wrong: the test double there is the JOINT (_JointSpy), not the clutch. Real remaining work is far smaller than a new module: construct a real LoadPathJointRuntime instead of _JointSpy, and supply a LedgerContributor that pushes the ECM-side scatter into add_cell_traction.

The current-state census is wrong on its own key measurement. Part A(ii) says of the fa_ecm/fa_clutch_warp/fa_maturation/substrate group '(measured: ac/ imports NONE of these)'. ac/solid/adhesion_clutch.py:37 is 'from ffn_sim.ff.fa_ecm import attach_clutches_to_ecm, clutch_ecm_spring_kernel'. My grep of ac/ for ffn_sim.ff.* confirms one fa_ecm import. This matters twice over: (a) the design misses an EXISTING ac/ clutch primitive (AdhesionClutchCompartment) that is the one-sided reaction-discarding version - ':78 _ecm_force_d: scratch reaction accumulator (rigid substrate -> discarded)' - so it is either the P0 fix target or must be explicitly retired, and (b) that module carries the sourced alpha2beta1 card the design tells the PI does not exist.

A0 proposes to 'Run forces_manifest.py over the adherent baseline config' where the baseline is the ac/ENGINE composed world. forces_manifest is hard-wired to the ac/CELL incumbent: _constant_channels() imports ffn_sim.ac.cell.assemble and ac.cell.compartments (forces_manifest.py:356-357), and dump_force_channels unconditionally calls assert_force_channels_cover_accumulate (:735), which statically parses ac/cell/driver.py::_accumulate_all against a hardcoded declared set (:273, :311-317). Run as specified it audits a DIFFERENT runtime than the one that executed - itself a metric-measures-the-wrong-thing defect. An engine-side observer is new code, not an extension, and 0.5 day is not the cost.

A6's rigid-limit protocol names a function that does not act on the object under test: 'sweep ECM/substrate stiffness upward toward the rigid limit using ff/substrate.py:48 resolve_substrate'. resolve_substrate returns k_sub for the Winkler ANCHOR path (substrate.py:46-55, kernels at :74 and :90), which is not wired into ECMStateOwner at all; stiffening the live Mikado collagen is a different operation (fibre modulus, crosslink density). Worse, using both at once is precisely the 'clutch + substrate Winkler spring stacked on a live ECM' double-count the design's own risk register forbids. A6 proposes what the risks section prohibits.

ff/fa_ecm.py:100-109 attach_clutches_to_ecm binds each clutch to the NEAREST collagen NODE via cKDTree - a node-based attachment on a discretized fibre. Refining the segment discretization at fixed physical fibre density multiplies the candidate nodes inside the capture radius, so the clutch count and per-clutch load are intrinsically mesh-dependent. A6's grid-invariance gate is therefore at risk of failing for a reason the design never identifies, and the correct primitive is already in the engine and unused: CollagenMaterialPointEndpointView.port_ref(segment_id, u) (ecm_world.py:793-820) gives a barycentric MATERIAL POINT at fixed arclength. Reuse that, not the KD-tree.

A9 says 'Extend ac_cell_assembled_viz.py with an adhesion isolation scene'. That script states at :10 and :16 that it is 'fully data-driven: the scene set is assembled from a state dump with NO per-component hardcoding' and that a new component 'gets its scenes automatically' once it appears in the dump. The work is in ac/engine/dump_state.py, not in the viz script.

Stage 3's A/B is not runnable against the engine solver as described. cg_check_every exists in both ac/cell/implicit_mechanics.py:1469 and ac/engine/sf_implicit.py:306,313, but the assembled per-fibre coarse path lives only in ac/cell (implicit_mechanics.py:1469 mg_assembled_coarse, :1916, fiber_arclength_mg.py:339,583, fiber_quotient_coarse.py). One of the two speed wins would have to be ported into the engine solver first - unbudgeted, and it crosses the frozen ac/cell boundary.
arithmetic_corrections: A5's central criterion is off by roughly four orders of magnitude in required statistics. With the recorded INTEGRIN_A5B1 constants (hand_kmc.py:14-16: kc0=0.4/s, Fc=7pN, ks0=0.5/s, Fs=30pN, KBT=4.28001e-3 pN.um) I computed k_off(0)=0.9000/s (lifetime 1.1111 s) and k_off(F*)=0.77855/s (lifetime 1.2844 s) - the catch peak is only +15.6% in mean lifetime. Across F=5,6,7,8,9 pN the lifetimes are 1.27146, 1.28131, 1.28443, 1.28145, 1.27306 s: a 0.13% spread over a 4 pN window. Lifetimes are exponential (CV=1), so SEM = tau/sqrt(N). Merely establishing the +15.6% peak at 3 sigma needs N >= (3/0.156)^2 ~= 370 events per bin; LOCATING the peak position (which criterion (a) explicitly demands) needs ~1e6 events per bin, i.e. ~1e7 unbinding events. At k_off ~= 0.8/s over the dependency's 10 FA sites that is 1e7/(10*0.8) = 1.25e6 s ~= 14.5 days of SIMULATED time, ~1.25e8 outer steps at dt=0.01 s, each with a stiff implicit CG solve. Infeasible by any budget. The design states no N, no confidence interval and no null - the same error class as the retracted '16 sigma' that turned out to be a within-realization SEM.

A2's negative control (a) does not fail the way stated. With x_catch = 0, k_off(F) = kc0 + ks0*exp(F*xs/kT) is monotone increasing, and I confirmed the numerical argmin over F in [0,60] lands at index 0, i.e. F = 0.0 - a minimum DOES exist at the sweep boundary. A gate phrased as 'a catch minimum exists' PASSES for pure slip. It only fails because the analytic F* becomes kT/xs * ln(0) = -inf and the comparison inherits an inf/NaN. Restate as: argmin index strictly interior (0 < i < N-1) AND k_off(argmin) < k_off(0) by a stated margin.

A7's maturation timescales make its 1-2 day estimate and its needs_gpu framing incoherent. TALIN_KU0 = 3.0e-4/s (fa_maturation.py:32); at F = 5 pN, F*dx/kT = 5*5e-4/4.28001e-3 = 0.584, so k_unfold = 3e-4*exp(0.584) = 5.4e-4/s, i.e. a ~1850 s mechanosensor. VIN_KREC = 0.03/s -> ~33 s. FA_KG0-FA_KD = 0.005/s -> the area fixed point has a >= 200 s time constant. Reaching a dA/dt fixed point needs O(1e3) s of physical time = O(1e5) outer steps at dt=0.01 with an implicit solve. Conversely, if the step only EVALUATES the instantaneous rate versus load, it needs no joint and no GPU and should be needs_gpu=false. As written it is neither - and the closed form F_fix = F_th*(k_d/(k_g0-k_d))^(1/n) is the correct algebraic root of fa_growth_rate (fa_maturation.py:67-68), so comparing the kernel's zero-crossing to it is again transcription, not physics.

Effort total is understated by roughly 3-5x. The listed steps sum to 0.5+0.5+0.5+3.5+2+2.5+2+1.5+2.5+1.5 ~= 17 days. Not budgeted anywhere: (i) the declared HARD PREREQ implicit solver for a stiff clutch in series into alpha-actinin at 4.6e5-8.2e5 pN/um (hand_kmc FILAMIN link_k=8.2e5, adhesion_clutch k_int=800) gets 0 days despite the SF slice being documented non-convergent at 15.5%; (ii) a device-resident point-to-SEGMENT capture search returning barycentric u (new_code item 4) is a new Warp neighbour structure, folded into A3; (iii) an engine-side forces_manifest observer, folded into A0's 0.5 day; (iv) porting the assembled per-fibre coarse into the engine solver for Stage 3; (v) 10 new device reductions plus host reference twins. A3 alone is 1-2 weeks, not 3-4 days.

The staging order is inverted against its own arithmetic. Stage 3 (speed) is placed after Stage 2, but Stage 2's own timescales (talin ~1850 s, FA area >= 200 s, bond statistics above) are unreachable without the ~40x from the two default-off wins. Speed is a PREREQUISITE for Stage 2, not its successor. Say so to the PI rather than asking whether adhesion should precede speed.
ducked_questions: ION CHANNELS - asked directly, never answered. The design mentions Piezo1 only as a 'Secondary' clause inside open_question #9 and takes no position, even though ff/piezo.py exists (tension-gated) and is in the reuse pool. Worse, the design's own sharp criterion ('a force that appears in the momentum balance with an equal-and-opposite reaction') actually INCLUDES the ion channels that set osmotic turgor: the PI-ratified constant Pi_0 = 40 Pa presses the cell onto the coat and is part of the basal load path. Turgor appears nowhere in the design's adherent baseline, which violates the physiological-baseline HARD rule ('the production config must still turn it ON at its physiological value') and leaves a force channel out of A0's confound audit. Give a position: mechanically-consequential channels (turgor-setting transporters, Piezo1) are IN as pressure/parameter channels and must be audited; kinase cascades are OUT.

GPU-ONLY BOND SEARCH - open_question #10 asks the PI whether an accepted-step-only host partner search is admissible. The hard rule already answers it: 'every physics kernel, PDE/KMC update, NEIGHBOR QUERY, and mechanical iteration is GPU-resident Warp with no authoritative per-step host state.' A bond partner search is a neighbour query feeding a KMC update. Asking is a hedge on a settled rule, and it conveniently reduces Stage 1 effort ('This changes the Stage 1 effort materially'). Note the design also mislabels the offender: it cites ff/fa_ecm.py:24 (the scipy import line) when the host KD-tree is at :100-109, and ac/solid/adhesion_clutch.py:29 already self-labels it 'an occasional host KD-tree step, out of the hot loop'.

ALPHA2BETA1 vs ALPHA5BETA1 - open_questions #5 and #6 send the PI a question the tree already answers, based on a false premise. #5 asks whether a provisional alpha2beta1 card is acceptable 'until alpha2beta1 is sourced'; ac/solid/adhesion_clutch.py:11-16 and :51-53 already carry a sourced alpha2beta1-collagen card (Attwood 2013, DOI 10.3390/ijms14022832, k_off0=0.44/s, x_beta=0.7nm -> f_beta ~= 5.9 pN) plus a sourced k_int=800 pN/um (Chan-Odde 2008 / Bangasser 2013). #6 asks the PI to adjudicate F* ~7 pN vs KB ~30 pN - that discrepancy belongs to alpha5beta1-fibronectin (fa_clutch_warp.py:13-16, hand_kmc.py:157-161) and is irrelevant if the baseline is alpha2beta1, which has no F* at all. Two PI decisions burned on already-answered questions, while the ONE real question - 'the sourced alpha2beta1 is slip-only; do we accept a slip-only integrin, and does that conflict with anything?' - is never asked. Note the 2026-06-21 catch-bond ratification the design leans on is CADHERIN (KU-4.2, Rakshit), explicitly not integrin (hand_kmc.py:157-158 says so), so A2's negative control labelling pure slip 'the forbidden abstracted option' flags the sourced physics as a violation.

CYTOSOL / MEDIUM - the PI baseline is 'cell in MEDIA, adherent on a 2D ECM'. The design's Stage 1 world is sf_arc + ECM + NMII with cortex as a port: no membrane, no cytosol, no medium, no turgor, and none of surface_porous_transfer / membrane_cytosol_boundary. Per the tree, cytosol is already at CUDA_UNIT. The design neither wires it nor states the omission as a labelled scope cut. 'Adherent cell in media' with no media should be called what it is.

The 'small basal patch' promise contradicts the geometry the named dependency supplies. Dependencies say 'Stage 1 can honestly start from a resting near-spherical cell contacting the plane over a small basal patch' and that spreading area 'must not be quoted from a Stage 1 artifact'. But sf_population.py:484-485 puts ventral FA ends at x = +/- 0.9*R in the z=0 plane - a 13.5 um basal span on a 7.5 um-radius cell, i.e. an already-spread footprint. The Stage 1 render will LOOK fully spread while the label says spreading is out of scope. Either rebuild the population for a small patch or state the contradiction in the artifact label.

A0 pass criterion (b) demands that ff/motility_warp.py:331 gravity_kernel 'report enabled=False or absent-from-config'. Its docstring says the opposite of what the design assumes: 'This is REAL physics (a derived body force ~ 1 pN/cell at MCF7 size), NOT a tuned proxy - it rests the cell on the substrate.' Under the physiological-baseline HARD rule an adherent cell in media DOES carry gravity minus buoyancy, so demanding enabled=False is itself a rule violation and an over-correction. The correct gate is enabled=True with provenance=DERIVED and value within a stated factor of Delta_rho*g*v_node; flag any deviation. Criterion (b) is also internally inconsistent: it accepts 'absent-from-config' while forbidding 'unobserved', which is the same state (forces_manifest.py:24-27 defines absence as enabled=None / observation='unobserved').

result.summary: Track 11's diagnostic content is the best part and three of its self-corrections are exactly right (verified: commit 09c14eb8 says "Full-fine applies/V-cycle 27-43 -> constant 4", and FINE_MESH_MULTIGRID_DESIGN_2026-07-24.md:377-378 records MG+FIX1+FIX2 at 1463 s vs the MG-off incumbent's 568 s = 2.58x SLOWER in wall; FIX1's host `self.active.numpy()[0]` at implicit_mechanics.py:2078-2080 really does violate driver.py:1201; CORTEX_KINK_AUDIT_2026-07-25.md really does reduce the MG line to a preconditioner). But the track as specified is not executable, for three independent structural reasons, each of which breaks several steps. (1) WRONG SOLVER: the 171.89 s headline came from `inner_solver = "erm_gauss_seidel_tournament"` (probe ledger), and `ProjectedAnalyticCG.solve()` runs ONLY under `analytic_implicit` (driver.py:483); with `implicit_coarse_modes = 0` the tournament's `preconditioned_direction` path never reaches `_operator` (its only in-preconditioner call site, implicit_mechanics.py:1929-1930, is gated on coarse_modes). So `_operator` — the object of S0's profiling, S4's transpose, S5's capture and S6's roofline — is NEVER CALLED on the baseline that produced the number. The real hot path is `_accumulate_all` + projector, run 16x per inner iteration (driver.py:352, 538-551), ~26.9 ms per evaluation, and it rebuilds the steric HashGrid every single time (steric_warp.py:157-158) — which also kills S5's capture scope, the opposite of what the design asserts. (2) BIT-IDENTITY IS PRECLUDED: `_dot_kernel` atomically adds into ONE f64 scalar over 551,434 threads (implicit_mechanics.py:1330-1333, launched 4x/CG iteration), every stiffness/force kernel uses per-node `wp.atomic_add` (implicit_mechanics.py:134-136, 190-192, 208-343), the ledger resultants likewise (ledger.py:103,113,123) — 192 atomic sites in ac/. CUDA f64 atomicAdd is arrival-order dependent, so same-seed re-runs are not bit-reproducible and the "BIT-IDENTICAL"/"BYTE-IDENTICAL" primary criteria of S1, S3, S4, S5 and S6 fail for reasons unrelated to the optimisation. (3) THE HEADLINE METRIC IS STRUCTURALLY ZERO: `outer_accepted = inner_converged` (driver.py:1125) and convergence needs max|PF|*dt_mu <= tol, i.e. max|PF| <= 7.449e-9/3.536e-8 = 0.211 pN against an actual 1483 pN — a factor 7000, and per the project's own GATE A verdict that residual is intrinsic discrete-myosin non-equilibrium (a MODELING decision). So "committed physical seconds per wall hour" is 0 for every arm and every ratio the track mandates is 0/0. Net: 8 of 10 steps have a primary pass criterion that cannot be evaluated as written. The step skeleton survives and the fixes are edits rather than a rewrite, hence NEEDS_REVISION rather than BROKEN — but nothing beyond a re-scoped S0 should be scheduled until items 1-3 are repaired.
must_fix: RE-SCOPE S0 ONTO THE PATH THAT ACTUALLY RUNS. The headline artifact records `inner_solver: erm_gauss_seidel_tournament` (resting_native_probe_2026-07-23.json ledger); driver.py:350-351 expands that to families (block_descent, anderson, erm_gauss_seidel, rkc1) and driver.py:483 shows `implicit_cg` is non-None only for `analytic_implicit`. With the probe's `implicit_coarse_modes: 0`, `_build_preconditioner`'s only `_operator` call (implicit_mechanics.py:1929-1930) is skipped, so `ProjectedAnalyticCG._operator` is never invoked. S0 must profile `_accumulate_all` (driver.py:141-167), `project_constraint_forces_kernel` (inner_mechanics.py:79-140), the WCA path including `StericForce._accumulate_pos` (steric_warp.py:156-174), and the tournament's candidate/line-search loop — not `_operator`/`_precondition`.

INSERT A DETERMINISM BASELINE AS THE FIRST STEP (S0b), WITH A PRE-REGISTERED FALLBACK. Run the identical native binary twice, same seed, same GPU, cleared Warp cache, and report whether the committed state is bit-identical. Given `wp.atomic_add(out, 0, ...)` in `_dot_kernel` (implicit_mechanics.py:1330-1333) and 192 atomic sites in ac/, expect NO. Pre-register the fallback now, not after the fact: acceptance moves to order-independent observables (`max_force_kernel`'s `wp.atomic_max`, inner_mechanics.py:189-192; integer counts; topology hashes; the documented race-free steric own-row RMW, steric_warp.py:9-16) plus a ULP budget derived from the measured self-repeat spread. Do NOT let the fallback be chosen after a failed bit-identity check — that is the gate-loosening the project forbids.

REPLACE THE MANDATED THROUGHPUT METRIC. `committed physical seconds per wall hour` is identically 0 on the baseline because `outer_accepted = inner_converged` (driver.py:1125-1127) and the third convergence clause (inner_mechanics.py:290-299) demands max|PF| <= 0.211 pN against 1483 pN. Report instead: wall per attempted outer step AT A FIXED achieved residual AND a fixed iteration budget; residual reduction per unit wall; per-stage kernel time; launches per step. Declare the accept-ratio axis BLOCKED on the GATE-A modeling decision rather than presenting it as a throughput observable.

FIX S0's CLOSURE CRITERION so it cannot fail when the design's own hypothesis is true. `wp.timing_begin(wp.TIMING_KERNEL)` returns GPU kernel times; launch gaps and Python launch overhead are exactly the wall it excludes, and those gaps ARE the latency-bound signal. Demanding Sum(kernel) == wall to 5% converts the most valuable observable into a failure. Report a three-way decomposition (Sum kernel + Sum memcpy + residual gap = wall) and gate only on the decomposition summing, with the residual gap published as the launch-overhead number. Also note the instrumentation cost: with ~6,400 force assemblies per outer step (16 candidates x 400 iterations), TIMING_KERNEL inserts on the order of 1e5 event pairs and will itself inflate the wall.

MOVE THE HOST-SIDE LOOP COUNTERS TO DEVICE ARRAYS BEFORE ANY `capture_while` WORK. implicit_mechanics.py:2066 bakes `wp.int32(iteration)` into `_cg_finalize_kernel`, which writes `iterations[0] = iteration`; inner_mechanics.py:277 and :306 take host `iteration` and host `slot`. Captured once, these freeze — arm C would destroy the iterations-to-latch histogram that S1 itself claims to measure. The in-tree capture precedent the design cites states this hazard verbatim (dcm_warp_hybrid.py:242-243: remesh off, no realloc in-graph, RNG step arg frozen at capture).

ADD THE MISSING CROSS-BLOCK COUPLING CHANNEL TO S3. The production solver globalizes through ONE device scalar: `_evaluate_projected_residual` reduces to `candidate_residual_d` (driver.py:538-551) and the best-candidate copy is gated by a device flag derived from it (driver.py:752-802, `best_candidate_d`, `take_trial_d`, `implicit_scale_accept_counts_d`). A shared line-search scalar means block 0's geometry chooses block 1's step scale — mechanical coupling that GATE 2 (force-only re-evaluation) and control 3 (NaN -> reject) both miss. Enumerate per-block line-search/candidate-acceptance scalars alongside the hash grid, dots and regularizer, and add a control that deliberately shares the line-search scalar.

RE-KEY THE DEVICE RNG PER BLOCK OR DROP S3 VARIANT B. Kinetics use `wp.rand_init(rng_seed ^ rng_epoch[0], tid)` on the GLOBAL element index: erm_tether.py:208,316; motor/segment_motor.py:131,175,226,442; motor/hand.py:153,203,244; engine/microtubule_rig.py:751. Index-blocked concatenation re-keys every stochastic draw, so a batched realization cannot be byte-identical to the same realization standalone at the same seed — GATE 1, which gates everything else, fails by construction. Book the >=13-site block-local-id change, or restrict S3 to variant A.

DE-SYNCHRONISE THE DRIVER LOOP BEFORE COSTING S3 VARIANT A. driver.py:1099 and :1115 call `wp.synchronize_device` inside the outer step (plus three more at :1060/:1063/:1072 when profiling), and ~14 per-step `.numpy()` readbacks follow at driver.py:1117-1127 / fluid/scheduler.py:282-303. A device-wide sync serialises every stream, so stream-parallel R cells gain nothing until the loop is restructured. The design's own cited precedent already caps the expectation: ENGINE_ACCELERATION_PLAN_2026-07-07.md:62-65 says 3-8x at n_fil~100, 'NOT at native 38k (single cortex already saturates); host-RNG KMC + per-fiber reshape cap the win'.

REWRITE S6(i). The ledger resultants are built with `wp.atomic_add` into single accumulators (ledger.py:103,113,123) and the gate is |reaction + traction|^2 (ledger.py:126-146) — a near-cancellation of large opposing sums, so atomic-order jitter is amplified to O(1) relative on the near-zero residual. Byte-identity is impossible in the pass direction; and once relaxed to a tolerance the f32-force negative control stops discriminating, because a plain no-op re-run would also 'fail'. Either make the two resultant reductions deterministic (two-pass tree reduction, and book its cost) or specify the control as a signal-to-noise comparison against the measured self-repeat spread with a pre-registered separation factor.

STATE THE ADHERENT-ON-2D-COLLAGEN COST DELTA, OR STATE THAT EVERY NUMBER IN THE TRACK IS PRE-BASELINE. The probe ledger records `N_fa_sites: 0`, `N_linc_sites: 0`, `per_region: {cortex}` only — a suspended resting cell with no ECM and no substrate contact. The 3,438x, the 24-days/run, the 65-GPU-years and all ten effort estimates are for a configuration that is explicitly not the PI's stated baseline.

DOWNGRADE S8 FROM A SCHEDULED STEP TO A BLOCKED ITEM WITH AN EXPLICIT ENTRY CONDITION (a stated wall-per-outer-step threshold). 300 training runs x 12,000 outer steps x 171.89 s = 6.2e8 s = 19.6 GPU-years; even at 100x it is 72 GPU-days. Booking '3-4 wk' next to that reads as schedulable.

WITHDRAW THE ROOFLINE NUMBERS AND RE-DERIVE THEM ON THE CORRECT STAGE. 3.02 ms is ff/'s per-CG-iteration time (including its preconditioner and reductions) for a different engine and a different solver; the ac production evaluation is ~26.9 ms (171.89 s / 400 iters / 16 slots). The qualitative conclusion (far below both roofs, so latency/occupancy/neighbour-query bound) probably survives and may strengthen, but R2's '5-8x utilisation headroom' inherits an order-of-magnitude attribution error.
tautological_gates: S0 CLOSURE IDENTITY IS SELF-DEFEATING: 'sum of per-kernel CUDA-event times equals stage wall to within 5%' fails precisely when the design's central hypothesis (launch/latency-bound) is TRUE, because CUDA-event kernel times exclude launch gaps and host overhead. The gap it treats as error is the observable it most needs.

'WITHIN THE MEASURED RUN-TO-RUN SPREAD' / 'WITHIN NOISE' IS A POST-HOC SELF-DEFINING TOLERANCE, used in S2(i), S2's h-independence clause, S3 GATE 3 and S6(iii). No pre-registered number. The in-tree precedent is STRICTER and should be reused: test_fiber_arclength_vcycle.py:369-371 pre-registers `red < 0.6` and `red17 <= red9 * 1.25`.
S2 CRITERION (iv) REQUIRES A CONVERGED OUTER STATE WHOSE NON-EXISTENCE IS THE DESIGN'S OWN HEADLINE FACT (inner_converged=false, inner_iters=400=budget, driver.py:1125-1127). Un-evaluable as written.

S3 GATE 2 CANNOT FAIL ON THE DOMINANT COUPLING CHANNEL. It perturbs block i and re-checks block j's FORCES, but the production tournament couples through the single global line-search residual scalar (driver.py:538-551, 752-802). Sharing that scalar produces real coupling that GATE 2, control 3 (NaN -> reject) and even GATE 1 (which would fail but be blamed on atomics/RNG) do not isolate.

THE 'ALREADY WIRED' ZERO-DtoH EVIDENCE IS VACUOUS IN THE ONLY NATIVE ARTIFACT. driver.py:1032 initialises `hot_dtoh_copies = positive_dtoh_copies = 0`; the probe records `hot_loop_dtoh_copies = 0` AND `profiler_positive_control_dtoh_copies = 0`, i.e. profile_memcpy was OFF and the zero is a default. `profile_memcpy` has no caller in the repo other than the CLI flag at driver.py:1395. Listing it under '(i) IMPLEMENTED + WIRED' is an overclaim; S0's third negative control is the right test but the design must also mark the existing zero as non-evidence so nobody cites it.

S2's 'h-INDEPENDENCE' IS A DIFFERENT h FROM THE ONE THE GREEN TEST PROVES. test_fiber_arclength_vcycle.py:363-371 refines along FIBER ARCLENGTH (9 vs 17 nodes/fiber, 2 vs 3 MG levels, CPU, crosslink-free operator). S2 proposes two CORTEX MESH resolutions. Citing the green test as CPU validation for S2's claim is the metric-measuring-something-else shape.

S1's RATIONALE THAT 'BIT-IDENTITY IS AVAILABLE HERE BY CONSTRUCTION, BECAUSE EVERY POST-CONVERGENCE KERNEL ALREADY GATES ON THE DEVICE LATCH' CONFLATES TWO THINGS. The latch argument covers post-convergence no-op launches; it says nothing about atomic reduction ordering (implicit_mechanics.py:1330-1333). The 'strongest possible acceptance test' is asserted, not established.
hidden_magnitude_deps: S3 GATE 4 ('peak HBM measured by NVML, not estimated') NEEDS AN OBSERVABLE THAT IS DISABLED ON THE TARGET MACHINE. gpu_memory_accounting.py:5 states the driver must have accounting mode enabled before the process starts, and :22 states the module never calls nvmlDeviceSetAccountingMode and never invokes sudo. The probe records `gpu_memory_accounting_probe_status: ACCOUNTING_DISABLED`, `gpu_memory_accounting_mode_enabled: False`, `gpu_memory_accounting_status: PARTIAL_MEMPOOL_ONLY`. Enabling it is a root-level `nvidia-smi -am 1` on the gbook — an ops prerequisite the design never names, so R (ensemble width) is not measurable as specified.

R2's ENSEMBLE SIZING USES THE WRONG ENGINE'S MEMORY FOOTPRINT. '84-132 MB/cell measured (sc0)' is ff/ (sc0_native70k_full.json: hbm_used_mb 84.259, Nc 494802, no membrane/nucleus/field/Biot). The ac native probe reports `warp_mempool_used_high_bytes = 895,599,775` (0.896 GB) and `gpu_bytes_observed_after_step = 1,127,284,736` (1.127 GB). 84-132 MB/cell implies R ~ 120-190; the measured ac figure implies R ~ 12-13. The design's stated R range (10-30) is right by accident and wrong by derivation.

THE DESIGN CLAIMS ac PEAK HBM IS ABSENT ('the only in-tree ac figure is an explicit estimate ... order 3-6 GB') WHILE QUOTING THE VERY ARTIFACT THAT CONTAINS TWO MEASURED FIGURES (mempool high-water 0.896 GB, device-observed 1.127 GB, same JSON). An observable listed as missing that is present in the design's own headline source.

S7's dt-PLATEAU ANCHOR IS UNNAMED AND ESCALATED TO PI. That is a legitimate ask, but combined with the flatness finding below it means S7 is not schedulable as written: without a named, dt-sensitive observable the refinement study can be flat by construction.

EVERY NUMBER IN THE TRACK IS FROM A SUSPENDED, EXPLICITLY NON-PHYSIOLOGICAL CONFIG, NOT THE PI's BASELINE. The probe's own ledger self-labels: `resting_bound_myosin_source: 'TEST-native-probe NOT physiological'`, `physiological_preload_status: BLOCKED_UNSOURCED_SINGLE_ERM_CAPACITY_BASIS`, `erm_kinetics_mode: DIAGNOSTIC_HARD_THRESHOLD_NOT_PRODUCTION`, `erm_pairing_mode: RADIAL_ONE_PER_MEMBRANE_NODE_DIAGNOSTIC`, `erm_density_source: ABSENT_FROM_CONTRACT_GRAPH`, `resting_bound_myosin_eligible_shortfall: true` (realized fraction 0.170 vs requested 0.30), and `overlap_free_cortex: false` against the driver default of True. Calling it 'the existential number, from a committed artifact, not an estimate' overstates what it is.
sums_to_zero_risks: THE TRACK'S MANDATED HEADLINE METRIC IS IDENTICALLY ZERO FOR A REASON NO SPEED WORK CAN CHANGE. The design decrees that the only reportable metric is committed physical seconds per wall hour, and repeats 'wall per COMMITTED physical second' in S1, S3, S4, S5 and S7. But driver.py:1125-1127 sets `outer_accepted = inner_converged` / `committed_time = dt_phys if inner_converged else 0.0`, and `inner_converged` requires all three of (inner_mechanics.py:290-299) max_displacement <= tol, max_constraint_error <= tol, and max|PF| * dt_mu <= tol. On the probe the first two pass by six orders (4.46e-15 and 1.22e-15 against 7.449e-9); the failing clause is the third, which needs max|PF| <= 7.449e-9 / 3.535943748517097e-8 = 0.211 pN against an actual ~1483 pN. Per the project's own GATE-A verdict that residual is intrinsic discrete-myosin local non-equilibrium requiring ~7x heads (unphysical), i.e. a MODELING decision. So every arm reports 0.0 and every ratio is 0/0 — the track cannot distinguish its own arms. Note also that the rejected candidate REDUCED the residual 2634.12 -> 1483.10 (44%) and was still rolled back: the step is discarded by a threshold, not by divergence, which the design's framing ('this is why speed is the product') misattributes.

S2's 'WALL PER DECADE OF RESIDUAL REDUCTION' HAS A STRUCTURALLY ZERO DENOMINATOR ON THE VERY CONFIGURATION S2 IS SPECIFIED FOR. FINE_MESH_MULTIGRID_DESIGN_2026-07-24.md:377-378 records both arms as residual-FLAT (OFF 'flat it5->39' at 4.0742; ON 'flat it10->39' at 3.4158). Flat means rho = 1, decades = 0, wall/decade = infinite for both arms. The design quotes the flatness in its own current_state and does not notice.
S3 GATE 3 (T(R)/T(1) > 1 AND MONOTONE) INHERITS THE ZERO: T(R) is defined in committed physical seconds, which is 0 for all R, so the gate evaluates 0/0.

S7's ACCEPT-RATIO REGRESSION GATE CANNOT FIRE. 'A throughput gain accompanied by a degraded accept ratio is a REGRESSION' — the accept ratio is already 0 and cannot degrade. Half of S7's anti-cheating protection is inert. The paired achieved-residual half does work and should carry the whole load.

THE OBVIOUS S7 ANCHOR OBSERVABLE IS EMPIRICALLY FLAT. The two committed native probes differ only in myosin capture radius; `resting_bound_myosin_n_bound` goes 1506 -> 2652 (+76%) yet `residual_start` is identical to all 16 digits (2634.1191655118346) and `residual_candidate` moves 7e-10 relative (1483.1048741614643 -> 1483.104875297183). An observable that moves 1e-9 when the bound-motor population moves 76% is a flat-by-construction plateau, i.e. exactly the vacuous refinement study S7's own negative control is meant to prevent.

S3 GATE 2 RUN IN THE 'DESIRED' DIRECTION IS THE WEAKER DIRECTION. The original merged-array bug was detected because coupling was ABSENT where it should have been present (cortex 39.8 nm, MT aster and nucleus 0.0 nm). Here block-diagonality is the desired outcome, so a gate that asserts zero response passes trivially for any implementation that simply does nothing across blocks — including one where a block silently never advances. Pair GATE 2 with a positive control that block j DOES respond to a perturbation inside block j.
reuse_errors: THE DESIGN OPTIMISES A SOLVER THE MEASURED BASELINE DOES NOT RUN. The 171.89 s headline is `inner_solver: erm_gauss_seidel_tournament` (probe ledger), expanded at driver.py:350-351 to (block_descent, anderson, erm_gauss_seidel, rkc1). `implicit_cg = analytic_workspace if inner_solver == 'analytic_implicit' else None` (driver.py:483) — so `ProjectedAnalyticCG.solve()` never runs. In the tournament, ProjectedAnalyticCG is reached only as `tangent_accelerator` via `preconditioned_direction` (driver.py:679; implicit_mechanics.py:1994-2006), which calls `_build_preconditioner` + `_precondition`; with the probe's `implicit_coarse_modes: 0` the only `_operator` call inside `_build_preconditioner` (implicit_mechanics.py:1929-1930) is skipped. S0's stated target ('per-kernel time for every kernel inside one _operator apply') profiles dead code on the baseline it cites.

THE REAL HOT PATH IS FORCE ASSEMBLY, NOT THE CG OPERATOR, AND IT IS UNPROFILED IN THE DESIGN. `_evaluate_projected_residual` (driver.py:538-551) = `_accumulate_all` + `project_constraint_forces_kernel` + `max_force_kernel`, repeated over `acceptance_slots = len(candidate_families) * implicit_line_search_steps = 4 * 4 = 16` (driver.py:352; probe `implicit_line_search_steps: 4`). 171.89 s / 400 iters = 429.7 ms per inner iteration; / 16 = ~26.9 ms per force+project evaluation, ~9x the 3.02 ms the design attributes to an 'operator apply'.

S5's CAPTURE-SCOPE CLAIM IS FALSE ON THE PRODUCTION PATH: `HashGrid.build` RUNS INSIDE THE INNER LOOP. `_accumulate_all` calls `cell.steric.accumulate` (driver.py:164) -> `StericForce._accumulate_pos` which launches `pos_to_f32` then `self.grid.build(self._qpts, float(self.r_c))` on EVERY call (steric_warp.py:157-158). That is ~6,400 grid rebuilds per outer step (16 x 400). S5's own audit ('no allocation, no HashGrid.build, no .numpy() inside the captured region') fails immediately, and the design's justification — 'the grid build already sits outside the CG loop, verified at implicit_mechanics.py:1732-1737 which consumes a prebuilt steric.grid.id' — is true only of the dead `_operator` path. The precedent it cites states the same constraint (dcm_warp_hybrid.py:242-243).

`wp.capture_while` CANNOT CAPTURE THE LOOP AS WRITTEN. implicit_mechanics.py:2066 passes host `wp.int32(iteration)` into `_cg_finalize_kernel` (defined ~:1388), which writes `iterations[0] = iteration`; captured once, it freezes, so arm C returns a wrong iteration count and destroys the iterations-to-latch histogram S1 promises to measure. Same blocker for the outer inner-solve loop: `update_convergence_kernel(iteration: wp.int32)` (inner_mechanics.py:277) and `record_convergence_history_kernel(slot, iteration)` (inner_mechanics.py:306).

BIT-IDENTITY, THE TRACK'S ONLY SAFETY NET, IS PRECLUDED BY THE CODE. `_dot_kernel` does `wp.atomic_add(out, 0, wp.dot(a[i], b[i]))` over 551,434 threads into ONE f64 scalar (implicit_mechanics.py:1330-1333), launched at :2048, :2050, :2057, :2071 (4x per CG iteration); every stiffness/force accumulation uses per-node `wp.atomic_add` (implicit_mechanics.py:134-136, 190-192, 208-209, 225-226, 252-253, 282-283, 307-308, 341-343); 192 atomic sites across ac/. CUDA f64 atomicAdd is arrival-order dependent and FP addition is non-associative. S1 ('dx BIT-IDENTICAL'), S3 GATE 1/2 ('BYTE-IDENTICAL'), S4 ('output must be bit-identical'), S5 ('committed state BIT-IDENTICAL') and S6(i) ('ledger residual BYTE-IDENTICAL') therefore all fail for reasons unrelated to the optimisation. What IS order-independent and should carry the load: `max_force_kernel`'s `wp.atomic_max` (inner_mechanics.py:189-192), integer counts (`implicit_scale_accept_counts_d`), and the documented race-free own-row steric RMW (steric_warp.py:9-16).

S3 VARIANT B IS BROKEN BY DEVICE RNG KEYING, AND THE DESIGN NEVER MENTIONS IT. Kinetics draw from `wp.rand_init(rng_seed ^ rng_epoch[0], tid)` keyed on the GLOBAL element index: erm_tether.py:208,316; motor/segment_motor.py:131,175,226,442; motor/hand.py:153,203,244; engine/microtubule_rig.py:751. Index-blocked concatenation re-keys every draw, so GATE 1 ('byte-identical to that realization run standalone at the same seed') fails by construction. >=13 kernels need a block-local id — unbooked new code.

S3 VARIANT A IS BLOCKED BY DEVICE-WIDE SYNCS AND PER-STEP HOST READBACK IN THE DRIVER LOOP. driver.py:1099 and :1115 call `wp.synchronize_device` inside the outer step (plus :1060/:1063/:1072 under profiling), and ~14 `.numpy()` readbacks follow (driver.py:1117-1127; fluid/scheduler.py:282-303). A device-wide sync serialises all streams. The design's own precedent caps the expectation anyway: ENGINE_ACCELERATION_PLAN_2026-07-07.md:33 asserts native force kernels saturate the A5000 so 'ensemble-batching and launch-overhead (CUDA-graph) wins shrink to ~1.1-1.5x', and :62-65 says the 3-8x was at n_fil~100 and 'NOT at native 38k'.

S6's LEDGER BYTE-IDENTITY IS BOTH UNACHIEVABLE AND, ONCE RELAXED, INSENSITIVE. The resultants are `wp.atomic_add` accumulations (ledger.py:103,113,123) feeding a near-cancellation |reaction + traction|^2 (ledger.py:126-146), so atomic-order jitter is amplified to O(1) relative on the near-zero residual. Byte-identity is impossible; relaxed to a tolerance, the f32-force negative control no longer discriminates from a no-op re-run.

S0's PROPOSED INSTRUMENTATION SITE ONLY COVERS THE SCHEDULER BRANCH. driver.py:1059-1080 wraps `sched.outer_step`; the non-scheduler branch (driver.py:1099-1127) has no timing_begin at all, and with profile_memcpy=True on that branch `positive_dtoh_copies` stays 0 so driver.py:1201 can never pass. Extending TIMING_MEMCPY to TIMING_KERNEL at that one site does not instrument every path the gate scripts use.

S5 AND S0 ARE MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE ON THE SAME ARM. `wp.timing_begin(wp.TIMING_KERNEL)` cannot resolve per-kernel times inside a replayed CUDA graph, so once S5 lands the profile that justifies the whole track is no longer takeable on the optimised path. Unaddressed sequencing conflict.

MINOR: prior dt-axis METHODOLOGY exists and is uncited — scripts/h7_dt_push_test.py already frames it correctly ('the largest multiple where gamma holds AND drift stays tiny', accuracy not stability) and scripts/h7_native_dt_sweep.py is a step-count sweep. Both are HOOMD/CPU-legacy so not executable, but the protocol is portable. Also, the proposed 'throughput accounting module' is largely aggregation over fields driver.py already emits (`committed_time_s`, `outer_accepted`, `outer_rolled_back`, `outer_step_wall_s`, `inner_iters`, `inner_iteration_budget`, driver.py:1207-1240).

VERIFIED-AS-CLAIMED (credit where due): implicit_mechanics.py:1459 ProjectedAnalyticCG with max_iterations=32, :1469 cg_check_every, :1473-1490 validate, :2078-2080 the host-read early exit, :1984 _operator with the projector launched twice at :1986/:1988, :1932 _precondition, :1714-1717 the projector launch, :1718 _stiffness; inner_mechanics.py:79-140 the one-thread-per-fiber Thomas sweep with 168-byte stride (7 nodes x 24 B); steric_warp.py:9-11,48-51 f32 grid index with f64 force math; transaction.py:1-60; ledger.py:130-143 and :329-352 with caller-owned tolerance; verify_forces.py:384 _inject_defects and :441 _selftest; forces_manifest.yaml:494-508 with both speed flags PI-owned and off; test_warp_only_contract.py (69 lines); ac_cortex_mesh_ab.py; gpu_memory_accounting.py; ensemble.py:431 run() and :458-460 the serial host loop; fiber_arclength_mg.py (888 lines); fiber_quotient_coarse.py; deflated_pcg.py; dcm_warp_hybrid.py:246,252; sf_implicit.py:306-323 and :313 cg_check_every default 0; all nine test_fiber_arclength_vcycle.py line references; Warp 1.14.0 with capture_while(condition: warp.array[int], while_body), capture_if, is_conditional_graph_supported, ScopedStream, TIMING_KERNEL all present and zero call sites in ac/ff; the Arruda SBI numbers (NPE NRMSE 0.20, 32,100 sims, ~1 s inference vs ABC 66,000-432,000) at references/analysis/25_...md:48-50.
arithmetic_corrections: 'THE GAP IS ~4-6 ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE' IS NOT DERIVABLE FROM ANY NUMBER IN THE DOCUMENT, AND THE ERROR IS STRATEGIC. Its own arithmetic: 1,000 runs x 600 s / 0.05 s = 1.2e7 outer steps x 171.89 s = 2.06e9 s = 65.4 GPU-years (both verified). To one GPU-month (2.59e6 s) that is 795x = 2.9 orders; to one GPU-year, 65x; on 8 GPUs over 3 months, 33x. Real-time equivalence for a single run is 3,438x = 3.5 orders. The honest gap is ~1e2-1e3, not 1e4-1e6. At ~800x, R3 (multi-GPU, Nx) + R4 (step-count, 2-100x) + R2 (ensemble, 4-10x) plausibly close it WITHOUT a neural surrogate — which changes the answer to the design's own hardest PI question and de-prioritises the 3-4 week S8.

BANDWIDTH ROOF UNDERSTATED BY ~1.6x: '10-20 x 11.9 MB against 768 GB/s predicts ~0.3-0.5 ms'. 494,802 x 24 B = 11.875 MB (correct); 10 x 11.875 MB / 768 GB/s = 0.155 ms, 20x = 0.31 ms. Correct range 0.15-0.31 ms, so observed/roof is ~10-20x, not ~5x. Direction favours the design's hypothesis; the stated number is still wrong.

THE 3.02 ms 'PER OPERATOR APPLY' IS AN ff/ PER-CG-ITERATION TIME, NOT AN ac OPERATOR APPLY. 633.8655916849772 / 210.1666 = 3.016 ms is arithmetically right, but sc0_native70k_full.json is the ff Cytosim-FEM engine (n_dof 1484406, clutch_n 300, substrate_n 12915, no membrane/nucleus/field/Biot) and each of its CG iterations includes its preconditioner and its reductions.
