The ac production evaluation is ~26.9 ms. Every downstream ratio ('~5x both roofs', '~15% of both roofs', R2's '5-8x utilisation headroom') inherits a ~9x attribution error.

S8 IS INFEASIBLE BY THE DESIGN'S OWN NUMBERS YET CARRIES A 3-4 WEEK ESTIMATE. 300 native training runs x 12,000 outer steps x 171.89 s = 6.19e8 s = 19.6 GPU-years; at a 100x speedup, 72 GPU-days. It must be a BLOCKED item with a numeric entry condition, not a scheduled step.

TRACK TOTAL ~78 WORKING DAYS (2.5 + 3.5 + 2.5 + 10.5 + 5 + 8.75 + 5 + 8.75 + 24.5 + 7) ~ 11 WEEKS SEQUENTIAL, all after the assembly tracks, plus procurement latency. With the unbooked work surfaced here (>=13 rand_init re-keyings, per-block hash grids / regularizer / line-search scalars, driver-loop de-synchronisation, device-side iteration counters, a determinism baseline, possibly deterministic two-pass reductions), S3 at '1-2 wk' and S5 at '1-1.5 wk' are optimistic by ~2-3x.

VERIFIED CORRECT: 12,000 x 171.89 s = 23.9 d and x1000 = 65.4 yr; 171.89 / 0.05 = 3,438x; 568 -> 1463 s = 2.58x slower (design says 2.6x); 64/12 = 5.33x (commit 09c14eb8 '~12 vs 64 iters = 5.3x'); A5000 GA102 8192 cores x 2 x ~1.695 GHz = 27.8 TF f32, /64 = 0.434 TF f64, 768 GB/s, 64 SM, 16 GB; ff deflated PCG 210.625 -> 122.5 iters with wall 899.6 -> 911.1 ms (0.987x) and the second variant 897.8 -> 1741.3 ms (0.516x); device-scalar CG 903.6 -> 832.7 ms = 1.085x; ff 70k Nc = 494,802 / n_triples = 353,430 / n_xl = 70,686 / hbm 84.259 MB; 215 lines containing float64 in implicit_mechanics.py.

ONE MORE FERMI CHECK THE DESIGN SHOULD ADD: the projector launch is only 70,686 threads on a 64-SM part (~2,209 warps, ~34.5 warps/SM against 48 max slots) and each thread walks a serial dependent Thomas chain of p = 6 over a 168-byte private stride. So the occupancy story is about the serial dependency chain and the 168-byte stride sitting inside 2 cache lines, not about thread starvation — which weakens S4's claimed 1.3-3x coalescing win (an L1/L2-resident 168 B per thread is already largely captured) and means the gather/scatter transpose S4 proposes adds two extra 11.9 MB passes for an uncertain gain.
ducked_questions: PI ITEM 3 (baseline = cell in media, ADHERENT ON 2D COLLAGEN-COATED ECM) IS NOT ANSWERED ANYWHERE. Every number is from a suspended cell: the probe ledger reads `N_fa_sites: 0`, `N_linc_sites: 0`, `N_cross_region_bonds: 0`, `per_region: {cortex: ...}` only, with no ECM or substrate-contact participant. The design mentions 'adherent-on-2D-collagen once that config exists' in an S0 protocol clause and as an S3 dependency, but never estimates the cost delta of adding focal adhesions + integrin catch-slip clutches + ECM fibers/crosslinks + membrane_ecm_contact + a contact problem + more transaction participants, and never states that its headline 65-GPU-years will be invalidated by it. 'Optimising a moving target' is listed as a risk; that is not the same as answering the PI's instruction.

PI ITEM 1/2 (MECHANICAL CONNECTEDNESS IS THE GATE, MAGNITUDES ARE NOT) IS ANSWERED ONLY IMPLICITLY. `connectors_involved: NONE` is defensible for a speed track, but the design should state plainly what fraction of Track 11 is admissible NOW — the answer is S0 alone, and S0 needs re-scoping onto force assembly first — and that everything else is post-assembly. As written, an 11-week track that contributes nothing to the PI's stated current gate is presented with no explicit statement of that fact.

THE DESIGN'S OWN MOST DECISIVE SELF-CHECK IS BURIED AS A SUB-CONTROL. 'Confirm a same-seed uncaptured re-run is bit-identical to itself' appears only as S5 negative control (c) and as a protocol sentence in S9. Per the atomic-reduction finding it is the gate that decides whether S1, S3, S4, S5 and S6 are executable at all. It must be a first-class step with its own pass/fail and a pre-registered fallback, and S1's contrary assertion ('bit-identity is available here by construction') must be withdrawn.

S7's ANCHORING OBSERVABLE IS ESCALATED TO PI WITHOUT DISCLOSING THAT THE OBVIOUS CANDIDATE IS EMPIRICALLY FLAT. The design proposes 'the accepted-step force-balance residual plus one mechanical observable' and asks PI to choose. It does not report that across the two committed native probes a +76% change in bound myosin heads (1506 -> 2652) moved `residual_start` by exactly zero digits and `residual_candidate` by 7e-10 relative. Handing PI a choice without that datum invites a flat-by-construction plateau.

WHETHER THE TRACK'S HEADLINE METRIC IS MEASURABLE TODAY IS NEVER ASKED. The design presents committed-s/wall-hour as the metric that fixes the project's ms/step confusion, and simultaneously documents the artifact in which it is 0.0. It should have asked PI directly: is the accept predicate's third clause (max|PF| <= 0.211 pN) the gate contract we intend, given the GATE-A finding that the residual is intrinsic discrete-myosin non-equilibrium? That is the actual blocking decision for the entire track, and it is nowhere in the nine open questions.

THE 'IS A HOST READBACK FOR LOOP CONTROL A VIOLATION?' QUESTION IS ASKED WELL BUT ANSWERED IN A WAY THE CODE CANNOT HONOUR YET. The recommended alternative (conditional-graph capture) is blocked by the host-side `wp.int32(iteration)` argument at implicit_mechanics.py:2066 and by `HashGrid.build` inside the force assembly (steric_warp.py:158). The recommendation should be conditioned on those two prerequisites rather than presented as 'strictly better, same skip, zero readback, fewer launches'.

THE PRECISION-PRECEDENT QUESTION IS ASKED ON TOO NARROW A BASIS. The design says 'the ONLY f32 is the steric hash-grid INDEX'. Verified true for the force math, but `wp.float32(steric.r_c)` is also passed as the query radius into `add_wca_stiffness_kernel` (implicit_mechanics.py:1736) and `wca_steric_kernel` (steric_warp.py:165) — an f32 cutoff inside a force/stiffness kernel, pruning-only but on the load path's kernel signature. The PI ruling should be asked about cutoff/threshold scalars as well as indices, since that is the boundary S6 will be argued against.

result.summary:
The design's reuse audit is genuinely accurate — I checked all ~30 cited file:line anchors and they exist and contain what is claimed (`sf_population.py:436` yields exactly 1 bundle / 2 fibers / 0 arc joints / 2 FA sites; `sf_implicit.py` is indeed untracked; `segment_query.py:125-141` really has no filament filter; `sf_motor_slice.py:160-166` metadata really is unconsumed). The scoping instinct is right and the negative-control discipline is the single best thing in it. But the two steps that carry the design's quantitative weight are both built on premises my own arithmetic refutes, and roughly a third of the blocking criteria either cannot fail or cannot pass.

THREE FINDINGS THAT INVALIDATE STEPS AS WRITTEN.

(1) M4 is dead three ways, and it hides the project's live hard-rule violation. The DERIVED stall cap `da_max=(f_stall−F)/k_xb` (`ac/motor/segment_motor.py:172`, `:223`) is a LINEAR-STALL force-velocity law, and at the driver's own documented `dt=0.01 s` (`scripts/ac_gate_b_sf_motor_native.py:66`) it OVERRIDES Hill over 70% of the load range: tau*v0 = 1.20 nm vs da_max(0) = 0.50 nm. Effective unloaded velocity is f_stall/(k_xb*dt) = 0.050 um/s, not v0 = 0.12 um/s. So M4(2) "v/v0 -> 1.000 +/- 0.01 as k_ext -> 0" FAILS by 58% on a CORRECT implementation; M4(3)'s kappa-curvature-sign check measures the cap's linear shape, so its negative control `--nc kappa-linear` cannot flip; and CLAUDE.md's "Hill force-velocity, NOT linear-stall" is being violated at runtime with no step in this track able to see it. Separately M4(4) is unreachable: with the landed constants F* = 1.3665 pN vs f_stall = 0.5 pN (2.73x), so the slip branch is never entered, the off-rate moves only 0.700 -> 0.687/s across the whole accessible range, and the duty signal is 2.56e-4 against a 1-seed Binomial SEM of 2.61e-2 — SNR 0.0098, needing 9.3e4 seeds for SNR 3 against a 1.5 d estimate.

(2) M5's centrepiece oracle rests on a false linearity claim. "The SF axial links are linear Hookean, so the whole single-pair inner problem is a linear SPD system... the angle-harmonics are the only nonlinear terms" is wrong. `ff/network_warp.py:39` is `k*(L-r0)*d/L` — geometrically NONLINEAR for r0 != 0 — and the NMII backbone rod and head arm (`harmonic_bond`, r0_head = 0.200 um) are too, and the design omits them from its nonlinear list entirely. Worse, the device operator is not even the true Hessian: `_central_action` (`ac/cell/implicit_mechanics.py:82-92`) PSD-CLAMPS the transverse term with `max(k*ext/L, 0)`. So a host "assemble and solve directly" gives one Newton step from the current configuration, not the equilibrium, and the 1e-8 um agreement criterion cannot be met. (The fix is cheap and right: host NEWTON to convergence on the true nonlinear residual — 156-300 DOF.)

(3) M2's nominal configuration has no equilibrium. With only the + group bound, all 10 crossbridge forces act at y = +0.200 um on a body whose centroid is at y = 0, so the minifilament carries a net torque of ~0.2*N*|f| with ZERO rotational restoring stiffness — the crossbridge force is purely along the frozen walk_dir (`segment_motor.py:497`), so a bound head has no transverse restoring force at all. It rotates indefinitely and the heads drift off the actin while nominally bound. M2's nominal therefore PRODUCES the ghost-anchor pathology it exists to detect, and its `--nc ghost-anchor` control is confounded with it. Relatedly, anchor B's reaction is identically 0 in M2 (nothing is bound to filament B), so half the decay criterion is vacuous.

Everything else is fixable, and the M0/M1/M3/M7 skeleton plus the gate-contract `negative_control` schema extension are worth keeping.
must_fix: M4: DELETE the absolute force-velocity shape gate as written and replace it with (a) a dt/tau INVARIANCE sweep proving the measured v(F=0) is v0 and not f_stall/(k_xb*dt) — currently 0.050 vs 0.120 um/s at the driver's dt=0.01 (segment_motor.py:172, :223; driver dt at scripts/ac_gate_b_sf_motor_native.py:66); and (b) a duty-vs-load SIGN gate (catch-slip => duty INCREASES with load; --nc detach-slip-only => duty DECREASES), which IS magnitude-free and IS measurable, instead of the non-monotonic-interior-peak gate whose F*=1.3665 pN is unreachable behind f_stall=0.5 pN.

M4: the run must not be authorised at any dt > f_stall/(k_xb*v0) = 4.17e-3 s, or the reported mechanism is the linear-stall proxy CLAUDE.md forbids. Add this as an explicit admissibility precondition on the driver, derived not tuned.

M5: replace the 'assemble the linear SPD system and solve directly' oracle with a host NEWTON solve to convergence on the true nonlinear residual. link_spring_kernel (ff/network_warp.py:39) and harmonic_bond (r0_head=0.200) are geometrically nonlinear, and the device operator PSD-clamps the transverse term (ac/cell/implicit_mechanics.py:82-92), so a one-shot linear solve cannot meet the 1e-8 um criterion. Report both the true-Hessian Newton equilibrium AND the clamped-operator fixed point; their difference is itself the diagnostic.

M2: the one-sided configuration is rotationally unforced-degenerate (net couple ~0.2*N*|f| about the minifilament centroid, zero rotational restoring stiffness because the crossbridge force is purely along the frozen walk_dir, segment_motor.py:497). Either add an explicit rigid-body rotational constraint declared as a MEASUREMENT FIXTURE, or reformulate M2 as a transient decay-RATE measurement rather than a converged-equilibrium test. As written 'after the inner solve converges' never happens.

ADD the missing observable the whole track needs and never measures: the NATIVE per-head head-to-bound-filament-line perpendicular residual, per accepted step. minifilament_topology.py:306 head_newton_residual is host PLACEMENT only. Because the crossbridge has no transverse stiffness, nothing currently prevents a 'bound' head from drifting arbitrarily far from its actin site — this is the strongest available test that the nmii<->sf_arc connector is real rather than nominal, and it is absent.

M3(b): the tolerance 'residual crossbridge tension <= 1e-9 * k_xb * mean abscissa' is wrong by ~7-9 orders. Heterogeneous per-head abscissae are elastically frustrated through the 100 pN/um arm (series with k_xb=1000 => 90.9 pN/um per head), so residual tension is bounded BELOW by ~O(f_stall)=0.5 pN, vs the ~3e-7 pN the criterion allows. Replace with the ACCOUNTING identity: shortening + delta(all stored strains) = sum(mean abscissa advance), closed to 1e-6. Same fix for M2's 'centroid translation == mean abscissa advance to 1e-6'.

M3(a): same correction — per-step shortening equals summed mean abscissa advance ONLY up to the change in stored crossbridge+arm strain (O(f_stall/k_eff) ~ 5.5 nm per head). The 1e-6 relative criterion is unachievable; the strain term must be an explicit measured member of the identity, not neglected.

M7: FIRST fix or explicitly declare that sf_mechanics.py:339 sets link_k to a per-link CONSTANT, not EA/seg. Over the proposed sweep the fiber's continuum axial stiffness changes 8x (1000/4 = 250 pN/um at n_per_fiber=5 vs 1000/32 = 31.25 at 33), so the gate compares physically DIFFERENT fibers and is guaranteed to fail for a reason that has nothing to do with the motor. The negative control --nc segment-length-scaled-k presumes the nominal already scales; it does not.

M6: the non-tautology test is identical to its own tautology negative control. The explicit inner solve is x += step*F (scripts/ac_gate_b_sf_motor_native.py:437-441 with _relax_free_nodes_kernel), so 'measured D = sum(F.dx)' IS exactly step*|F|^2 — bit-identical to --nc dissipation-modelled. And on the implicit path CG iterates are not physical states, so F.dx has no meaning there. Redefine dissipation from a declared physical mobility law along the ACCEPTED outer-step displacement only, and drop the claim that measuring F.dx avoids the tautology.

M6(1): the slide identity is checked against its own definition. new_code_needed defines slide := loads_hill/k_xb - abscissa and then M6(1) verifies slide == loads_hill/k_xb - abscissa to 1e-12. To be non-vacuous, slide must be computed INDEPENDENTLY from geometry (dot(x_att0 - x_head, w) minus its stored bind-time value), which DOES require a new device array — contradicting 'no new device array, only a readback'.

M6(3): 'W >= 0 on every accepted step' will fail on a correct run. loads_hill can be NEGATIVE (compressed crossbridge) while delta-abscissa >= 0, so W < 0 for any assisted head. Worse, hill_velocity has a POLE at F = -kappa*f_stall = -0.25 pN (hand.py:111-118 divides by 1 + f/kappa); the stall cap is the ONLY thing bounding it. Rewrite as a per-head sign decomposition and state that the cap is doing double duty as a numerical bound, not only as a stall guard.

Move M1(1), M1(3), M1(4), M1(6), M3(c), M0(b), M0(e) and M8's nominal OUT of the blocking mechanism set — every one is guaranteed by construction (see tautological_gates). Keep them as REPORTED instrumentation. The blocking set must be limited to claims whose stated negative control demonstrably flips them AND whose nominal outcome is not forced by geometry, momentum bookkeeping, or algebra.

The Dirichlet anchor reaction — the design's own primary transmitted-load observable — is DESTROYED before it can be read: _pin_force_kernel (scripts/ac_gate_b_sf_motor_native.py:135-139, launched at :440) zeroes force at pinned nodes, and the implicit path masks it in the operator (sf_implicit.py Dirichlet projector). Capture the unmasked assembled force at pinned nodes between accumulate() and the mask launch. This is not in new_code_needed and without it M1's primary criterion is unmeasurable.

Resolve the internal contradiction: the design mandates 'each --nc must be a config-level perturbation, never a source edit', yet drop-reaction-b, isotropic-crossbridge, wrong-tangent, merge-arrays, reset-abscissa-before-ledger and dissipation-modelled all require alternate kernels or builders. Either declare a sanctioned negative-control kernel family (versioned, contract-stamped, never a runtime path) or drop those six.

Fix the flagship risk arithmetic before it drives design. 'T_max 0.254 pN from 301 bound heads = five heads worth' misattributes: the landed run has 16 minifilaments (sf_motor_native_gate.json), so 301/16 = 18.8 bound per minifilament and 9.4 per side, and T_max/head_load_max = 4.66 is consistent with ~9 heads at roughly half the maximum load. There is no evidence of massive internal cancellation. Keep the cancellation ledger as instrumentation but drop the 0.05 flag threshold, which is an undeclared magic number with no derivation.
tautological_gates: M1(1) equality half — 'reaction at A and B equal and opposite to 1e-9' is implied by global momentum conservation plus the fact that the only external forces are the two Dirichlet reactions. It holds for ANY internal force law, correct or not, and its stated negative control (--nc flip-polarity) flips the SIGN, not the equality. This is the exact NG-1 critique the design itself levels ('|reaction_B|/|reaction_A| is a SYMMETRY measure, not a transmission measure') recommitted one paragraph later. At best it is a convergence proxy, duplicating M5 more weakly.

M1(1) inward half — barbed ends point OUTWARD by construction (sf_population.py:411-412; measured bipolar dot -1.0000) and abscissa is monotone non-decreasing (hill_velocity clamped >= 0 at hand.py:118, da_max >= 0 at segment_motor.py:172). There is no reachable state in the nominal build with an outward reaction.

M1(3) 'both head groups engaged, n_bound(+)>0 AND n_bound(-)>0' — at k_on=50/s and k_off≈0.700/s the emergent phi_b = 0.9862, so P(a 10-head group has zero bound) = (1-0.9862)^10 = 2.5e-19. Unfailable. And --nc parallel-pair does NOT flip it: heads still bind under same-polarity geometry, they just pull the same way. The design's claim that parallel-pair makes (1)+(3) fail is wrong for (3).

M1(4) 'cross-binding count == 0' — heads sit at +/-0.200 um and filaments at +/-0.200 um (verified: lateral separation 0.4000 um), capture is 0.210 um, and the measured max placement residual is 0.055 um, so the distance to the wrong filament is >= 0.345 um. Geometrically impossible. The design states the derived inequality itself and then presents the check as load-bearing evidence.

M1(6) 'net force on the isolated system == 0 to 1e-12' — the M1 system is NOT isolated (it has two pins), so this is either the internal-force sum (identically zero by the +f/-(1-t)f/-t f construction at segment_motor.py:497-500) or R_A+R_B, i.e. a restatement of M1(1). The design's own risk list says 'any net force metric is guaranteed zero and proves nothing' and then blocks on it.

M3(c) 'system centroid drift == 0 to 1e-12 per step' — momentum-conserving forces plus a single uniform relax step (x += step*F, _relax_free_nodes_kernel) make the centroid displacement exactly step*(sum F)/N = 0. Code-shape identity, not physics; --nc one-node-pinned flips it trivially.
M6(1) slide identity — slide is DEFINED as loads_hill/k_xb - abscissa and then the criterion verifies that definition to 1e-12. This is the A/A0 = V/V0 = 1.000 pattern exactly.

M0(b) torque identity and exponent — |tau| = |f|*d_perp is an algebraic consequence of the force triple (net torque = (x_head - x_att0) x f, which I verified is the correct expression), so both the 1e-10 identity check and the 'scaling exponent 1.000 +/- 0.01' are arithmetic, dressed as a scaling gate.

M0(e) 'sign(dot(f_head, walk_dir)) == +1' — f_head IS (scalar)*walk_dir by construction (segment_motor.py:496) and the scalar equals k_xb*abscissa at fixed geometry, with abscissa monotone non-decreasing. Cannot be negative.

M2 'the transmitted reaction at BOTH anchors decays toward 0' — with only the + group bound, filament B carries no force at all, so anchor B's reaction is identically 0 from step 1. Half the criterion is met by construction, and the spec is ambiguous about whether a non-decaying anchor A could still pass an aggregate metric.

M8 nominal — with n_ventral=2 the bundles sit at y = -1.875 and +1.875 (separation 3.75 um >> capture 0.210), axial links are emitted per-fiber only, and arc joints are zero. Zero cross-bundle binding and zero cross-bundle stiffness are guaranteed. A 0.5 d native gate for what is a host unit test. It also inverts the failure it invokes: the 494,802-node block-diagonal disaster was co-location WITHOUT a connector (missing coupling), not spurious coupling.

M1(2) 'transmitted reaction == 0 when n_bound == 0' — the builder places the fiber at rest length, so passive force is zero. This can only fail if the BUILDER injects prestress; it has no sensitivity to any motor bug. Reproduces the already-landed GATE-B claim tension_zero_while_no_head_is_bound.
hidden_magnitude_deps: M4(4) requires FOUR GAP catch-slip constants (k_catch0/x_catch/k_slip0/x_slip, all required-no-default per cortex_motor_slice.py:214-217 and ac_gate_b_sf_motor_native.py:266-270) plus f_stall just to be EVALUABLE — and worse, whether it can pass at all is the ratio F*/f_stall of five GAP constants. With the landed set F* = 1.3665 pN vs f_stall = 0.5 pN, so it cannot pass. This is billed as a shape gate; it is a five-parameter referendum, the exact defect the design correctly diagnoses in NG-1.

M4(2) 'v/v0 -> 1.000 +/- 0.01 as k_ext -> 0' is presented as an EXACT limit but is gated by dt <= f_stall/(k_xb*v0) — three GAP constants (f_stall, k_xb the declared MASTER knob, v0). At the driver's dt=0.01 it reads 0.417.

M4(3) 'curvature sign set by kappa' depends on kappa, which params_i0b3.yaml records as a THREE-way unresolved conflict (0.25 muscle / 0.5 Kovacs / inf linear), and is in any case masked by the linear stall cap over the sub-0.7*f_stall range.

M3(b) tolerance '1e-9 * k_xb * mean abscissa' is scaled by k_xb, the declared MASTER GAP force knob, and the physically achievable residual is set by f_stall and k_head_arm (both GAP). A tolerance whose satisfiability depends on three unsourced constants is not a magnitude-free gate.

M1(5) 'a value < 0.05 with >10 heads bound raises a LOAD-PATH-CANCELLATION flag' — 0.05 has no derivation anywhere in the design. It is an empirical magic number in a Magic-Number-Block project, and it was chosen off a ratio (0.254/0.0546) that I show is misattributed by ~20x.
M7 'the finest two rungs agree to <= 2%' — 2% is undeclared and underived. Contrast with the design's own praise of derived thresholds elsewhere.

M4's normalisation F_stall_ensemble is itself measured from the same GAP constants, so the 'collapse' plot's x-axis is not magnitude-free either; a collapse in self-normalised coordinates is much weaker evidence than the design implies.

The retained NG-1 diagnostic keeps phi_b >= 0.70 and 'reaction ~= analytic F_side' in its check set. The design says to keep and re-run NG-1 but does not say those two must be demoted out of any verdict; outputs/ac_magnitude/REPORT.md:44-49 is the record of exactly that trap (6/6 at L_p=1.0 um, 4/6 at 0.13 um).
sums_to_zero_risks: The design names the dipole-guarantee risk ('its net force is zero BY CONSTRUCTION, so any net force metric is guaranteed zero and proves nothing') and then puts three such metrics in its blocking set: M1(1) equal-and-opposite, M1(6) net force == 0, M3(c) centroid drift == 0. This is the crawl failure's structure — every edge present, net effect nil — reproduced inside the gate that is supposed to detect it.

M2, the one asymmetric probe the design correctly identifies as the real test of the load path, is structurally broken by an unnoticed non-zero SUM: the + group's 10 forces act at y = +0.200 um on a body centred at y = 0, giving a net couple ~0.2*N*|f| with zero rotational restoring stiffness (the crossbridge force is purely along frozen walk_dir, segment_motor.py:497). The minifilament rotates without bound, so the run never reaches the converged state the criterion is written against, and the heads drift off the actin while flagged bound — producing the fake load path M2 was built to catch.

M2's anchor-B reaction is identically zero because nothing binds filament B, so the 'both anchors decay' criterion is half-vacuous and cannot distinguish a genuine decay at A from an aggregate that is dominated by B's structural zero.

Cross-binding (design risk #2, 'self-cancelling internal load') is geometrically impossible in the nominal build — I verified lateral separation 0.4000 um, capture 0.210 um, max placement residual 0.055 um. The risk is real only under --nc capture-2x, i.e. only when deliberately broken, so it cannot be the reason M1(4) blocks.

'Both head groups on the SAME filament' (design risk #2 second clause) is likewise excluded by the same 0.210 < 0.400 margin. The design's stated mitigation ('excluded today only by the derived inequality, never verified at runtime') is accurate but the residual risk is essentially nil at the pair scale, so this risk is inflated to make M1(4) look load-bearing.
reuse_errors: FALSE PHYSICS CLAIM, kills M5: 'the SF axial links are linear Hookean ... (the angle-harmonics are the only nonlinear terms)'. ff/network_warp.py:39 is f = (k*(L-r0)/L)*d — geometrically nonlinear for r0 != 0. The NMII backbone rod and head arm (harmonic_bond, r0_head = 0.200 um) are nonlinear too and are omitted from the design's nonlinear list entirely. Only ff/forces_warp.py:46 (cytosim second-difference bending) is actually linear.

The device operator is not the true Hessian, which M5 also assumes: _central_action (ac/cell/implicit_mechanics.py:82-92) PSD-CLAMPS the transverse term with max(k*ext/L, 0), dropping it entirely for compressed links. So even the linearised host assembly would have to choose between matching the device (clamped, not the Hessian) and matching the force (unclamped). The design does not notice the choice exists.

'rank-one K = k_xb*w w^T' is imprecise: add_segment_crossbridge_stiffness_kernel (ac/cell/implicit_mechanics.py:311-343) is rank-one over the THREE-node stencil with weights [1, -(1-t), -t] outer-producted with w. The 3x3 head-head block alone is k_xb*w w^T. M0(d)'s FD comparison must use the 9x9 stencil operator or it will mis-diagnose.

'F4 Bell full-|F|' is presented as a distinct load channel, but segment_motor.py:311/:390/:533 all set loads_full[h] = wp.abs(loads[h]). Since the force is purely along w, |F| IS |tangential| — the two channels are algebraically identical, so no gate can distinguish them and no bug in the split can be caught.

sf_mechanics.py:339 sets link_k to a per-link CONSTANT k_axial, not EA/seg. M7's negative control --nc segment-length-scaled-k presumes the nominal already scales with segment length; it does not. Consequence: the sweep compares fibers whose continuum axial stiffness differs by 8x (250 -> 31.25 pN/um series from n_per_fiber 5 -> 33).

PI open-question #2 (capture 0.05 vs 0.210) is STALE: ac/cell/assemble.py:177-186 already records 'RECONCILED 2026-07-24', names 0.210 as the same physical quantity as ff/hand_kmc NMIIA_MYOSIN.capture_radius_um, and marks 0.05 'EXPLICITLY-RETIRED'. Only docs/v2_audit/cell_engine/ROLLING_ROADMAP.md:75 is stale. The design escalated a resolved item and hung a conclusion on it ('the answer decides whether some heads are out of reach by construction').

The Dirichlet reaction — M1's declared primary observable — is currently destroyed before it can be read: _pin_force_kernel (scripts/ac_gate_b_sf_motor_native.py:135-139, launched :440) zeroes force at pinned nodes, and sf_implicit.py's Dirichlet projector masks it in the operator. new_code_needed does not list capturing the pre-mask force.

Self-contradiction on negative controls: the design mandates 'each must be a config-level perturbation, never a source edit', yet drop-reaction-b, isotropic-crossbridge, wrong-tangent, merge-arrays, reset-abscissa-before-ledger and dissipation-modelled all require alternate kernels or builders.

--nc isotropic-crossbridge inverts the hard rule's polarity. A 3-D bond at r0_xb=0 gives f = k*d, a genuine Hookean bond that IS couple-balanced and holds the head on its site in all three directions; the 1-D projection onto w is the abstraction that both breaks couple balance and leaves a bound head with zero transverse restoring force. The design makes the fine-grained option its NEGATIVE CONTROL and asks PI which to keep.

M3(d) 'the A:B slide ratio equals the inverse ratio of their node counts (overdamped uniform per-node mobility) — a scaling gate, no constant needed' certifies a lumped uniform-per-node drag proxy, which is precisely what the {sf,mt,if}_cytosol_transfer connectors and ff/biot_fluid_warp.py exist to replace. It is also solver-path dependent (it is a property of x += step*F, and a Jacobi-preconditioned PCG has non-uniform effective mobility), so it directly contradicts M5's requirement that the answer be INVARIANT to solver path.

Every 'bit-identical' / 'byte-identical' claim (attach_enabled mask default all-ones, abscissa accumulator additive-default-on, cg_check_every) needs the Warp kernel-cache-clear discipline stated. Editing a @wp.kernel and getting a byte-identical native result is a known false positive in this project; without `rm -rf ~/.cache/warp/<ver>` the bit-identity check proves nothing.
arithmetic_corrections: catch_slip_peak_force(0.35, 1.0e-3, 0.35, 0.6e-3, 4.28e-3) = 1.3665 pN, i.e. 2.733x f_stall = 0.5 pN. Closed form kT/(x_c+x_s)*ln(k_c0*x_c/(k_s0*x_s)) confirms. Over the accessible load range [0, f_stall] the off-rate only falls 0.70000 -> 0.68682 /s (1.9%), monotone decreasing throughout — no interior peak exists. M4(4) cannot pass.

M4(4) duty signal-to-noise: phi_b goes 0.986193 -> 0.986450 across the entire accessible range, a signal of 2.564e-4 = 0.0051 heads out of 20, against a 1-seed Binomial SEM of 2.609e-2 = 0.522 heads. SNR = 0.0098 at 1 seed, 0.0278 at the proposed 8 seeds. 9.3e4 seeds are needed for SNR 3. Estimated effort 1.5 d is off by orders of magnitude.

The stall cap dominates Hill: tau*v0 = 0.01*0.12 = 1.20 nm but da_max(F=0) = f_stall/k_xb = 0.50 nm, so min() picks the CAP. The cap governs for F/f_stall < 0.70 (70% of the range) and gives an effective unloaded velocity f_stall/(k_xb*tau) = 0.0500 um/s vs v0 = 0.1200 — a ratio of 0.417. The cap's v(F) is LINEAR in (f_stall - F).
The Hill law only governs at F=0 for dt <= f_stall/(k_xb*v0) = 4.167e-3 s. The driver's documented dt = 0.01 s is 2.40x too large. The design never sweeps dt/tau; M7 sweeps space only.

M0(a): the momentum residual is 1.96e-16 RELATIVE over 2e4 random draws, not exactly zero — (1-t) rounds, so (1-t)f + tf differs from f by ~1 ulp. The design's prose 'exact momentum conservation, no tolerance band needed' is wrong (its numeric criterion happens to survive).

M0(d) is unimplementable as written. For an affine force the central-difference error is pure roundoff O(eps/h) and RISES as h falls: I measured 7.46e-15 at h=1e-2 rising monotonically to 8.39e-8 at h=1e-9. There is no O(h^2) branch to demonstrate, and 'a nonzero O(h^0) floor is a bug' misreads the expected roundoff floor. 'the FD step chosen by the standard h*sqrt(eps) rule' is also not a step rule (central-difference optimum is ~eps^(1/3)).

hill_velocity has a POLE at F = -kappa*f_stall = -0.250 pN (hand.py:111-118 divides by 1 + f/kappa; I reproduced a ZeroDivisionError in the host twin at exactly -0.25). v reaches 449.9 um/s at F = -0.2499 pN. The DERIVED stall cap is the ONLY thing bounding this; the design describes the cap purely as a stall-crossing guard and misses its second, load-bearing role.
M6(3) 'W >= 0 on every accepted step' will fail: W = sum(F_h * delta-abscissa_h) with F_h = loads_hill[h] < 0 for any compressed crossbridge and delta-abscissa >= 0 always.

The flagship risk ratio is misattributed by ~20x. T_max/head_load_max = 0.25411/0.05455 = 4.66, but the landed run has 16 minifilaments, so 301/16 = 18.8 bound per minifilament and 9.4 per side. 4.66 is entirely consistent with ~9 heads at roughly half the max load. 'roughly five heads worth of transmitted load from 301 bound heads' compares a single-segment tension against a population summed over 16 independent sarcomeres.

M3(b) tolerance is off by ~7-9 orders. Arm(100) + xb(1000) in series = 90.9 pN/um per head, so heterogeneous abscissae leave a frustration tension bounded below by ~O(f_stall) = 0.5 pN, versus the 1e-9*k_xb*A ~ 3e-7 pN allowed at A = 0.3 um.

Ceiling arithmetic the design never states: the maximum transmitted reaction the pair gate can ever produce is N_side*f_stall = 10*0.5 = 5.0 pN, with a per-head stall stretch of only f_stall/k_xb = 0.50 nm. Any observable requiring more load than 5 pN is out of reach by construction.

The geometry arithmetic DOES check out (I built it): n_ventral=1/n_dorsal=0/n_arc=0/n_cap=0 gives 1 bundle, 2 fibers, 0 arc joints, 2 FA sites, 6 cortex sites, filament contour 6.9005 um, lateral separation 0.4000 um, and segment length 1.7251 um (n_per_fiber=5) down to 0.2156 um (33). M5's 'a few hundred DOF' is right: 156 DOF at n_per_fiber=9, 300 at 33.
Total effort 0.5+1.5+0.5+1+1.5+1+1.5+0.5+0.5+1+1 = 10.5 d as claimed, but M4 (1.5 d) is unachievable and M5 (1 d) must absorb a host Newton solver instead of a linear solve.
ducked_questions: TORQUE — offered PI a three-option menu (accept and bound it / add a compensating couple / drive d_perp to zero) instead of stating the physics. The couple is not a placement artifact: it is intrinsic to PROJECTING the crossbridge force onto walk_dir while applying it at an off-axis point (segment_motor.py:496-500). Under the hard rule, the couple-balanced 3-D bond IS the fine-grained option and the 1-D projection is the abstraction — the design has it backwards, using the 3-D bond as its negative control. It should have said so and let PI reject a stated position.

DIRICHLET PIN vs FULL ADHESION CIRCUIT — the PI has already stated the baseline (adherent on 2D collagen-coated ECM) and this is the magnets-versus-full-adhesion-circuits question. ff/fa_clutch_warp.py, ff/fa_anchor.py, ff/fa_maturation.py, ff/substrate.py and ff/ecm_library.py all exist and are unwired; replacing the pin with the integrin catch-slip clutch on a collagen substrate is a WIRING task over existing modules, exactly the reuse opportunity the brief flags. The design defers the whole thing to open_question #5 and proposes no step for it.

CAPTURE RADIUS — asked as PI question #2 when ac/cell/assemble.py:177-186 already records the 2026-07-24 reconciliation to 0.210 with 0.05 explicitly retired. The design read the stale ROLLING_ROADMAP.md:75 line and not the code it cites elsewhere.

SF AXIAL MECHANICS — asks PI to choose between inextensibility-with-Lagrange-multiplier and the k_axial penalty spring, without reporting the code fact that decides half of it: sf_mechanics.py:339 makes link_k a per-link constant, so the penalty spring is not even discretization-consistent and the M7 sweep would compare different fibers. That is determinable, not a PI decision.

PI PRIORITY #5 (parameters as eventual OUTPUTS) — no step addresses identifiability or sensitivity. A single-pair system with ~150-300 DOF is the cheapest place in the project to map which observables are sensitive to which GAP constants, which is the prerequisite for ever inferring molecular parameters from macroscopic data. Absent entirely.

PI PRIORITY #4 (speed is THE goal after assembly) — blanket-forbids both in-tree wins during M1-M8, but sf_implicit.py's own docstring states cg_check_every returns dx bit-identical either way, so forbidding it costs 5.3x for zero risk. No cost model or launch-overhead analysis is given, and at ~100 nodes this suite is entirely GPU-launch-overhead bound, which is the one performance fact that matters here.

NO TRANSVERSE-CONTACT QUESTION AT ALL — the design never asks whether a bound head stays on its actin, and never proposes an observable for it, even though the directional crossbridge gives a bound head ZERO transverse restoring force. For a track whose stated purpose is to prove the nmii<->sf_arc connector is real rather than nominal, this is the most important unasked question.

GOVERNANCE — the ladder-rung question is the right one to escalate, but the design also declines to propose a default ('I will not decide this myself'). A reviewer-usable design states a recommended answer and its rationale so PI is ratifying or overruling, not authoring.

result.summary: The physics essay is the track's real deliverable and it is largely sound: the Brinkman-screening framing (ell_B = sqrt(k) = 2.2-6.5 nm, viscous/Darcy ratio (ell_B/L)^2), the LBM rejection, and the absence audit all check out — I independently reproduced every row of the DOF/memory table and confirmed by grep that `stokes|brinkman|vorticity|curl` appear nowhere in ff/, ac/, common/ except the lumped 6*pi*eta*R drags. The VALIDATION LAYER, however, is not usable as written. Three of the eight steps carry gates that provably cannot do their job, and I measured two of them: with an EXACTLY LINEAR pressure field (analytic curl identically zero) the incumbent masked stencil (ffn_sim/ac/fluid/velocity.py:50-71) produces normalised |curl q| = 0.879 over all 9,978 live fluid cells and 0.482 with a 1-cell buffer, reaching 0.000 only at erosion depth >= 2 which retains 33.0% of the domain. So S1's "<1e-12" criterion FAILS a correct incumbent build on 67% of the domain, is a pure algebraic identity on the 33% where it passes, and S8's decisive pass criterion ("vorticity renders numerically ZERO under the incumbent Darcy backend") is factually false — the panel cannot discriminate the two physics. Separately, the #1 recommended operator is specified with div v = 0, which is mathematically incompatible with the incumbent's storage balance S dp/dt + alpha div v_s + div q = s_water (ffn_sim/ac/fluid/biot_substrate.py:6-8), so the claimed "degenerates exactly to today's Darcy at k->0" regression oracle and S4(3) are impossible as written. The headline remediation number is misattributed by ~1000x: I computed gamma(eta=65.9)/gamma_Brinkman = 62.9, not 65,900 (65,900 is gamma(65.9)/gamma(solvent), i.e. units.py:140 vs units.py:67) — and that wrong number is used to mandate deleting cross-track code. Worse, the Brinkman drag is identically zero for any affine volume-preserving skeleton motion, so the proposed replacement removes essentially all shear dissipation while every S5 gate passes. Finally the "NATIVE RESULT ON RECORD" that anchors S4's boundary data is a StaticSphereMembraneProvider with nucleus=None and a prescribed analytic hemispherical div_vs at phi=0.5 placeholder — no solid, no cortex, no nucleus. Keep S0 (genuinely the highest-value item), keep the REV concept, re-sequence so the decision precedes the 5-7 week build it authorizes, and rewrite the gate layer.
must_fix: CONTINUITY EQUATION IS WRONG. new_code_needed item 1, the S2 protocol, and the reuse entry all specify 'div v = 0'. The incumbent solves S dp/dt + alpha div(v_s) + div(q) = s_water (ffn_sim/ac/fluid/biot_substrate.py:6-8, kernel :38-80) — a NON-divergence-free storage problem. A div-free Stokes-Brinkman operator cannot reduce to it at k->0. Therefore the claimed 'k->0 limit is a bit-comparable regression oracle' (reuse item on biot_pmass_update_kernel) and S4 pass criterion (3) are unachievable as specified. Either write the poro-Brinkman system with the storage + alpha*div(v_s) continuity, or delete the reduction claim and stop calling biot_pmass_update_kernel an oracle for it.

S4, THE DECISION GATE, IS MIS-DERIVED AND MUST BE REPLACED. Its slope-1.00+/-0.05 criterion is a BULK scaling (delta/v ~ k/L_eff^2) but a global relative-L2 norm on a bounded domain is dominated by the wall layer, where Brinkman no-slip and Darcy mask-flux differ by O(1) in the tangential component over a shell of thickness max(ell_B, dx): rel-L2 ~ sqrt(3*dx/R) = 0.45 at dx=0.5 um, R=7.5 um, INDEPENDENT of k, so the measured exponent is ~0 and a correct implementation FAILS. Restricting the norm to bulk cells recovers slope 1 but then measures exactly the stencil ratio k/dx^2 — a tautology. Criterion (2) is additionally ambiguous by 225x (it quotes both 2.0e-5 at L=0.5 um and 8.9e-8 at L=7.5 um as the prediction).

ADD AN ell_B-RESOLUTION PRECONDITION AND APPLY THE DESIGN'S OWN HONESTY TEST TO ITS OWN #1 RECOMMENDATION. ell_B = 2.24-6.5 nm is unresolved at every affordable dx. At dx=100 nm, (dx/ell_B)^2 ~ 2000, so the discrete reaction term dominates every cell, no-slip is realised as a one-cell velocity drop (effective slip length ~dx, i.e. ~40x ell_B), and wall vorticity ~ v_D/dx is set by the grid. The claimed gains of whole-cell Brinkman at 100-250 nm — 'adds real shear, vorticity, no-slip on large surfaces' — are grid artifacts at those resolutions. The design applies exactly this a_eff/dx honesty test to IBM blobs in S6(c) but exempts its own recommended grid; no step in S1-S8 reports ell_B/dx.

S2 NEVER VALIDATES THE OPERATOR AT THE k IT WILL RUN AT. Every S2 gate is on the k->inf (pure Stokes) branch: Poiseuille 1.5 shape ratio, 6*pi*mu*a*v sphere drag, reciprocity, MMS. There is no oracle for finite physiological k anywhere. Add the exact analytic Brinkman channel (cosh profile), whose u_max/u_mean is a dimensionless function of h/ell_B — a proper magnitude-free shape/scaling gate that would also expose the resolution problem above.

DO NOT DELETE ff/motility_warp.py:407 physical_node_gammas IN THE SAME COMMIT, AND ADD A VOLUME-PRESERVING-SHEAR DISSIPATION GATE FIRST. For an affine skeleton velocity with div v_s = 0, lap(v_s) = 0 and v = v_s with grad p = 0 solves the Brinkman equation exactly, so (mu/k)(v_f - v_s) = 0 at every node: the drag pair is wired at all 494,802 nodes and contributes exactly zero dissipation to rigid translation, rigid rotation, and uniform shear. All five S5 gates pass with that hole open. Measured additionally: for the compressive mode the Brinkman channel reconstructs only ~1/63 of the 65.9 Pa*s per-node channel. Replacing one with the other is a physics regression that the S0 census would then actively enforce.

VERIFY, DO NOT INHERIT, surface_porous_transfer ADJOINTNESS. The design lists it under '(i) IMPLEMENTED + WIRED / force-real'. In the ENGINE it is ONE-SIDED: ffn_sim/ac/cell/fsi_coupling.py:8-10 states FieldGrid allocates div_vs as ZEROS and the driver never fills it; SolidDilatationCoupling is constructed only in ffn_sim/ac/cell/driver.py:504 and ac/cell/native_gates/, never in ac/engine — a grep of ac/engine/*.py finds grid.div_vs only at interior_column_slice.py:196,207,221,270, all snapshot/rollback. The reaction path the docstring asserts (interior_column_slice.py:288-292, 'the fluid feels the work-conjugate reaction through the Biot div(v_s) source term the moving cortex imprints') is not connected in the engine. Reclassify as one-sided and add a gate on div_vs being filled.

RE-SEQUENCE. S4 is described as the gate that decides 'BEFORE committing to a full-cell Stokes rewrite', but S2 (3-4 weeks, the largest item) + S3 (2-3 weeks) ARE that commitment and are scheduled first, and the design calls S0-S4 'unconditional'. The Darcy-vs-Brinkman question at the affordable dx can be answered by a 1-D analytic Brinkman boundary-layer calculation plus the REV — no whole-cell saddle-point MG solver, no GPU. Order: S0 -> S3 (the only step serving PI priority 5) -> analytic/CPU stand-in for S4 -> PI decision -> S2 only if authorised.

RE-LABEL THE NG-4 EVIDENCE AND STOP BUILDING S4 ON IT. ffn_sim/ac/cell/ng4_payload.py:79-82 uses StaticSphereMembraneProvider with nucleus=None; :89-100 _hemisphere_div_vs PRESCRIBES an analytic div_vs = -eps_rate in the z>0 hemisphere; :130 comments 'RAMP phase: div_vs prescribed'. There is no solid, no cortex, no nucleus, and ng4_payload.json records "phi_provisional_GAP": 0.5. It is a manufactured-source operator test that executed on CUDA, not a native coupled result. S4's 'SAME boundary data as the recorded NG-4 run' imports a stripped configuration into the PI decision gate — the seventh occurrence of the pattern the design itself warns about.

WITHDRAW OR RENAME THE phi = 0.925 CLOSURE, AND STATE THE c_v CONSEQUENCE OF MEASURING k. The proposed phi is 1 minus the explicit F-actin volume fraction from CORTEX-only density; ffn_sim/ac/fluid/params_i0b1b.yaml:32-35 states the mechanically relevant phi excludes bound water and macromolecular crowding and is 'plausibly lower' than the 0.7 water-fraction UPPER proxy — so the 'measured' value sits above the file's own upper bound. Separately, ffn_sim/ac/fluid/params_i0b1.yaml c_v policy is PI-ratified: 'k, mu, M must stay CONSISTENT with this c_v (c_v = k*M/mu); they are never prescribed independently'. A REV k of 0.93-4.2e-17 m^2 (the design's own range) is 1.9-8.3x the running 5e-18 and forces either c_v off its Moeendarbary anchor (50 -> 95-400 um^2/s) or M/S down by the same factor, which changes Skempton B and invalidates the very NG-4 numbers (2.0201, 1.99841) S7 uses as its preservation criterion. Never mentioned.

FIX THE ANALYTIC ORACLES. Hasimoto's periodic correction is 1/(1 - 1.7601*c^(1/3) + 1.5593c - 2.8746c^2) with c = (4/3)pi(a/L)^3, so c^(1/3) = 1.6119(a/L); the design's '1 - 1.7601(a/L)' drops that factor and is +18.6% wrong at a/L = 1/8, +8.0% at 1/16 — larger than any second-order convergence signal, so S2(c) either fails a correct solver or certifies a 20%-wrong one depending on box size. The Brenner gate does not specify sphere-wall orientation (F ~ a/h perpendicular vs ln(a/h) parallel), so 'the correct leading exponent in a/h' is undefined. And S6's h/a = 100 negative control needs ~1 mm of domain (>= 1e12 cells at dx = 100 nm) — infeasible on the S2 grid; it silently requires the BEM closure the design ranks as a niche tool.

ADD REV-SIZE CONVERGENCE AND FIX THE CORTEX REV GEOMETRY. Permeability from a periodic REV is systematically L-dependent; S3's gate (1) uses seed-to-seed spread at FIXED L, which cannot detect a finite-size bias. Also the 0.4 um-thick cortex patch is 2x the 0.2 um shell used to derive rho_L = 1500 um/um^3, halving the enclosed density; and all-periodic BCs cannot represent a 0.2 um layer bounded by membrane on one side and cytosol on the other — the NORMAL-direction cortex permeability, the one surface_porous_transfer actually needs, is a boundary-layer problem, not a periodic-REV problem.

ADD THE OBSERVABLE THAT CATCHES THE HISTORICAL FAILURE. Nothing in S1-S8 measures PER-COMPARTMENT DISPLACEMENT UNDER A FLUID LOAD — the only test that caught the 39.8 nm cortex / 0.0 nm nucleus+MT block-diagonal defect. The design names that failure in its risk list and then omits it from every pass criterion. Also add a separate ledger channel for the drag force vs the -alpha*V*grad(p) pressure force; today both would land in the same array (biot_substrate.py:274) and the pressure term would be credited with drag it does not supply.

EXTEND S0's ENUMERATION AND NAME ITS UNLISTED PREREQUISITE. The census list omits ffn_sim/ac/cell/driver.py FIRE (fire_velocity_d at :381, fire_mix_and_step_kernel at :69, dt_mu MUTATED on device at :618) and the RKC1 Chebyshev recurrence (:577) — both carry velocity state and both are velocity-proportional numerical dissipation. Classifying them NUMERICAL-MOBILITY by fiat means the census cannot fail on the most likely contamination path once a physical drag exists. Also: driver.py:7-10 is a quasi-static descent with no physical velocity at all, so S5's (mu/k)(v_f - v_s) has no v_s to consume; a physical time step and a physical solid velocity are unlisted hard prerequisites of S5.
tautological_gates: S1 pass criterion 'normalised |curl q| at round-off (<1e-12 relative)' is BOTH non-failable and failing-for-a-correct-build, depending on where it is evaluated. I replicated ffn_sim/ac/fluid/velocity.py:50-71 exactly (masked central difference with one-sided-to-centre fallback) on a 43^3, dx=0.5 um sphere R=7.5 + nucleus R=5.0 mask (9,978 live FLUID cells, matching the design's ~9,800) with an EXACTLY LINEAR p = 3x+2y-z whose analytic curl is identically zero. Erosion-depth study of normalised |curl q|*dx/max|q|: depth 0 (100% of FLUID) = 8.79e-1; depth 1 (66.1%) = 4.82e-1; depth 2 (33.0%) = 0.000e+00; depth 3 (5.3%) = 0.000e+00. So on 67% of the live domain a correct incumbent build fails the gate for a pure stencil reason, and on the 33% where it passes the gate is the algebraic identity curl(uniform-coefficient central-difference gradient) = 0, which no p field can violate. Script: /private/tmp/claude-502/-Users-sw1-ffn-cellsim/db982de2-47e9-4da5-a475-fb7e4bc840d9/scratchpad/curl_check.py

S1's negative control (solid-body rotation v = omega x r) does NOT rescue this. It proves the curl diagnostic has sensitivity; it says nothing about the stencil's spurious vorticity. The design's own risk text names 'the irrotationality gate passes trivially if the curl diagnostic itself is broken' and then supplies the control for exactly that, while missing the real defect.

S1's second half is unrunnable as scheduled: 'Repeat with an ARTIFICIALLY non-uniform k(x) field' requires the k_ij(x) device field that the design lists under new_code_needed and schedules later. ffn_sim/ac/fluid/velocity.py:33 takes mobility as a scalar wp.float64. And the physical vorticity source |grad k x grad p|/mu at dx=0.5 um is a one-cell k jump, i.e. the same grid-scale magnitude as the 0.1-0.9 spurious floor I measured — so the 'slope 1.00 +/- 0.05' cannot be extracted.

S8's decisive panel is FACTUALLY INVERTED. 'The vorticity scene shows a numerically ZERO field under the incumbent uniform-k Darcy backend and a structured NON-ZERO field under the Brinkman backend near solid boundaries — i.e. the render VISUALLY distinguishes the two physics'. The Darcy backend will show structured non-zero vorticity of normalised magnitude 0.1-0.9 concentrated exactly where the Brinkman signal is expected (67% of the domain, boundary-localised). The panel discriminates nothing.

S2 pass criterion (a) 'max|div v| <= solver tolerance and AT ROUND-OFF FOR THE PROJECTED FIELD' is the exact antipattern the design itself lists three sections later: 'an incompressibility gate evaluated on the projected field rather than the pre-projection field always passes'. The pass criterion and the risk contradict each other in the same document.

S5(b) 'sum of all internal fluid+solid forces = 0 to round-off' and S5(d) 'COM drift at round-off' are identities of the Peskin transpose, already gated to round-off by ffn_sim/ac/fluid/ibm_reference.py. Worse, ffn_sim/ff/motility_warp.py:400-404 contains a kernel whose docstring is 'the net pushed vector is subtracted uniformly over the cortex nodes, so the spreading push exerts ZERO net force on the cell' — a COM-drift gate can pass because a code path removes net force by construction, not because the coupling is adjoint.

S5(a) 'release a single unanchored filament in a uniform IMPOSED v_f' cannot fail given a correct sign: f = -c(v_s - v_f) with c > 0 in an overdamped step is monotone exponential relaxation by construction, and 'relaxation exponent independent of dt' is a property of the integrator, not of the physics. It is also one free filament in an imposed field — the least-connected configuration available, the reaction on the fluid discarded — which contradicts both PI priority 1 (connectedness) and the validate-at-full-native hard rule, in the step that is supposed to prove the compartments deform each other.

S3 gate (1) grid invariance is judged 'below the seed-to-seed stochastic spread across >=5 network realisations'. Seed spread at fixed REV size cannot detect the systematic finite-size bias of a periodic-REV permeability, so a systematically biased k passes.

S7 pass criterion (1) requires tau(c_v/2)/tau(c_v) = 2.00 +/- 0.05. That ratio is a property of the diffusion operator's scaling in c_v, not of the coupled physics: halving c_v halves the rate constant in a linear parabolic problem, so any consistent discretisation returns 2.00. The incumbent already measured 1.9984. It cannot detect a broken fluid-solid coupling.
hidden_magnitude_deps: S4 pass criterion (2) requires the a-priori number (ell_B/L)^2 with ell_B = sqrt(k). k = 5.0e-18 m^2 is 'draft/Medium', provisional, with source recorded as 'Happel-Brenner permeability closure (closure NOT in corpus)' (ffn_sim/ac/fluid/params_i0b1.yaml k_perm). The design's own independent re-derivation gives 0.93-4.2e-17, i.e. 1.9-8.3x larger, moving the prediction from 2.0e-5 to as much as 1.7e-4 at L = 0.5 um; plus the 225x L ambiguity. A gate whose a-priori target is uncertain by 2-3 orders of magnitude is not evaluable under a directive that magnitudes are not the gate.

S5's drag coefficient needs BOTH k (draft) and phi (NULL). ffn_sim/ac/fluid/params_i0b1b.yaml:20 records native_run_blocked_on: ["phi_porosity"] and :29 value: null. And the form is wrong: the Darcy drag per unit BULK volume is (mu/k)*q = (mu/k)*phi*(v_f - v_s), so the design's (mu/k)(v_f - v_s) is 1/phi too large — 2x at the phi = 0.5 placeholder. So the step claims 'no coefficient magnitude needed' while its wiring is both blocked on a null GAP and mis-normalised by it.

The design's headline 'more favourable than expected' finding — 'max|v_f - v_s| = 0.474 um/s ... Pe = 0.47*7.5/3 = 1.2, so advection is marginally relevant, contra the steady-state Pe<<1 claim in docs/cfd_transport_program' — is built entirely on placeholders. ng4_payload.json: max_vf_minus_vs_um_s = 0.4741728590391876 is EXACTLY 2 x max_q_um_s = 0.2370864295195938, i.e. q/phi at the placeholder "phi_provisional_GAP": 0.5. And max_q itself is just mobility x max|grad p| = 5.0e-3 x 47.417 = 0.23708 to all digits, i.e. the provisional k restated. The D = 3 um^2/s in the Peclet number is D_c, which ffn_sim/ac/fluid/NATIVE_GATE_SPEC.md:85 records as 'draft/Medium ... ratification + MCF7 applicability OPEN'. Three unclosed numbers producing a claim that contradicts a project document.

The proposed phi = 0.925 closure is a magnitude smuggle in the shape of a measurement. 1500 um/um^3 x pi(4 nm)^2 = 0.0754 is verified arithmetic, but it is 1 minus the EXPLICIT F-ACTIN volume fraction of the CORTEX, not the Darcy pore fraction of the cytoplasm: it counts no ribosomes, organelles, or soluble protein. ffn_sim/ac/fluid/params_i0b1b.yaml:32-35 states this outright ('the mechanically-relevant phi excludes bound water + the macromolecular-crowded excluded volume, so it is plausibly lower and MUST be sourced, not guessed') with the 0.7 water fraction as an UPPER proxy. The proposal therefore closes a PI GAP with a value above the file's own upper bound, and v_f - v_s = q/phi would shift by up to 1.85x.

The whole-cell (ell_B/L)^2 prediction is extrapolated from CORTEX density. rho_L = 1500 um/um^3 is derived over the 0.2 um cortical shell (70,686 x 3 um / (706.9 x 0.2 um^3) = 1500 — verified). Interior cytoplasm has far lower F-actin length density, so xi_interior >> 25.8 nm and k_interior is correspondingly larger. Using cortex numbers to set the a-priori target of the decision gate is the coarse-configuration-conclusion pattern applied to the gate designed to prevent it.

sigma_refl = 1.0 in MembraneFluxBC is an unsourced assumption — ffn_sim/ac/fluid/params_i0b1.yaml L_p note: 'reflection coeff sigma=1.0 assumed' — and it multiplies dPi in the Kedem-Katchalsky flux the design cites as 'FULLY DELIVERED'. It appears in no BLOCKED banner; the S8 list is (k, phi, c_0, D_c, L_p, Pi_0).
S6(d)'s '< 4 cells across the film => BLOCKED' uses an unsourced threshold of 4 as a criterion. As a reporting convention it is fine; stated as a pass/fail boundary it is a magic number.
sums_to_zero_risks: THE PRIMARY ONE, UNNOTICED BY THE DESIGN: the Brinkman drag pair is identically zero for every affine volume-preserving skeleton motion. If v_s is affine with div v_s = 0, then lap(v_s) = 0, and v = v_s with grad p = 0 satisfies mu*lap(v) - (mu/k)(v - v_s) = grad p exactly, so (mu/k)(v_f - v_s) = 0 at every node. The pair is wired at all 494,802 nodes and contributes exactly zero dissipation to rigid translation, rigid rotation and uniform shear — the dominant cytoskeletal modes, and precisely the modes by which compartments deform each other (PI priority 1). Every S5 gate passes with this hole open: (a) uses an imposed uniform v_f (compressive-free but relative), (b)/(d) are transpose identities, (c) is a sign test, (e) is bit-identity. This is structurally the crawl failure — every edge present, net effect nil. Required gate: apply a volume-preserving shear to the skeleton and require non-zero pairwise dissipation. Absent.

Consequence the design gets backwards: because the drag vanishes for shear, the claim 'the 65.9 Pa*s IS the poroelastic composite that (mu/k)(v_f - v_s) reconstructs' is false for the dominant mode, and S5's mandated same-commit DELETE of ff/motility_warp.py:407 physical_node_gammas would remove essentially all shear dissipation from the cell. The S0 census, asserting exactly one PHYSICAL-DISSIPATION owner per (component, velocity) pair, would then actively PREVENT restoring it. A single-ownership gate over channels with different functional support enforces the deficit.

surface_porous_transfer is one-sided in the engine, so its 'load path' currently terminates. Fluid -> solid exists (Peskin scatter of -alpha*V_node*grad(p), ffn_sim/ac/fluid/biot_substrate.py:228-274). Solid -> fluid does not: ffn_sim/ac/cell/fsi_coupling.py:8-10 records that FieldGrid allocates div_vs as ZEROS and the driver never fills it, and SolidDilatationCoupling is constructed only at ffn_sim/ac/cell/driver.py:504 and in ac/cell/native_gates/ — a grep of ac/engine/*.py finds grid.div_vs only in interior_column_slice.py snapshot/rollback (:196, :207, :221, :270). The design classifies the connector as force-real and bidirectional on the strength of a docstring.

The pressure body force itself sums to zero on a closed symmetric cell. node_vol[:n_actin] = cell_vol / n_actin (ffn_sim/ac/cell/assemble.py:931-932) is a UNIFORM weight over a shell, so -alpha*V*grad(p) is a gradient field with uniform quadrature: its resultant over the closed shell is zero by construction, and for a symmetric cell so is the per-compartment resultant. Per-node |F| will look large (the design quotes ~40 pN/node on the membrane) while nothing moves. The design flags this in risk (a) and then supplies no per-compartment displacement-under-load observable in any pass criterion.

The local k_ij(x) field is neutralised on the solid side before it can matter. node_volume is uniform (cell_vol/n_actin) regardless of local filament density, so if the drag reuses it — which the design implies by routing through the existing PressureCoupling/Peskin machinery — the per-node drag weight is density-independent and the measured spatially-varying k_ij affects the solid only through v_f. The de-lumping deliverable is cancelled at the transfer step unless a second, density-derived pore-volume array is introduced. The design's only stated concern about the volume is non-duplication with the pressure work.

The interior fluid cannot resist whole-cell motion at all: a rigidly translating cell has div v_s = 0, hence no pressure source, hence q = 0 and v_f = v_s, hence zero drag. So the interior Brinkman channel contributes exactly nothing to motility, which is what ff/implicit_ff.py:170's modal 6*pi*eta*R was supplying. Deleting that (S5's item 5) without the exterior bath (S6, gated behind the S4 decision) leaves the cell with zero translational drag.
reuse_errors: 'Dump-format extension so the state dump carries the Eulerian grid fields (p, v, k_ij, phi, vorticity) with their origin/dx metadata, since the current dump path is node-centric' — false, and contradicted by a file the design itself cites. ffn_sim/ac/cell/dump_coupled.py:118-124 already writes p_field, div_vs, q_field, v_f_field, mask, grid_shape, grid_dx, grid_origin into the npz. Only k_ij/phi/vorticity are new.

'Cost-ledger harness for NG-9: per-configuration N_unique_active / N_allocated / N_nodes / N_state / peak GPU bytes / dt_outer / inner iterations, with a structural refusal ...' — the contents are already specified verbatim at ffn_sim/ac/fluid/NATIVE_GATE_SPEC.md:62-67, including 'Publish the SS A.1 ledger: N_unique_active, N_allocated, N_nodes, N_state, peak GPU_bytes, and dt_outer/inner-iteration counts. Never lower a biological density to fit memory.' The harness is genuinely missing (ac/fluid/native_gates/ contains only ng0_parity.py), so this is implementing an existing spec, not authoring one.

S8 is NG-10, already specified at ffn_sim/ac/fluid/NATIVE_GATE_SPEC.md:68-77 down to the slab cut, |v_f|, q discharge streamlines, membrane hydraulic-flux hotspots, nucleus relative-no-flux shell, full-res-no-downsampling and browser_check verification. The design re-specifies it as new design work; only the vorticity scene, the k_ij/phi/free-fluid overlays and the drag-channel layer are additions.

The reuse list omits ffn_sim/ac/engine/load_path.py, which already implements the pattern S0 proposes to invent: resolve_fa_series_group ':274-278 enforce its double-stiffness guard', plus a Sanity Gate at :19-24 asserting 'double-count: the ACTIN_ANCHOR and FA_CLUTCH semantic edges resolve to exactly one spring energy and one force scatter' and 'conservation: the central pair force is equal-and-opposite, moment-free, and its interpolation/scatter are adjoints, so nodal virtual work equals -dU'. That is single-ownership + adjointness enforcement already in code.

The reuse list omits ffn_sim/ff/piezo.py (Piezo1 tension-gated open probability, KB-3.10, CA_FEEDBACK_GAIN = 0.0 default-off) even though it was in the reuse-before-rebuild list handed to the designer and the fluid track owns the membrane flux BC where an ion/osmolyte channel enters. It also omits ffn_sim/ff/ff_virial_stress.py, the existing per-node stress machinery the 'wall traction' observable would naturally extend.

The Peskin transpose claim is true of the raw kernels but not of the pair the engine runs. ffn_sim/ff/biot_fluid_warp.py:117/132/170 (_peskin4 / ibm_spread_kernel / ibm_interp_kernel) are the plain adjoint pair gated by ac/fluid/ibm_reference.py.
